docs.text:
Done Signal Pico connection Destination socket contact CLK Pico GP2 - header pin 4 U4 AHCT244 input - pin 2 RESET# Pico GP3 - header pin 5 U1 Z80 RESET# - pin 26 BUSREQ# Pico GP4 - header pin 6 U4 AHCT244 input - pin 4 BOOT_READ_DISABLE Pico GP5 - header pin 7 U4 AHCT244 input - pin 6 PICO_DATA_UP_OE# Pico GP6 - header pin 9 U3 HCT32 input - pin 10 DATA_DOWN_OE# Pico GP7 - header pin 10 U10 LVC245 OE# - pin 19 IO_RELEASE Pico GP9 - header pin 12 U3 HCT32 input - pin 5

Wire all Pico connections from the table above with other active devices absent. Continuity-check every destination socket contact and adjacent pins. Tick each row after checking its connection; progress is saved in the Phase 1 checklist.

docs.title: Phase 1 Firmware
docs.text:
Build z80_stage01_supervisor; load build/src/stage01_supervisor/z80_stage01_supervisor.uf2 using the firmware/console procedure. Maintained application.

Done Command Behavior Measurement s Sample input/data levels Monitor inputs may float with U7 absent w Walk seven control outputs, 250 ms each Scope the correct empty socket contact and neighbors r Hold RESET# alternately HIGH/LOW GP3/header 5 and Z80 socket 26: 3.20-3.40 V / near zero d Hold one data GPIO HIGH; advance D0-D7 Probe U9/U10 A pins 2-9 x Restore defaults and data inputs Both OE requests HIGH; RESET LOW

docs.title: Single-Step Data-Pin Test
docs.text: Type d without Enter. One GP10-GP17 output stays HIGH until the next d; all others remain LOW. The ninth step restores input mode. If the initial inputs are not all LOW, firmware refuses the test: check the eight individual 10 kOhm GP10-GP17 pull-down resistors. Use x to stop. USB disconnect restores any held data/reset test.

docs.title: Test Plan
docs.text:
Apply external +5 V before USB. Check Pico 3.3 V and that no GPIO sees +5 V.

At startup GP6/GP7/GP4/GP5 must be HIGH; GP2/GP3/GP9 LOW.

Scope each walking output at its empty destination; software PASS only means the sequence ended. Use held r/d levels for meter checks. Do not run these commands with CPU, SRAM, or any other active device fitted.

docs.title: Pass Gate
docs.text:
• Correct routing and no neighboring pin activity.
  • Isolated defaults.
  • Valid rail voltages.

Floating monitor readings are not a pass or a fault by themselves.

docs.title: Maintained Source
docs.text:
These complete files are included from the repository at documentation build time, not copied into this page.

Phase 1 application - src/stage01_supervisor/main.c 
#include <stdio.h>

#include "pico/stdlib.h"
#include "pico/stdio_usb.h"
#include "z80sbc/pins.h"
#include "z80sbc/supervisor.h"

static const uint TEST_OUTPUT_PINS[] = {
  PIN_CLK,
  PIN_RESET_N,
  PIN_BUSREQ_N,
  PIN_BOOT_READ_DISABLE,
  PIN_DATA_UP_OE_N,
  PIN_DATA_DOWN_OE_N,
  PIN_IO_RELEASE,
};

static const uint DATA_HEADER_PINS[] = {14, 15, 16, 17, 19, 20, 21, 22};
static int data_step = -1;
static bool reset_high = false;

static uint print_data_levels(void) {
  uint high_mask = 0;
  printf("Data GPIO levels:");
  for (uint bit = 0; bit < 8; ++bit) {
    bool level = gpio_get(PIN_DATA_0 + bit);
    high_mask |= (uint)level << bit;
    printf(" D%u/GP%u=%u", bit, PIN_DATA_0 + bit, (unsigned)level);
  }
  printf("\n");
  return high_mask;
}

static void restore_safe_levels(void) {
  z80_safe_startup();
  data_step = -1;
  reset_high = false;
}

static void toggle_reset_output(void) {
  reset_high = !reset_high;
  gpio_put(PIN_RESET_N, reset_high);
  printf("RESET# GP3 commanded %s: Pico header pin 5, Z80 socket pin 26\n",
         reset_high ? "HIGH" : "LOW");
    printf("Expected voltage at both contacts: %s (measure relative to common GND)\n",
      reset_high ? "3.20-3.40 V" : "near 0 V");
    printf("RESET# must never exceed the Pico 3.3 V rail; no 5 V pull-up permitted\n");
  printf("r: toggle RESET#, x: restore safe levels (Phase 1 only); measure the voltage\n");
}

static void step_data_output(void) {
  if (data_step < 0) {
    restore_safe_levels();
    if (print_data_levels() != 0) {
      printf("NOT STARTED: data inputs must all be LOW; check RN3 and wiring\n");
      return;
    }
    for (uint bit = 0; bit < 8; ++bit)
      output_with_initial_level(PIN_DATA_0 + bit, false);
  } else {
    gpio_put(PIN_DATA_0 + (uint)data_step, false);
  }

  ++data_step;
  if (data_step == 8) {
    restore_safe_levels();
    printf("DONE: data steps finished; safe levels restored, GP10-GP17 inputs\n");
    return;
  }

  uint bit = (uint)data_step;
  gpio_put(PIN_DATA_0 + bit, true);
  printf("D%u HIGH: GP%u, Pico header pin %u, AHCT245/LVC245 A%u pin %u\n",
         bit, PIN_DATA_0 + bit, DATA_HEADER_PINS[bit], bit + 1, bit + 2);
  printf("Other data pins LOW; d: next, x: restore safe levels (Phase 1 only)\n");
}

static void print_status(void) {
  printf("BUSACK#=%u IORQ#=%u RD#=%u WR#=%u\n",
         gpio_get(PIN_BUSACK_N), gpio_get(PIN_IORQ_N),
         gpio_get(PIN_RD_N), gpio_get(PIN_WR_N));
  print_data_levels();
}

int main(void) {
  z80_safe_startup();
  stdio_init_all();

  printf("\nZ80 ROMless SBC - Stage 1 supervisor\n");
  printf("r: toggle RESET# HIGH/LOW (Phase 1 hardware only)\n");
  printf("w: walking output test (Phase 1 hardware only)\n");
  printf("d: step D0-D7, hold one HIGH (Phase 1 hardware only)\n");
  printf("x: restore safe levels and return data GPIOs to inputs\n");
  printf("s: sample input status\n");

  while (true) {
    if (!stdio_usb_connected()) {
      if (data_step >= 0 || reset_high)
        restore_safe_levels();
      tight_loop_contents();
      continue;
    }

    int command = getchar_timeout_us(0);
    if (command == 'r') {
      toggle_reset_output();
    } else if (command == 'w') {
      restore_safe_levels();
      printf("walking %u outputs\n",
             (unsigned)(sizeof(TEST_OUTPUT_PINS) / sizeof(TEST_OUTPUT_PINS[0])));
      z80_walking_output_test(TEST_OUTPUT_PINS,
                              sizeof(TEST_OUTPUT_PINS) / sizeof(TEST_OUTPUT_PINS[0]),
                              250);
      printf("PASS: safe levels restored\n");
    } else if (command == 'd') {
      step_data_output();
    } else if (command == 'x') {
      restore_safe_levels();
      printf("DONE: safe levels restored, GP10-GP17 inputs\n");
    } else if (command == 's') {
      print_status();
    }
    tight_loop_contents();
  }
}
Shared startup and isolation - src/common/supervisor.c 
#include "z80sbc/supervisor.h"

#include "pico/stdlib.h"
#include "z80sbc/pins.h"

void output_with_initial_level(uint pin, bool level) {
  gpio_init(pin);
  gpio_put(pin, level);
  gpio_set_dir(pin, GPIO_OUT);
}

void input_with_no_pull(uint pin) {
  gpio_init(pin);
  gpio_set_dir(pin, GPIO_IN);
  gpio_disable_pulls(pin);
}

void z80_isolate_buses(void) {
  gpio_put(PIN_DATA_UP_OE_N, 1);
  gpio_put(PIN_DATA_DOWN_OE_N, 1);
}

void z80_safe_startup(void) {
  output_with_initial_level(PIN_DATA_UP_OE_N, 1);
  output_with_initial_level(PIN_DATA_DOWN_OE_N, 1);
  output_with_initial_level(PIN_RESET_N, 0);
  output_with_initial_level(PIN_BUSREQ_N, 1);
  output_with_initial_level(PIN_BOOT_READ_DISABLE, 1);
  output_with_initial_level(PIN_IO_RELEASE, 0);
  output_with_initial_level(PIN_CLK, 0);
  for (uint pin = PIN_DATA_0; pin <= PIN_DATA_7; ++pin)
    input_with_no_pull(pin);
  input_with_no_pull(PIN_BUSACK_N);
  input_with_no_pull(PIN_IORQ_N);
  input_with_no_pull(PIN_RD_N);
  input_with_no_pull(PIN_WR_N);
  input_with_no_pull(PIN_PORT_A0);
  input_with_no_pull(PIN_PORT_A1);
  input_with_no_pull(PIN_PORT_A2);
  input_with_no_pull(PIN_PORT_A4);
}

void z80_walking_output_test(const uint *pins, size_t count,
                             uint32_t dwell_ms) {
  for (size_t index = 0; index < count; ++index)
    output_with_initial_level(pins[index], false);

  for (size_t active = 0; active < count; ++active) {
    for (size_t index = 0; index < count; ++index)
      gpio_put(pins[index], index == active);
    sleep_ms(dwell_ms);
  }

  z80_safe_startup();
}

docs.title: Phase 10 - WebSocket Terminal Console
docs.text:
Goal: use CP/M in a web browser over the Pico 2 W's Wi-Fi. USB remains the fallback terminal.

Clear checklist

  • Start here: complete the Phase 9 automatic CP/M loader.
  • Unchanged: 120 MHz Pico clock, 20 MHz scope-measured Z80 clock, BIOS and disk layout.
  • Hardware: onboard Wi-Fi plus the 3.3 V matrix display. PCB changes remain deferred.

docs.title: First connection and USB provisioning
docs.text: See Related projects for building C applications with DCC, importing application disks from Altair 8800 AI Edition, and deploying them with the Z80ROMlessSBC VS Code disk tasks.

docs.title: 1. Deploy from VS Code
docs.text:
Before any update

Save CP/M work. Apply external +5 V before USB and keep it applied. Never power the populated board from USB alone. Disk updates overwrite selected drives without backups.

Open the Command Palette, run Tasks: Run Task, then choose:

Update Exact task name What changes Firmware Build and flash Pico - Phase 10 firmware Preserves disks and ENV settings All disks Flash Pico - All disks (A-D) Replaces A-D; preserves firmware and ENV CP/M system disk Flash Pico - Drive A Replaces A with a regenerated native image; checks boot compatibility BDS C disk Flash Pico - Drive B Replaces B only Escape disk Flash Pico - Drive C Replaces C only Blank disk Flash Pico - Drive D Replaces D only
  • Firmware confirmation: Proceed. Disk confirmation: Replace selected disks. Both default to Cancel.
  • Firmware and disk tasks force-update without a previous-firmware handshake; save CP/M work first. All tasks verify written bytes and request reboot.
  • Disk tasks do not rebuild firmware or applications. Install updated applications into the source disk first.
  • Setup/details: firmware build and provisioning and VS Code disk tasks.

Phase 10 firmware deployed.

First checkout or manual build

Initialize the WebSocket submodule before building or running the firmware task:

git submodule update --init --recursive
cmake -S . -B build -G Ninja -DPICO_BOARD=pico2_w
cmake --build build --target z80_stage10_websocket_terminal -j

Output: build/src/stage10_websocket_terminal/z80_stage10_websocket_terminal.uf2. These commands build only; they do not deploy. Flash verification proves written bytes, not a successful CP/M boot.

docs.title: 2. Set Wi-Fi over USB
docs.text:
1. Open the USB terminal. CP/M starts without waiting for Wi-Fi or a browser.
  2. Press Ctrl-] c to open configuration. Missing/invalid Wi-Fi credentials open it automatically.
  3. Select 1 - Wi-Fi, then C. Enter your SSID and password.
  4. Press Q to return to the main menu, then Q again to exit.

Saved changes trigger a safe reboot. No changes means no reboot. A storage error cancels reboot and is reported. Save application work first: flushing disks cannot save unsaved application RAM.

docs.title: 3. Open the browser terminal
docs.text:
1. Press Ctrl-] s on USB to display the Pico's address.
  2. Open http://<pico-ip>:8088/.

  3. Press Enter for a fresh CP/M prompt, then try DIR.

  4. Pico address verified and terminal page opened.

  5. Use a trusted local network only. The terminal has no authentication or TLS; never expose port 8088 to the Internet.
  6. The browser needs Internet access on first use to load xterm.js dependencies.
  7. Reload the terminal page after firmware updates.

docs.title: Unified system configuration
docs.text:
Ctrl-] c opens setup over USB, even while a browser owns the terminal. It saves the same environment variables that you can edit from CP/M with C:ENV.

Menu Use it for 1 - Wi-Fi C sets SSID/password; U clears them 2 - Remote filesystem Stores FS_SERVER only; remote file access is not implemented or required for Wi-Fi 3 - Chat 1 OpenAI, 2 compatible endpoint, 3 Ollama; 4-6 model, token limit and temperature; 7 thinking 4 - OpenWeatherMap C sets API key, location and units 5 - Timezone C sets POSIX TZ; for example, AEST-10 means UTC+10 Key Action Enter Keep the existing value - Clear the value; clearing the Wi-Fi password selects an open network ESC Cancel the current unsaved edit S Show settings, with secrets masked Q Return to the main menu; at the main menu, exit

Settings persist in plaintext onboard flash, not encrypted storage. Passwords and API keys are hidden during entry and masked on display.

Validation, saved changes and service settings
  • Wi-Fi: SSID up to 32 bytes; WPA2 password 8-63 bytes or a 64-digit hexadecimal key.
  • Saving: each key is atomic, but a multi-field edit is not. After a failed save, reopen setup and retry affected fields. Unrelated keys are preserved.
  • Disconnect: unsaved edits are discarded; saved edits still require reboot when exiting setup. Viewing settings does not count as a change.
  • ENV: values are stored literally. Network ENV edits apply on reboot or setup reload; saved Wi-Fi edits can reconnect immediately.
  • Chat: custom/Ollama endpoints need scheme, host and path, for example http://192.168.1.26:11434/v1/chat/completions. Only OpenAI receives CHAT_OPENAI_KEY; custom-provider authentication is unsupported. Model/options are consumed by the CP/M application. See CHAT configuration.
  • Weather: location can be Sydney,AU or lat=-33.8&lon=151.2; units are metric, imperial or standard.
  • Timezone: empty means UTC; AEST-10AEDT,M10.1.0,M4.1.0/3 includes daylight saving. Use TZ, not UTC_OFFSET.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Symptom Check or action No Pico address Ctrl-] s shows ip=unavailable; check Wi-Fi settings. Association times out after 30 seconds and retries after 5 seconds. Page opens, but no prompt Press Enter. Old output is not replayed to a new browser. CP/M still does not respond Use Ctrl-] s to inspect boot evidence, disk errors, queue drops and browser ownership. A working web page does not prove Z80 operation. USB ignores normal typing A browser owns CP/M. Close it to return to USB; USB supervisor commands still work. Second browser cannot connect Only one browser may own the terminal. Browser disappears USB ownership returns on disconnect/Wi-Fi loss, or after five missed pongs; pings are sent every five minutes. The Z80 keeps running. Wrong address Use the Pico's address, not FS_SERVER. HTTP/WebSocket use port 8088; ?altair=<pico-ip> changes the host only. Configuration save fails Reopen Ctrl-] c, inspect saved values and retry affected fields.

Confirm boot and network faults separately.

Ctrl-] s also shows uptime, reset causes and matrix status without injecting periodic diagnostics into CP/M output.

docs.title: HT16K33 8x8 matrix
docs.text:
Expected display while the Z80 is running: a horizontal row moves every 500 ms without Wi-Fi; a vertical column moves every 250 ms when Wi-Fi is connected. The display holds its last pattern while the supervisor stops the Z80 or pauses storage work. It is a supervisor diagnostic, not proof that a CP/M application is responsive.

Backpack marking Pico connection J2 pin + / VCC 3V3, physical pin 36 4 - / GND Common GND 5 C / SCL GP26, physical pin 31 3 D / SDA GP22, physical pin 29 2 Vi2c / IO, if fitted 3V3 4
  • Power and both pull-ups must be 3.3 V, never 5 V. Disconnect power safely before rewiring.
  • Follow the printed markings, not an assumed connector order. The external module is schematic A2, with no PCB footprint.
  • Keep other devices off this diagnostic bus. The driver scans 0x70-0x77; the tested board uses 0x72.
  • Check Ctrl-] s for address, state and errors. The module shares the Pico's 3.3 V budget and runs at reduced brightness (wiring guide).
Display implementation and host test

matrix_display.cpp runs on core 1 after network work. Each pass performs at most one non-blocking FIFO operation; RAM updates use two eight-byte chunks. Both halves of a frame use the same connectivity state, so a Wi-Fi change takes effect on the next full frame. USB status reports the displayed pattern and its interval.

New transactions require a running CPU and no flash pause. If permission changes, finish the transaction through STOP before holding the pattern. A 5 ms FIFO timeout or transfer NACK disables the display, releases resources and records the error. No Z80 bus GPIO or new core-0 handshake is used.

matrix_i2c.pio uses open-drain pins at nominal 100 kHz without clock stretching.

cmake --build build/host-control --target matrix_display_test -j
ctest --test-dir build/host-control --output-on-failure -R '^matrix_pio_HT16K33$'

The original moving row was bench-tested with CP/M and networking. Host tests check row/column RAM writes and connectivity changes between chunks; the new column pattern still needs checking on hardware. Host tests do not qualify physical waveform margins or core-0 latency.

docs.title: Network time and CLOCK services
docs.text:
• Wi-Fi enables automatic time sync with pool.ntp.org; until then, calendar queries return CLOCK_UNSYNCED.
  • Set TZ to AEST-10 for UTC+10 without daylight saving. Use the USB menu or C:ENV literal insert. Direct ENV changes apply on the next request; empty means UTC.
  • Look up time-zone abbreviations and UTC offsets on Wikipedia, or use this city-to-POSIX TZ lookup for complete rules. Enter the POSIX string, not the city name; its offset sign is reversed (-10 means UTC+10).

docs.title: System environment variables
docs.text:
One settings store, two ways to edit it:

  • USB configuration: press Ctrl-] c and choose a menu. It validates and saves the ENV values below.
  • CP/M command line: run C:ENV to list settings, or C:ENV NAME=VALUE to update one.
Used by ENV variables Purpose / values Wi-Fi WIFI_SSID, WIFI_PASSWORD Network name and password; empty password selects an open network Remote filesystem FS_SERVER Server IPv4 address; stored only, remote file access is not implemented Chat connection CHAT_PROVIDER, CHAT_ENDPOINT, CHAT_OPENAI_KEY openai, compatible or ollama; full URL for custom/local providers; API key for OpenAI only Chat options CHAT_MODEL, CHAT_MAX_TOKENS, CHAT_TEMPERATURE Model name, positive token limit and temperature 0-2 Chat thinking CHAT_THINK Chat menu 7: false (off), true (on/medium) or default (server choice); CHAT 1.7-c11 compatible/Ollama requests only Weather OWM_KEY, OWM_LOCATION, OWM_UNITS API key, city/country or coordinates, and metric (default), imperial or standard Local time TZ POSIX timezone string; empty means UTC

docs.title: Update from CP/M
docs.text:
C:ENV -H
C:ENV OWM_UNITS
C:ENV OWM_UNITS=metric

These show help, read one value and update it. ENV listings may reveal passwords and API keys. Both interfaces save to plaintext onboard flash.

Values containing + or -: prefer the USB menu, which saves literal text. The ENV app can interpret ordinary assignments as arithmetic. Use C:ENV -I NAME=VALUE for a literal insert; if the key already exists, delete it first with C:ENV -D NAME. This matters for keys, model names, coordinates and timezone rules.

docs.title: When changes take effect
docs.text:
• USB menu: exiting after saved changes safely reboots; save CP/M work first.
  • C:ENV Wi-Fi settings: reboot or reload the configuration shell.
  • C:ENV timezone/weather: timezone applies on the next request; weather reloads within one second, without reboot.
  • C:ENV chat settings: provider/endpoint/key and CHAT 1.7-c11 thinking settings apply on the next request/turn; restart CHAT after changing model, token limit or temperature.

Weather needs Wi-Fi and synchronized time; missing settings do not stop CP/M. For service-specific setup and errors, see chat, weather and the ENV command reference.

docs.title: Test plan
docs.text:
Tick only after recording hardware results. A successful build or host test is not hardware qualification.

  • Boot: test USB-only, then no USB/no Wi-Fi. Reconnect USB; confirm BIOS/CCP evidence and no fatal error.
  • Ownership: run browser DIR; no duplicate USB output. USB Ctrl-] s still works; a second browser is rejected.
  • Traffic: sustain output and paste over 128 bytes. Check order, zero drops/faults and no duplicate output when ACKs pause.
  • Keys: test Ctrl+C, Ctrl+Z, Ctrl+M/Enter, ESC, arrows, Insert/Delete and Page Up/Down. Ctrl+M is carriage return.
  • Disks: repeat Phase 9 sentinel, A-D, warm-boot and copy tests through the browser.
  • Recovery: disconnect browser/Wi-Fi during output and writes; verify USB fallback and no stale replay. Suspend the browser computer; verify missed-pong counting and fallback after the fifth missed response. Without a browser, Wi-Fi changes must preserve USB queues.
  • Settings: reboot and verify persistence. Reject invalid/overlong values, hide secrets and report failed saves.
  • Weather: run CLOCK with Wi-Fi/time ready; verify conditions, units and forecast while typing and using disks. Drop Wi-Fi: cached values remain readable with increasing age. Test invalid/missing keys and recovery without reboot.
  • Performance: compare CLOCK redraws and active-play BREAKOUT response. Record bytes/second, key-to-echo latency and maximum network-poll gaps during reads, cached writes and flash commits.
What host tests establish
  • Console tests cover concurrent 256 KiB transfers, handover and queue bounds.
  • Terminal tests cover ordering, duplicate suppression, sequence wrap, backpressure, ACK retries, 1 ms batching and the four-frame window.
  • With PICO_SDK_PATH, WebSocket tests use the actual server with fake lwIP and real Mbed TLS; weather tests also verify the firmware TLS configuration and bundled CA.
  • Weather tests cover all 15 fields, caching, cancellation, malformed responses and failures.
  • These prove software behavior, not wireless throughput or hardware latency. See firmware testing.

docs.title: Pass gate
docs.text:
• Browser remains responsive at the baseline clock.
  • Status matches queued bytes and active transport.
  • Interactive commands, warm boot and A-D copies pass.
  • No HTTP, WebSocket or Wi-Fi work runs on core 0.
  • No unexplained drops, trap faults or storage errors.
  • Complete Phase 9 final acceptance.

docs.title: Core ownership and terminal routing
docs.text:
Developer reference: expand only when changing or diagnosing firmware.

Core responsibilities and terminal ownership
  • Core 0: Z80 GPIO/clock/traps, journal recovery, validated SRAM loading, queued supervisor requests and flash quiescence. No USB endpoint calls.
  • Core 1: USB, runtime storage, ENV, services, Wi-Fi and HTTP/WebSocket. Disk work runs before network work; networking uses pico_cyw43_arch_lwip_poll.
  • Queues: 128-byte console RX, 512-byte TX, four supervisor entries and a 4 KiB diagnostic ring (128-byte drain/pass). Short locks and atomic state publication separate cores.
  • Ownership: one browser replaces ordinary USB I/O; USB supervisor/setup stays available. Switching transports clears queued input/output. Wi-Fi changes alone do not clear USB-owned queues.
  • Disconnected: output is discarded and TX-ready stays set. Intentional discards are distinct from reported queue overflows.
  • Ports: 0x00 data; 0x01 bit 0 RX-ready, bit 1 TX-room/disconnected, bit 7 active transport. Storage/service ports and safe stop/flush are unchanged.

docs.title: Module boundaries
docs.text:
Which module owns what? Module Responsibility network_runtime.cpp Wi-Fi lifecycle, CYW43 polling, IPv4 publication and SNTP; no terminal queues web_terminal.cpp HTTP/WebSocket sessions, heartbeat and flow control; no Wi-Fi configuration network_services.c Schedules network, weather and chat services chat.c, chat_stream.c, chat_network.cpp Bounded chat ABI, HTTP/SSE parsing and asynchronous DNS/TCP/TLS; core boundary is the service mailbox terminal_queue.c Transport-neutral queues and ownership usb_console.c Core-1 USB/alarm initialization and bounded stdout routing

Wi-Fi disables power saving after association; failure drops the link and retries. IPv4 publication refreshes once per second. Chat never touches terminal queues, USB input or Z80 GPIO.

docs.title: Acknowledged terminal protocol, version 4
docs.text:
Protocol and buffer limits

Use the served browser page, not a raw-byte WebSocket client. Version 1/2/3 pages are rejected. Messages start with a one-byte type and four-byte little-endian sequence; data sequences start at 1 and wrap modulo 2^32.

Type Direction Sequence / payload 5 HELLO Pico to browser Version 4 / none 6 READY Browser to Pico Version 4 / none 1 OUTPUT Pico to browser Output sequence / 1-512 bytes 3 OUTPUT_ACK Browser to Pico Last consumed output sequence / none 2 INPUT Browser to Pico Input sequence / 1-64 bytes 4 INPUT_ACK Pico to browser Accepted input sequence / none 7 REBOOT Browser to Pico Zero / none 8 REBOOT_STATUS Pico to browser Status code / none

Reboot Zeta-80: the toolbar button asks for confirmation, then sends a control frame directly to the Pico supervisor, independently of CP/M input and its queue. The supervisor drains outstanding disk/service work, flushes storage, holds RESET and stops the clock, then reboots the Pico after one second. Terminal networking stays active while disk/application workers are paused, so restart and error statuses can still be delivered. Before reboot, the supervisor sends the restarting status and explicitly closes the WebSocket; this starts browser reconnection without waiting for a TCP timeout. Startup reloads and verifies CP/M. Wi-Fi disconnects briefly; the browser automatically reconnects for this operation and clears reboot progress as soon as the terminal handshake completes and controls are re-enabled. The supervisor reports CP/M ready after observing BIOS and CCP boot markers. Unsaved application data is lost; flushing preserves only writes already received by the Pico.

The browser distinguishes Waiting for Pico supervisor (request not yet acknowledged) from Flushing disks (the supervisor has begun the stop). Neither message proves that flash is currently being written.

Storage failure cancels automatic reboot. Core 0 cancels a stop/restart after 30 seconds. Independently, core 1 expires an unfinished request after 35 seconds, including when core 0 stops servicing its loop. That deadline survives browser disconnects; retries cannot extend it. An expired request cannot later start or resume automatic reboot. Any orderly stop already begun remains pending. Timeout is retained until the board restarts; the button stays disabled so reconnecting cannot queue another reboot. Inspect USB supervisor status/logs before manual recovery. No deadline forces reset through unfinished writes.

The browser also reports unconfirmed progress after 40 seconds, including when a newly opened page receives an existing request. It never resends reboot automatically. Ordinary disconnects still require manual connection.

Status codes: 0 idle, 1 requested, 2 flushing, 3 restarting, 4 storage error, 5 timeout, 6 rejected (busy/stopped/storage failure), 7 CP/M ready. Requests during an active reboot are idempotent. Controls require the active connection and completed version-4 handshake. Update firmware and any separately hosted terminal page together.

  • Output: four frames retain at most 2 KiB. ACKs are cumulative, after xterm consumes bytes; duplicates are not rendered twice. Retry after 250 ms; oldest-frame timeout is 15 seconds.
  • Batching: isolated/full frames send immediately. Later partial frames wait up to a fixed 1 ms deadline, then the next service pass. Flash pauses may delay service. Accepted TCP writes are not duplicated after failed flushes.
  • Input: one frame waits for RX space; admission/rejected ACKs retry each pass. ACK means queued, not executed. The browser caps pending input at 64 KiB, rejects an overflowing paste entirely and warns when disconnect discards input.
  • Bounds: 69-byte incoming messages; queued payload at most 1,024 bytes/16 messages; dispatch at most eight per connection/pass. Overflow disconnects.
  • Memory: maximum build buffer 521 bytes; four frames use 2,084 of 5,840 TCP send-buffer bytes. Core-1 stack is 8 KiB in main RAM. These are not total memory-use measurements.
  • Cleanup: one-second close grace; callback-safe abort also runs offline. Heartbeat pings every 5 minutes. A missing pong is counted at the next heartbeat; the fifth miss releases ownership.

docs.title: Terminal performance diagnostics
docs.text:
Read the Ctrl-] s counters Fields Meaning frames, bytes Original TCP-accepted output; excludes retries and headers retransmits, write_blocks, flush_failures Application retries, enqueue backpressure and explicit burst-flush failures timeouts Sessions released by heartbeat/output timeout window_full_polls, window_wait_max_us Full-window service passes and longest full interval ack_max_us Longest first-enqueue to consumption-ACK interval; includes transport and browser scheduling net_poll_gap_max_us Longest gap between CYW43 polls, including storage/USB work and pauses [webbuf] frames, retained, staged, peak Finalized frames, retained/staged payload and high-water marks [webbatch] avg_bytes, max_bytes, small_le16, full Original-frame sizes/counts; excludes retries [consolebuf] rx, tx, peak Console occupancy, capacity and high-water marks

Compare deltas for the same workload. Small frames are not inherently a fault; full windows plus high ACK age suggest consumer/transport pressure. bytes / frames measures batching, not throughput.

Occupancy clears on handover; peaks survive it. Web counters reset on reboot; console peaks reset on initialization. Counters wrap modulo 2^32; microsecond maxima saturate at UINT32_MAX. Fields are individual atomic snapshots, not one transaction.

Pre-batching baseline, 22 Oct 2026: CLOCK delivered 19 redraws in 20 seconds (97.5 ms median, 926.2 ms maximum; longest internal gap 863.5 ms). Median payload was 7 bytes; browser consumption was 0.3 ms at p95. This is not evidence of a post-change speedup.

docs.title: Required Integration Order
docs.text:
Preserve the Phase 9 startup sequence
  1. Initialize safe GPIOs and console/control queues.
  2. Start core 1; initialize its alarm pool, USB and flash lockout.
  3. With RESET held, recover the journal, load SRAM and independently verify it.
  4. Initialize storage/service queues before enabling workers; enable the trap and 20 MHz run clock.

Boot/core-1 failure leaves RESET asserted. Core 0 continually services flash ownership requests. Stop drains disk/service/provisioning work before holding RESET; reboot reloads CP/M. Use dedicated builds for RAM/clock qualification.

docs.title: Maintained source
docs.text:
Phase 10 compiles the Phase 9 application with Z80_STAGE09_AUTOBOOT=1 and Z80_STAGE10_NETWORK=1; it does not maintain a separate loader.

  • Phase 10 build configuration
  • Browser page and update tool (CMake compresses changes automatically)

enum {

  SYSTEM_CLOCK_HZ = 120000000,
  USB_COMMAND_ESCAPE = 0x1D,

static void publish_cpu_state(void) {
  __atomic_store_n(&cpu_state,
                   (running ? CPU_RUNNING : 0) |
                   (stop_requested ? CPU_STOPPING : 0) |
                   (loading ? CPU_LOADING : 0), __ATOMIC_RELEASE);
}

static uint8_t __not_in_flash_func(virtual_read)(uint8_t port, void *context) {
  (void)context;
  switch (port) {
  case 0x00:
  case 0x01:
    return z80_terminal_io_read(port);
  case 0x10:
  case 0x11:
  case 0x12:
  case 0x13:
  case 0x14:
    return z80_flash_disk_io_read(port);
  case IO_SERVICE_COMMAND_PORT:
  case IO_SERVICE_REQUEST_PORT:
  case IO_SERVICE_RESPONSE_PORT:
  case IO_TIMER_PORT:
  case HTTP_COMMAND_PORT:
  case HTTP_DATA_PORT:
    return z80_io_port_in(port);
  default:
    return 0xFF;
  }
}

static void __not_in_flash_func(virtual_write)(uint8_t port, uint8_t value,
                                              void *context) {
  (void)context;
  if (port == 0x00) {
    z80_terminal_io_write(port, value);
    return;
  }
  if (diagnostic_active && port == 0x06) {
    uint32_t offset = diagnostic_count;
    if (offset < DIAGNOSTIC_BYTES) {
      const uint8_t *source =
          (const uint8_t *)(XIP_BASE + Z80_FLASH_DISK_OFFSET);
      if (value != source[offset] && diagnostic_result == 0) {
        diagnostic_fault_offset = offset;
        diagnostic_expected = source[offset];
        diagnostic_actual = value;
        diagnostic_result = 0xE1;
      }
    } else {
      diagnostic_result = 0xE1;
    }
    diagnostic_count = offset + 1;
    return;
  }
  if (diagnostic_active && port == Z80_BOOT_REPORT_PORT) {
    if (diagnostic_result == 0)
      diagnostic_result = value == 0x5A &&
                          diagnostic_count == DIAGNOSTIC_BYTES ? 0x5A : 0xE1;
    return;
  }
  switch (port) {
  case Z80_BOOT_REPORT_PORT:
    if (value == Z80_BOOT_REPORT_BIOS)
      __atomic_fetch_or(&boot_markers, 1u, __ATOMIC_RELEASE);
    else if (value == Z80_BOOT_REPORT_CCP)
      __atomic_fetch_or(&boot_markers, 2u, __ATOMIC_RELEASE);
    break;
  case 0x10:
  case 0x11:
  case 0x12:
  case 0x13:
  case 0x14:
    z80_flash_disk_io_write(port, value);
    break;
  case IO_SERVICE_COMMAND_PORT:
  case IO_SERVICE_REQUEST_PORT:
  case IO_SERVICE_RESPONSE_PORT:
  case IO_TIMER_PORT:
  case HTTP_COMMAND_PORT:
  case HTTP_DATA_PORT:
    z80_io_port_out(port, value);
    break;
  default:
    break;
  }
}

static void core1_service(void) {
  bool active = __atomic_load_n(&workers_ready, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE);
  if (active) {
    if (__atomic_load_n(&flash_pause_request, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE)) {
      if (!__atomic_load_n(&flash_paused, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE)) {
        z80_flash_core1_service();
        z80_io_ports_core1_service();
#ifdef Z80_STAGE10_NETWORK
        z80_network_setup_core1_service();
#endif
        if (z80_flash_disk_quiescent() && z80_io_ports_quiescent()
#ifdef Z80_STAGE10_NETWORK
            && z80_network_setup_quiescent()
#endif
        )
          __atomic_store_n(&flash_paused, 1, __ATOMIC_RELEASE);
      }
    } else {
      __atomic_store_n(&flash_paused, 0, __ATOMIC_RELEASE);
      z80_flash_core1_service();
      z80_io_ports_core1_service();
#ifdef Z80_STAGE10_NETWORK
      z80_network_setup_core1_service();
#endif
    }
  }
  z80_usb_console_service();
  service_usb();
#ifdef Z80_STAGE10_NETWORK
  if (active) {
    if (__atomic_load_n(&flash_pause_request, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE))
      z80_network_terminal_core1_service();
    else
      z80_network_core1_service();
  }
  if (active) {
    uint32_t state = __atomic_load_n(&cpu_state, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE);
    z80_matrix_core1_service(
        (state & (CPU_RUNNING | CPU_STOPPING | CPU_LOADING)) == CPU_RUNNING &&
        !__atomic_load_n(&flash_pause_request, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE));
  }
#endif
}

static void core1_main(void) {
  bool flash_ready = flash_safe_execute_core_init();
  bool usb_ready = z80_usb_console_init();
  if (!flash_ready || !usb_ready)
    printf("\n[diag] FAIL: core 1 USB/flash-safe initialization.\n");
  __atomic_store_n(&core1_ready, flash_ready && usb_ready ? 1u : 2u,
                    __ATOMIC_RELEASE);
  while (true) {
    if (usb_ready)
      core1_service();
    tight_loop_contents();
  }
}

static void hold_cpu(void) {
  z80_io_trap_disable();
  z80_cpu_fail_closed();
  running = false;
  image_verified = false;
  stop_requested = false;
  diagnostic_active = false;
}

static const char *fault_name(z80_flash_fault_point_t point) {
  static const char *const names[] = {
    "none", "after journal data", "after journal header",
    "after target erase", "after partial target program",
    "after target verification", "after journal header clear",
    "safe-execute entry failure", "safe-execute exit failure",
  };
  return point <= Z80_FLASH_FAULT_SAFE_EXECUTE_EXIT
             ? names[(unsigned int)point] : "invalid";
}

static const char *boot_error_name(z80_boot_error_t error) {
  static const char *const names[] = {
    "none", "journal recovery",
    "manifest (requires 65536 bytes and JP FD00h)",
    "payload CRC", "loader controls", "SRAM write", "SRAM read",
    "SRAM mismatch", "flash-safe core initialization", "cancelled",
  };
  return (unsigned int)error < sizeof(names) / sizeof(names[0])
             ? names[(unsigned int)error] : "invalid";
}

static bool observe_boot(const z80_boot_status_t *status, void *context) {
  (void)context;
  static const char *const phases[] = {
    "journal recovery", "manifest/CRC validation", "SRAM load",
    "SRAM verify", "verified; RESET held LOW",
  };
  if (status->completed % 4096u == 0 &&
      (!Z80_STAGE09_AUTOBOOT ||
       (__atomic_load_n(&usb_state, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE) & USB_CONNECTED)))
    printf("[boot] %s: %lu/%lu\n", phases[status->phase],
           (unsigned long)status->completed, (unsigned long)status->total);
  if (Z80_STAGE09_AUTOBOOT)
    return true;
  return !__atomic_load_n(&load_cancelled, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE) &&
         (__atomic_load_n(&usb_state, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE) & USB_CONNECTED);
}

static void load_image(void) {
  if (boot_attempted || running || runtime_started) {
    printf("\n[diag] Load already attempted; stop and reboot Pico to reload.\n");
    return;
  }
  boot_attempted = true;
  loading = true;
  __atomic_store_n(&load_cancelled, 0, __ATOMIC_RELEASE);
  publish_cpu_state();
  if (!Z80_STAGE09_AUTOBOOT)
    printf("\n[boot] Load/verify only; x cancels at a 256-byte boundary.\n");
  bool loaded = z80_flash_storage_init_observed(observe_boot, NULL);
  loading = false;
  publish_cpu_state();
  if (!loaded) {
    const z80_boot_status_t *status = z80_flash_boot_status();
    boot_failure = boot_error_name(status->error);
    hold_cpu();
    printf("[boot] FAIL: %s phase=%u completed=%lu address=%04x "
           "expected=%02x actual=%02x; RESET held LOW\n",
           boot_error_name(status->error), (unsigned int)status->phase,
           (unsigned long)status->completed, status->address,
           status->expected, status->actual);
    return;
  }
  image_verified = true;
  if (!Z80_STAGE09_AUTOBOOT)
    printf("[boot] PASS: 65536 bytes loaded and independently read back; "
           "CPU not running. Ctrl-] g starts CP/M at nominal 20 MHz.\n");
}

static void start_cpm(void) {
  if (!image_verified || running || runtime_started) {
    printf("\n[diag] Start rejected: first load/verify with Ctrl-] l; "
           "a stopped run requires Pico reboot.\n");
    return;
  }
  __atomic_store_n(&boot_markers, 0, __ATOMIC_RELEASE);
  bios_announced = ccp_announced = false;
  boot_timed_out = false;
  z80_io_ports_init();
  runtime_started = true;
  if (!z80_io_trap_enable(virtual_read, virtual_write, NULL) ||
      !z80_cpu_release_reset_and_run(RUN_CLOCK_HZ)) {
    boot_failure = "trap/clock start";
    hold_cpu();
    printf("[boot] FAIL: trap/clock start; RESET held LOW\n");
    return;
  }
  running = true;
  __atomic_store_n(&workers_ready, 1, __ATOMIC_RELEASE);
  boot_deadline = make_timeout_time_ms(10000);
  if (!Z80_STAGE09_AUTOBOOT)
    printf("\n[boot] CPU released from reset; configured clock=%lu Hz. "
           "Waiting for BIOS evidence, not yet a CP/M PASS.\n",
           (unsigned long)z80_clock_get_hz());
}

static void start_disk_diagnostic(void) {
  if (!image_verified || runtime_started || running) {
    printf("\n[diag] Disk test requires Ctrl-] l and no prior run.\n");
    return;
  }
  image_verified = false;
  diagnostic_count = diagnostic_result = 0;
  diagnostic_fault_offset = UINT32_MAX;
  diagnostic_next_progress = 65536;
  if (!z80_cpu_load_and_verify(z80_disk_diagnostic,
                               sizeof(z80_disk_diagnostic))) {
    hold_cpu();
    printf("\n[diag] FAIL: disk diagnostic load/readback; RESET held LOW\n");
    return;
  }
  diagnostic_active = true;
  if (!z80_io_trap_enable(virtual_read, virtual_write, NULL) ||
      !z80_cpu_release_reset_and_run(RUN_CLOCK_HZ)) {
    hold_cpu();
    printf("\n[diag] FAIL: disk diagnostic start; RESET held LOW\n");
    return;
  }
  running = true;
  boot_deadline = make_timeout_time_ms(300000);
  printf("\n[diag] Read-only Z80 INIR/OTIR disk test at nominal 20 MHz: "
         "all 4 drives x 2560 records x 128 bytes. No disk writes. "
         "CP/M SRAM image replaced; reboot afterward.\n");
}

static void diagnostic_command(int command) {
  if (command == 'l') {
    load_image();
  } else if (command == 'g') {
    start_cpm();
  } else if (command == 't') {
    start_disk_diagnostic();
  } else if (command == 's') {
    print_status(true);
  } else if (command == 'h') {
    print_help();
  } else if (command == 'x') {
    if (!running || diagnostic_active) {
      hold_cpu();
      printf("\n[diag] RESET held LOW; reboot required before a new run.\n");
      print_help();
    } else {
      stop_requested = true;
      flush_submitted = false;
      __atomic_store_n(&flash_pause_request, 1, __ATOMIC_RELEASE);
      printf("\n[diag] Stop requested; waiting for disk completion/flush.\n");
    }
  } else if (command == 'r') {
    if (running || stop_requested)
      printf("\n[diag] Reboot rejected: stop and flush with Ctrl-] x first.\n");
    else
      watchdog_reboot(0, 0, 0);
  } else if (command >= '0' && command <= '8') {
    if (!running) {
      printf("\n[diag] Fault command rejected: CPU is not running.\n");
      return;
    }
    z80_flash_fault_point_t point =
        (z80_flash_fault_point_t)(command - '0');
    z80_flash_disk_arm_fault(point);
    printf("\n[diag] Armed: %s; next disk write/flush may reboot Pico.\n",
           fault_name(point));
  } else {
    printf("\n[diag] Unknown command; Ctrl-] h for help.\n");
  }
}

static void forward_terminal_byte(uint8_t value) {
  if (value == 0)
    return;
  if (value == '\n' && previous_cr) {
    previous_cr = false;
    return;
  }
  previous_cr = value == '\r';
#ifdef Z80_STAGE10_NETWORK
  z80_terminal_usb_receive(value);
#else
  z80_terminal_receive(&value, 1);
#endif
}

static void receive_usb_byte(uint8_t value) {
  uint32_t state = __atomic_load_n(&cpu_state, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE);
  if (command_pending) {
    command_pending = false;
    if (value != USB_COMMAND_ESCAPE) {
#ifdef Z80_STAGE10_NETWORK
      if (value == 'c') {
        if ((state & (CPU_RUNNING | CPU_STOPPING)) == CPU_RUNNING)
          z80_network_setup_request();
        else
          printf("\n[config] Rejected: CP/M must be running, not stopping.\n");
        return;
      }
#endif
      if (value == 'x' && (state & CPU_LOADING) && !Z80_STAGE09_AUTOBOOT)
        __atomic_store_n(&load_cancelled, 1, __ATOMIC_RELEASE);
      else {
        uint16_t command = value;
        if (!queue_try_add(&control_commands, &command))
          printf("\n[diag] FAIL: supervisor command queue full; retry command.\n");
      }
      return;
    }
  } else if (value == USB_COMMAND_ESCAPE) {
    ansi_input_reset();
    command_pending = true;
    return;
  }
  if (state & CPU_LOADING) {
    if (value == 'x' && !Z80_STAGE09_AUTOBOOT)
      __atomic_store_n(&load_cancelled, 1, __ATOMIC_RELEASE);
    return;
  }
#ifdef Z80_STAGE10_NETWORK
  if ((state & (CPU_RUNNING | CPU_STOPPING)) == CPU_RUNNING &&
      z80_network_setup_input(value))
    return;
  if (z80_terminal_browser_connected())
    return;
#endif
  if (!(state & CPU_RUNNING)) {
    if (Z80_STAGE09_AUTOBOOT)
      printf("\n[diag] CPU held; Ctrl-] s for status, "
             "Ctrl-] r to retry automatic boot.\n");
    else
      printf("\n[diag] CPU held; use Ctrl-] l then Ctrl-] g.\n");
    return;
  }
  forward_terminal_byte(
      ansi_input_process(value, to_ms_since_boot(get_absolute_time())));
}

static void service_usb(void) {
  bool connected = stdio_usb_connected();
  uint32_t state = __atomic_load_n(&cpu_state, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE);
  if (state != previous_cpu_state) {
    ansi_input_reset();
    previous_cr = false;
    previous_cpu_state = state;
  }
#ifdef Z80_STAGE10_NETWORK
  z80_terminal_usb_connected(connected);
  bool browser_connected = z80_terminal_browser_connected();
  if (browser_connected != browser_was_connected) {
    ansi_input_reset();
    previous_cr = false;
    browser_was_connected = browser_connected;
  }
  z80_network_setup_usb_service(
      connected, (state & (CPU_RUNNING | CPU_STOPPING)) == CPU_RUNNING);
  if (z80_network_setup_reboot_requested()) {
    uint16_t command = USB_CONFIG_REBOOT;
    if (queue_try_add(&control_commands, &command)) {
      z80_network_setup_reboot_queued();
      config_reboot_queue_full = false;
    } else if (!config_reboot_queue_full) {
      printf("\n[config] Supervisor queue full; retrying orderly reboot.\n");
      config_reboot_queue_full = true;
    }
  }
#else
  z80_terminal_set_connected(connected);
#endif
  __atomic_store_n(&usb_state, (connected ? USB_CONNECTED : 0)
#ifdef Z80_STAGE10_NETWORK
                   | (browser_connected ? USB_BROWSER : 0)
                   | (z80_network_setup_active() ? USB_SETUP : 0)
#endif
                   , __ATOMIC_RELEASE);
  if (connected != usb_was_connected)
    ansi_input_reset();
  if (connected && !usb_was_connected) {
    command_pending = false;
    previous_cr = false;
    uint16_t command = USB_REPORT_CONNECTION;
    if (!queue_try_add(&control_commands, &command))
      printf("\n[diag] FAIL: connection report queue full; Ctrl-] s for status.\n");
  }
  usb_was_connected = connected;
  if (!connected)
    return;
  for (unsigned int count = 0; count < 32; ++count) {
    int input = getchar_timeout_us(0);
    if (input < 0)
      break;
    receive_usb_byte((uint8_t)input);
  }
  if ((state & CPU_RUNNING) && !command_pending
#ifdef Z80_STAGE10_NETWORK
      && !z80_network_setup_active() && !z80_terminal_browser_connected()
#endif
  )
    forward_terminal_byte(
        ansi_input_process(0, to_ms_since_boot(get_absolute_time())));
  if (stdio_usb_connected()
#ifdef Z80_STAGE10_NETWORK
      && !z80_network_setup_active() && !z80_terminal_browser_connected()
#endif
  ) {
    uint8_t data[32];
    size_t capacity = tud_cdc_write_available();
    if (capacity > sizeof(data))
      capacity = sizeof(data);
    size_t count = z80_terminal_peek(data, capacity);
    if (count) {
      size_t accepted = z80_usb_console_write(data, count);
      z80_terminal_supply(data, accepted);
    }
  }
  uint32_t rx = z80_terminal_rx_drop_count();
  uint32_t tx = z80_terminal_tx_drop_count();
  if (rx != reported_rx_drops || tx != reported_tx_drops) {
    printf("\n[diag] FAIL: terminal overflow rx=%lu tx=%lu; "
           "reduce paste/output rate and repeat acceptance.\n",
           (unsigned long)rx, (unsigned long)tx);
    reported_rx_drops = rx;
    reported_tx_drops = tx;
  }
}

static void service_control(void) {
#ifdef Z80_STAGE10_NETWORK
  if (z80_web_terminal_reboot_status() == Z80_WEB_REBOOT_REQUESTED) {
    if (config_reboot_after_stop || config_reboot_ready || stop_requested ||
        !running || diagnostic_active || z80_flash_disk_has_fatal_error()) {
      z80_web_terminal_set_reboot_status(Z80_WEB_REBOOT_REJECTED);
    } else if (z80_web_terminal_begin_reboot()) {
      web_reboot_active = true;
      web_reboot_deadline = make_timeout_time_ms(30000);
      config_reboot_after_stop = true;
      diagnostic_command('x');
    }
  }
  if (web_reboot_active &&
      z80_web_terminal_reboot_status() == Z80_WEB_REBOOT_TIMEOUT) {
    web_reboot_active = false;
    config_reboot_after_stop = config_reboot_ready = false;
    printf("\n[web] Reboot cancelled after network-side timeout; "
           "orderly stop remains pending.\n");
  }
  if (web_reboot_active && z80_flash_disk_has_fatal_error()) {
    web_reboot_active = false;
    config_reboot_after_stop = config_reboot_ready = false;
    z80_web_terminal_set_reboot_status(Z80_WEB_REBOOT_STORAGE_ERROR);
  }
  if (web_reboot_active && time_reached(web_reboot_deadline)) {
    web_reboot_active = false;
    config_reboot_after_stop = config_reboot_ready = false;
    // Keep draining/stopping; never force a reset through an unfinished write.
    z80_web_terminal_set_reboot_status(Z80_WEB_REBOOT_TIMEOUT);
    printf("\n[web] Reboot timed out; automatic restart cancelled. "
           "Orderly stop remains pending.\n");
  }
  if (config_reboot_ready && time_reached(config_reboot_deadline)) {
    config_reboot_ready = false;
    watchdog_reboot(0, 0, 0);
    return;
  }
#endif
  uint16_t command;
  if (queue_try_remove(&control_commands, &command)) {
#ifdef Z80_STAGE10_NETWORK
    if (command == USB_CONFIG_REBOOT) {
      if (!running || diagnostic_active || z80_flash_disk_has_fatal_error()) {
        printf("\n[config] FAIL: automatic reboot rejected: CP/M is not "
               "running normally or storage has failed. CPU state unchanged; "
               "inspect Ctrl-] s before manual recovery.\n");
      } else {
        config_reboot_after_stop = true;
        if (!stop_requested)
          diagnostic_command('x');
      }
    } else if ((config_reboot_after_stop || config_reboot_ready) &&
               command != 's' && command != 'h' &&
               command != USB_REPORT_CONNECTION) {
      printf("\n[config] Orderly reboot in progress; command rejected.\n");
    } else
#endif
    if (command == USB_REPORT_CONNECTION) {
      if (!Z80_STAGE09_AUTOBOOT) {
        print_help();
        print_status(false);
      } else if (!running && !loading && boot_attempted) {
        printf("\n[boot] %s; RESET held LOW. Ctrl-] s for status, "
               "Ctrl-] r to reboot.\n",
               boot_failure != NULL ? "FAIL: automatic CP/M boot stopped"
                                    : "CP/M stopped");
        print_status(false);
      }
    } else if (startup_failed && command != 'r' && command != 's' &&
               command != 'h') {
      printf("\n[diag] Rejected: core 1 initialization failed; CPU held reset.\n");
    } else {
      diagnostic_command(command);
    }
  }
  publish_cpu_state();
}

static void service_run(void) {
  if (!running)
    return;
  if (diagnostic_active) {
    uint32_t interrupts = save_and_disable_interrupts();
    uint32_t count = diagnostic_count;
    uint32_t result = diagnostic_result;
    restore_interrupts(interrupts);
    if (result != 0 || time_reached(boot_deadline)) {
      hold_cpu();
      printf("\n[diag] %s: disk bytes checked=%lu/%u "
             "fault_offset=%08lx expected=%02x actual=%02x; "
             "RESET held LOW; Ctrl-] r then load CP/M again.\n",
             result == 0x5A ? "PASS" : "FAIL",
             (unsigned long)count, DIAGNOSTIC_BYTES,
             (unsigned long)diagnostic_fault_offset,
             diagnostic_expected, diagnostic_actual);
    } else if (count >= diagnostic_next_progress) {
      printf("[diag] disk bytes checked=%lu/%u\n",
             (unsigned long)count, DIAGNOSTIC_BYTES);
      diagnostic_next_progress += 65536;
    }
    return;
  }
  uint32_t markers = __atomic_load_n(&boot_markers, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE);
  if ((markers & 1u) && !bios_announced) {
    bios_announced = true;
    if (!Z80_STAGE09_AUTOBOOT)
      printf("\n[boot] Observed BIOS cold-entry report from Z80.\n");
  }
  if ((markers & 2u) && !ccp_announced) {
    ccp_announced = true;
    if (!Z80_STAGE09_AUTOBOOT)
      printf("\n[boot] Observed BIOS handoff to CCP; "
             "confirm A>, DIR and transient/warm-boot tests manually.\n");
  }
  if (!boot_timed_out && (!bios_announced || !ccp_announced) &&
      time_reached(boot_deadline)) {
    boot_failure = "BIOS/CCP evidence timeout";
    printf("\n[boot] FAIL: BIOS/CCP evidence timeout; stopping safely. "
           "Rebuild/provision the matching boot package if markers are absent.\n");
    stop_requested = true;
    boot_timed_out = true;
    __atomic_store_n(&flash_pause_request, 1, __ATOMIC_RELEASE);
  }
  if (z80_flash_disk_has_fatal_error()) {
#ifdef Z80_STAGE10_NETWORK
    if (config_reboot_after_stop) {
      config_reboot_after_stop = false;
      printf("\n[config] FAIL: storage error; automatic reboot cancelled.\n");
    }
    if (web_reboot_active) {
      web_reboot_active = false;
      z80_web_terminal_set_reboot_status(Z80_WEB_REBOOT_STORAGE_ERROR);
    }
#endif
    boot_failure = "fatal storage error";
    hold_cpu();
    printf("\n[diag] FAIL: fatal storage error; RESET held LOW. "
           "Reboot to recover; preserve USB log.\n");
    return;
  }
#ifdef Z80_STAGE10_NETWORK
  if (bios_announced && ccp_announced && !stop_requested &&
      z80_web_terminal_reboot_status() == Z80_WEB_REBOOT_IDLE)
    z80_web_terminal_set_reboot_status(Z80_WEB_REBOOT_CPM_READY);
#endif
  if (!stop_requested)
    return;
  if (flash_resuming) {
    if (!__atomic_load_n(&flash_paused, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE)) {
      flash_resuming = false;
      flush_submitted = false;
      __atomic_store_n(&flash_pause_request, 1, __ATOMIC_RELEASE);
    }
    return;
  }
  if (__atomic_load_n(&flash_paused, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE)) {
    // Exclude a last I/O IRQ between checking the queue and asserting reset.
    uint32_t interrupts = save_and_disable_interrupts();
    bool quiescent = z80_flash_disk_quiescent();
    if (quiescent)
      hold_cpu();
    restore_interrupts(interrupts);
    if (quiescent) {
#ifdef Z80_STAGE10_NETWORK
      if (config_reboot_after_stop) {
        config_reboot_after_stop = false;
        config_reboot_ready = true;
        config_reboot_deadline = make_timeout_time_ms(1000);
        if (web_reboot_active)
          z80_web_terminal_set_reboot_status(Z80_WEB_REBOOT_RESTARTING);
        printf("\n[config] Disks flushed; RESET held LOW, PWM stopped. "
               "Rebooting in one second.\n");
      } else
#endif
      {
        printf("\n[diag] Disk quiescent; RESET held LOW, PWM stopped. "
               "Ctrl-] r reboots/reloads the supervisor.\n");
        print_help();
      }
    } else {
      flash_resuming = true;
      __atomic_store_n(&flash_pause_request, 0, __ATOMIC_RELEASE);
    }
  } else if (!flush_submitted &&
             z80_flash_disk_status() == DISK_READY) {
    z80_flash_disk_io_write(0x10, 5);
    flush_submitted = true;
  }
}

int main(void) {
  z80_safe_startup();
  reset_was_watchdog = watchdog_caused_reboot();
  reset_fault = z80_io_trap_take_reset_fault();
  set_sys_clock_pll(1200000000, 5, 2);
  z80_terminal_queue_init();
  queue_init(&control_commands, sizeof(uint16_t), 4);
  z80_usb_console_prepare();
#ifdef Z80_STAGE10_NETWORK
  z80_network_setup_init();
#endif
  bool clock_ready = clock_get_hz(clk_sys) == SYSTEM_CLOCK_HZ;
#ifdef Z80_STAGE10_NETWORK
  multicore_launch_core1_with_stack(core1_main, core1_network_stack,
                                   sizeof(core1_network_stack));
#else
  multicore_launch_core1(core1_main);
#endif
  core1_started = true;
  absolute_time_t ready_deadline = make_timeout_time_ms(1000);
  while (!__atomic_load_n(&core1_ready, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE) &&
         !time_reached(ready_deadline))
    tight_loop_contents();
  if (!clock_ready ||
      __atomic_load_n(&core1_ready, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE) != 1) {
    z80_cpu_fail_closed();
    startup_failed = true;
    boot_failure = !clock_ready ? "expected 120 MHz supervisor clock"
                               : "core 1 USB/flash-safe initialization";
    while (true) {
      printf("FAIL: %s; CPU held reset\n", boot_failure);
      service_control();
      busy_wait_us_32(1000000);
      tight_loop_contents();
    }
  }
  if (Z80_STAGE09_AUTOBOOT) {
    load_image();
    if (image_verified)
      start_cpm();
  }
  publish_cpu_state();
  while (true) {
    if (__atomic_load_n(&workers_ready, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE))
      z80_flash_core0_service();
    if (core1_started && z80_io_ports_reboot_requested()) {
      hold_cpu();
      watchdog_reboot(0, 0, 0);
      while (true)
        tight_loop_contents();
    }
    service_control();
    service_run();
    publish_cpu_state();
    tight_loop_contents();
  }
}
Shared terminal queues and transport handover 
#include "z80sbc/terminal.h"

#include <string.h>

#include "pico/critical_section.h"
#include "pico/stdlib.h"

enum {
  TERM_DATA_PORT = 0x00,
  TERM_STATUS_PORT = 0x01,
  TERM_RX_DEPTH = 128,
  TERM_TX_DEPTH = 512,
  TERM_STATUS_RX_READY = 1u << 0,
  TERM_STATUS_TX_ROOM = 1u << 1,
  TERM_STATUS_CLIENT = 1u << 7,
};

typedef struct {
  uint8_t *data;
  size_t capacity;
  size_t head;
  size_t count;
  size_t peak;
} terminal_ring_t;

static uint8_t rx_data[TERM_RX_DEPTH];
static uint8_t tx_data[TERM_TX_DEPTH];
static terminal_ring_t rx_queue = {rx_data, TERM_RX_DEPTH, 0, 0, 0};
static terminal_ring_t tx_queue = {tx_data, TERM_TX_DEPTH, 0, 0, 0};
static critical_section_t terminal_lock;
static uint32_t client_connected;
static uint32_t browser_connected;
static bool usb_connected;
static uint32_t rx_drops;
static uint32_t tx_drops;

static void clear_queues(void) {
  rx_queue.head = rx_queue.count = 0;
  tx_queue.head = tx_queue.count = 0;
}

static void __not_in_flash_func(ring_add)(terminal_ring_t *ring, uint8_t value) {
  ring->data[(ring->head + ring->count++) & (ring->capacity - 1)] = value;
  if (ring->count > ring->peak)
    ring->peak = ring->count;
}

static size_t ring_peek(const terminal_ring_t *ring, uint8_t *data,
                        size_t capacity) {
  size_t count = capacity < ring->count ? capacity : ring->count;
  size_t first = ring->capacity - ring->head;
  if (first > count)
    first = count;
  memcpy(data, ring->data + ring->head, first);
  memcpy(data + first, ring->data, count - first);
  return count;
}

static size_t ring_remove(terminal_ring_t *ring, uint8_t *data,
                          size_t capacity) {
  size_t count = ring_peek(ring, data, capacity);
  ring->head = (ring->head + count) & (ring->capacity - 1);
  ring->count -= count;
  return count;
}

void z80_terminal_queue_init(void) {
  if (!critical_section_is_initialized(&terminal_lock))
    critical_section_init(&terminal_lock);
  clear_queues();
  rx_queue.peak = tx_queue.peak = 0;
  __atomic_store_n(&client_connected, 0, __ATOMIC_RELEASE);
  __atomic_store_n(&browser_connected, 0, __ATOMIC_RELEASE);
  usb_connected = false;
  __atomic_store_n(&rx_drops, 0, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
  __atomic_store_n(&tx_drops, 0, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
}

uint8_t __not_in_flash_func(z80_terminal_io_read)(uint8_t port) {
  if (port != TERM_DATA_PORT && port != TERM_STATUS_PORT)
    return 0xFF;
  critical_section_enter_blocking(&terminal_lock);
  uint8_t value = 0;
  if (port == TERM_DATA_PORT) {
    if (rx_queue.count) {
      value = rx_queue.data[rx_queue.head];
      rx_queue.head = (rx_queue.head + 1) & (TERM_RX_DEPTH - 1);
      --rx_queue.count;
    }
  } else {
    bool connected = z80_terminal_client_connected();
    if (rx_queue.count)
      value |= TERM_STATUS_RX_READY;
    if (!connected || tx_queue.count < TERM_TX_DEPTH)
      value |= TERM_STATUS_TX_ROOM;
    if (connected)
      value |= TERM_STATUS_CLIENT;
  }
  critical_section_exit(&terminal_lock);
  return value;
}

void __not_in_flash_func(z80_terminal_io_write)(uint8_t port, uint8_t value) {
  if (port != TERM_DATA_PORT)
    return;
  critical_section_enter_blocking(&terminal_lock);
  if (z80_terminal_client_connected()) {
    if (tx_queue.count < TERM_TX_DEPTH)
      ring_add(&tx_queue, value);
    else
      __atomic_fetch_add(&tx_drops, 1, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
  }
  critical_section_exit(&terminal_lock);
}

void z80_terminal_receive(const uint8_t *data, size_t length) {
  if (data == NULL)
    return;
  for (size_t index = 0; index < length; ++index) {
    critical_section_enter_blocking(&terminal_lock);
    if (rx_queue.count == TERM_RX_DEPTH) {
      rx_queue.head = (rx_queue.head + 1) & (TERM_RX_DEPTH - 1);
      --rx_queue.count;
      __atomic_fetch_add(&rx_drops, 1, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
    }
    ring_add(&rx_queue, data[index] == '\n' ? '\r' : data[index]);
    critical_section_exit(&terminal_lock);
  }
}

size_t z80_terminal_peek(uint8_t *data, size_t capacity) {
  if (data == NULL)
    return 0;
  critical_section_enter_blocking(&terminal_lock);
  size_t count = ring_peek(&tx_queue, data, capacity);
  critical_section_exit(&terminal_lock);
  return count;
}

size_t z80_terminal_supply(uint8_t *data, size_t capacity) {
  if (data == NULL)
    return 0;
  critical_section_enter_blocking(&terminal_lock);
  size_t count = ring_remove(&tx_queue, data, capacity);
  critical_section_exit(&terminal_lock);
  return count;
}

bool z80_terminal_browser_try_receive(const uint8_t *data, size_t length) {
  if (data == NULL || length == 0 || length > TERM_RX_DEPTH)
    return false;
  critical_section_enter_blocking(&terminal_lock);
  bool accepted = z80_terminal_browser_connected() &&
                  TERM_RX_DEPTH - rx_queue.count >= length;
  if (accepted)
    for (size_t i = 0; i < length; ++i)
      ring_add(&rx_queue, data[i] == '\n' ? '\r' : data[i]);
  critical_section_exit(&terminal_lock);
  return accepted;
}

void z80_terminal_browser_connect(void) {
  critical_section_enter_blocking(&terminal_lock);
  clear_queues();
  __atomic_store_n(&browser_connected, 1, __ATOMIC_RELEASE);
  __atomic_store_n(&client_connected, 1, __ATOMIC_RELEASE);
  critical_section_exit(&terminal_lock);
}

void z80_terminal_set_connected(bool connected) {
  critical_section_enter_blocking(&terminal_lock);
  __atomic_store_n(&client_connected, connected, __ATOMIC_RELEASE);
  if (!connected)
    tx_queue.head = tx_queue.count = 0;
  critical_section_exit(&terminal_lock);
}

void z80_terminal_browser_disconnect(void) {
  critical_section_enter_blocking(&terminal_lock);
  if (z80_terminal_browser_connected()) {
    __atomic_store_n(&browser_connected, 0, __ATOMIC_RELEASE);
    __atomic_store_n(&client_connected, usb_connected, __ATOMIC_RELEASE);
    clear_queues();
  }
  critical_section_exit(&terminal_lock);
}

bool z80_terminal_browser_connected(void) {
  return __atomic_load_n(&browser_connected, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE) != 0;
}

void z80_terminal_usb_connected(bool connected) {
  critical_section_enter_blocking(&terminal_lock);
  if (!z80_terminal_browser_connected()) {
    __atomic_store_n(&client_connected, connected, __ATOMIC_RELEASE);
    if (usb_connected != connected)
      clear_queues();
  }
  usb_connected = connected;
  critical_section_exit(&terminal_lock);
}

void z80_terminal_usb_receive(uint8_t value) {
  critical_section_enter_blocking(&terminal_lock);
  if (usb_connected && !z80_terminal_browser_connected()) {
    if (rx_queue.count == TERM_RX_DEPTH) {
      rx_queue.head = (rx_queue.head + 1) & (TERM_RX_DEPTH - 1);
      --rx_queue.count;
      __atomic_fetch_add(&rx_drops, 1, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
    }
    ring_add(&rx_queue, value == '\n' ? '\r' : value);
  }
  critical_section_exit(&terminal_lock);
}

size_t z80_terminal_usb_supply(uint8_t *data, size_t capacity) {
  if (data == NULL)
    return 0;
  critical_section_enter_blocking(&terminal_lock);
  size_t count = usb_connected && !z80_terminal_browser_connected()
                     ? ring_remove(&tx_queue, data, capacity) : 0;
  critical_section_exit(&terminal_lock);
  return count;
}

uint32_t z80_terminal_rx_drop_count(void) {
  return __atomic_load_n(&rx_drops, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
}

uint32_t z80_terminal_tx_drop_count(void) {
  return __atomic_load_n(&tx_drops, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
}

z80_terminal_buffer_stats_t z80_terminal_get_buffer_stats(void) {
  critical_section_enter_blocking(&terminal_lock);
  z80_terminal_buffer_stats_t stats = {
      (uint32_t)rx_queue.count, TERM_RX_DEPTH, (uint32_t)rx_queue.peak,
      (uint32_t)tx_queue.count, TERM_TX_DEPTH, (uint32_t)tx_queue.peak,
  };
  critical_section_exit(&terminal_lock);
  return stats;
}

bool __not_in_flash_func(z80_terminal_client_connected)(void) {
  return __atomic_load_n(&client_connected, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE) != 0;
}
Core-1 network lifecycle 
#include "network_runtime.h"

#include <cstdio>
#include <cstring>

#include "pico/cyw43_arch.h"
#include "pico/stdlib.h"
#include "lwip/apps/sntp.h"
#include "lwip/netif.h"
#include "network_setup.h"
#include "z80sbc/io_ports.h"
#include "../common/io_service.h"

namespace {
constexpr uint32_t RETRY_DELAY_MS = 5000;
constexpr uint32_t ASSOCIATION_TIMEOUT_MS = 30000;
enum class WifiState { uninitialized, associating, online, association_backoff };
WifiState wifi_state = WifiState::uninitialized;
absolute_time_t retry_deadline = nil_time;
absolute_time_t association_deadline = nil_time;
absolute_time_t address_deadline = nil_time;
bool time_client_started;
z80_network_config_t active_config = {};
uint32_t network_generation;

void clear_address() {
  ++network_generation;
  z80_io_ports_set_network_address("");
  address_deadline = nil_time;
}

void start_association() {
  int result = cyw43_arch_wifi_connect_async(
      active_config.ssid, active_config.password,
      active_config.password[0] ? CYW43_AUTH_WPA2_AES_PSK : CYW43_AUTH_OPEN);
  if (result == PICO_OK) {
    association_deadline = make_timeout_time_ms(ASSOCIATION_TIMEOUT_MS);
    wifi_state = WifiState::associating;
  } else {
    retry_deadline = make_timeout_time_ms(RETRY_DELAY_MS);
    wifi_state = WifiState::association_backoff;
    printf("[network] FAIL: association start=%d; retry in 5 seconds.\n", result);
  }
}

void refresh_network_address() {
  if (!time_reached(address_deadline))
    return;
  address_deadline = make_timeout_time_ms(1000);
  char address[16] = {};
  cyw43_arch_lwip_begin();
  if (netif_default != nullptr &&
      ip4addr_ntoa_r(netif_ip4_addr(netif_default), address,
                     sizeof(address)) == nullptr) {
    address[0] = '\0';
    printf("[network] FAIL: IPv4 address formatting.\n");
  }
  cyw43_arch_lwip_end();
  if (strcmp(address, "0.0.0.0") == 0)
    address[0] = '\0';
  char previous[16];
  z80_io_ports_get_network_address(previous, sizeof(previous));
  if (strcmp(previous, address) != 0)
    z80_io_ports_set_network_address(address);
}
}  // namespace

extern "C" uint32_t z80_network_generation(void) {
  return network_generation;
}

extern "C" bool z80_network_poll(void) {
  if (!z80_wireless_init())
    return false;
  cyw43_arch_poll();
  const z80_network_config_t *config = z80_network_config();
  if (config == nullptr) {
    if (wifi_state != WifiState::uninitialized) {
      clear_address();
      cyw43_wifi_leave(&cyw43_state, CYW43_ITF_STA);
      wifi_state = WifiState::uninitialized;
      active_config = {};
    }
    return false;
  }
  if (strcmp(active_config.ssid, config->ssid) != 0 ||
      strcmp(active_config.password, config->password) != 0) {
    clear_address();
    if (wifi_state != WifiState::uninitialized)
      cyw43_wifi_leave(&cyw43_state, CYW43_ITF_STA);
    active_config = *config;
    wifi_state = WifiState::uninitialized;
  }
  if (wifi_state == WifiState::uninitialized) {
    cyw43_arch_enable_sta_mode();
    start_association();
    return false;
  }
  if (wifi_state == WifiState::association_backoff) {
    if (time_reached(retry_deadline))
      start_association();
    return false;
  }

  cyw43_arch_lwip_begin();
  int status = cyw43_tcpip_link_status(&cyw43_state, CYW43_ITF_STA);
  cyw43_arch_lwip_end();
  if (wifi_state == WifiState::associating) {
    if (status == CYW43_LINK_UP) {
      int result = cyw43_wifi_pm(&cyw43_state, CYW43_NO_POWERSAVE_MODE);
      if (result != PICO_OK) {
        cyw43_wifi_leave(&cyw43_state, CYW43_ITF_STA);
        retry_deadline = make_timeout_time_ms(RETRY_DELAY_MS);
        wifi_state = WifiState::association_backoff;
        printf("[network] FAIL: disabling Wi-Fi power saving=%d; retry in 5 seconds.\n",
               result);
        return false;
      }
      cyw43_arch_lwip_begin();
      if (!time_client_started) {
        sntp_setoperatingmode(SNTP_OPMODE_POLL);
        sntp_setservername(0, "pool.ntp.org");
        sntp_init();
        time_client_started = true;
      }
      cyw43_arch_lwip_end();
      wifi_state = WifiState::online;
    } else if (status < CYW43_LINK_DOWN || time_reached(association_deadline)) {
      cyw43_wifi_leave(&cyw43_state, CYW43_ITF_STA);
      retry_deadline = make_timeout_time_ms(RETRY_DELAY_MS);
      wifi_state = WifiState::association_backoff;
      printf("[network] FAIL: association status=%d or timeout; retry in 5 seconds.\n",
             status);
      return false;
    } else {
      return false;
    }
  }
  if (status != CYW43_LINK_UP) {
    clear_address();
    cyw43_wifi_leave(&cyw43_state, CYW43_ITF_STA);
    retry_deadline = make_timeout_time_ms(RETRY_DELAY_MS);
    wifi_state = WifiState::association_backoff;
    printf("[network] Wi-Fi link lost; retry in 5 seconds.\n");
    return false;
  }
  refresh_network_address();
  return true;
}
