#include <atomic>
#include <cstdint>
#include <cstdio>
#include <cstring>
#include <new>

#include "pico/cyw43_arch.h"
#include "pico/stdlib.h"
#include "pico_ws_server/web_socket_server.h"
#include "web_terminal.h"
#include "z80sbc/io_ports.h"
#include "z80sbc/terminal.h"

namespace {
constexpr uint16_t SERVER_PORT = Z80_WEB_TERMINAL_PORT;
constexpr uint32_t SERVER_CONNECTIONS = 4;
constexpr uint32_t SERVER_RETRY_MS = 5000;
constexpr size_t FRAME_BYTES = Z80_WEB_TERMINAL_FRAME_BYTES;
constexpr size_t INPUT_BYTES = 64;
constexpr size_t HEADER_BYTES = 5;
constexpr size_t OUTPUT_WINDOW = Z80_WEB_TERMINAL_OUTPUT_WINDOW;
constexpr uint32_t OUTPUT_COALESCE_US = 1000;
constexpr uint32_t PROTOCOL_VERSION = 4;
constexpr uint32_t FRAME_RETRY_MS = 250;
constexpr uint32_t REBOOT_DEADLINE_MS = 35000;
constexpr uint32_t HEARTBEAT_MS = 30u * 1000u;
constexpr uint32_t PONG_TIMEOUT_MS = 20u * 1000u;
// Tolerate two misses; disconnect on the third consecutive miss.
constexpr uint8_t MAX_MISSED_PONGS = 2;
// xterm ACKs output only after its write callback runs; allow a backgrounded
// or busy browser to drain the bounded output window before restoring USB.
constexpr uint32_t OUTPUT_ACK_TIMEOUT_MS = 5u * 60u * 1000u;
enum : uint8_t {
  OUTPUT = 1, INPUT = 2, OUTPUT_ACK = 3, INPUT_ACK = 4,
  HELLO = 5, READY = 6, REBOOT = 7, REBOOT_STATUS = 8,
};

struct OutputFrame {
  uint8_t data[HEADER_BYTES + FRAME_BYTES];
  size_t length;
  absolute_time_t retry;
  absolute_time_t deadline;
  bool sent;
};
OutputFrame output_frames[OUTPUT_WINDOW];
size_t output_head;
size_t output_count;
size_t retained_output_bytes;
size_t staged_output_length;
absolute_time_t output_batch_deadline = nil_time;
z80_web_terminal_stats_t terminal_stats;
uint8_t pending_input[INPUT_BYTES];
size_t pending_input_length;
uint32_t output_sequence;
uint32_t input_sequence;
bool input_ack_pending;
bool protocol_ready;
std::atomic<uint32_t> reboot_status{Z80_WEB_REBOOT_IDLE};
uint32_t reported_reboot_status = UINT32_MAX;
// Core 1 owns this deadline. Keep it across browser disconnects so core 0
// cannot leave a request looking active forever if its main loop stalls.
absolute_time_t reboot_deadline;
bool reboot_deadline_active;
WebSocketServer *server;
bool server_started;
absolute_time_t server_retry_deadline = nil_time;
std::atomic<int32_t> active_connection{-1};
// Retain the closing session's identity until its deferred diagnostics arrive.
std::atomic<int32_t> last_disconnected_connection{-1};
std::atomic<bool> pending_connected{false};
std::atomic<bool> pending_disconnected{false};
std::atomic<uint32_t> pending_ws_close_reason{
    (uint32_t)WebSocketServer::CloseReason::unknown};
std::atomic<int32_t> pending_ws_transport_error{0};
absolute_time_t hello_retry;
absolute_time_t ping_retry;
absolute_time_t pong_deadline;
uint32_t ping_sequence;
uint8_t ping_payload[4];
bool awaiting_pong;
bool activity_since_ping;
uint8_t missed_pongs;
uint32_t session_network_generation;
bool network_online;

void increment_stat(uint32_t &counter, uint32_t amount = 1) {
  __atomic_fetch_add(&counter, amount, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
}

void set_disconnect_reason(z80_web_terminal_disconnect_reason_t reason) {
  __atomic_store_n(&terminal_stats.last_disconnect_reason, (uint32_t)reason,
                   __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
}

const char *ws_close_reason_name(WebSocketServer::CloseReason reason) {
  switch (reason) {
  case WebSocketServer::CloseReason::peer_tcp_closed: return "peer-tcp-closed";
  case WebSocketServer::CloseReason::peer_websocket_close: return "peer-ws-close";
  case WebSocketServer::CloseReason::invalid_websocket_input: return "invalid-ws-input";
  case WebSocketServer::CloseReason::receive_queue_message_limit: return "receive-queue-message-limit";
  case WebSocketServer::CloseReason::receive_queue_byte_limit: return "receive-queue-byte-limit";
  case WebSocketServer::CloseReason::pong_backpressure: return "pong-backpressure";
  case WebSocketServer::CloseReason::tcp_write_error: return "tcp-write-error";
  case WebSocketServer::CloseReason::tcp_output_error: return "tcp-output-error";
  case WebSocketServer::CloseReason::tcp_error: return "tcp-error";
  case WebSocketServer::CloseReason::close_timeout: return "close-timeout";
  case WebSocketServer::CloseReason::server_abort: return "server-abort";
  case WebSocketServer::CloseReason::local_close: return "local-close";
  default: return "unknown";
  }
}

uint32_t ws_close_reason_code(WebSocketServer::CloseReason reason) {
  switch (reason) {
  case WebSocketServer::CloseReason::peer_tcp_closed: return Z80_WEB_TERMINAL_WS_CLOSE_PEER_TCP_CLOSED;
  case WebSocketServer::CloseReason::peer_websocket_close: return Z80_WEB_TERMINAL_WS_CLOSE_PEER_WEBSOCKET_CLOSE;
  case WebSocketServer::CloseReason::invalid_websocket_input: return Z80_WEB_TERMINAL_WS_CLOSE_INVALID_INPUT;
  case WebSocketServer::CloseReason::receive_queue_message_limit: return Z80_WEB_TERMINAL_WS_CLOSE_RECEIVE_QUEUE_MESSAGE_LIMIT;
  case WebSocketServer::CloseReason::receive_queue_byte_limit: return Z80_WEB_TERMINAL_WS_CLOSE_RECEIVE_QUEUE_BYTE_LIMIT;
  case WebSocketServer::CloseReason::pong_backpressure: return Z80_WEB_TERMINAL_WS_CLOSE_PONG_BACKPRESSURE;
  case WebSocketServer::CloseReason::tcp_write_error: return Z80_WEB_TERMINAL_WS_CLOSE_TCP_WRITE_ERROR;
  case WebSocketServer::CloseReason::tcp_output_error: return Z80_WEB_TERMINAL_WS_CLOSE_TCP_OUTPUT_ERROR;
  case WebSocketServer::CloseReason::tcp_error: return Z80_WEB_TERMINAL_WS_CLOSE_TCP_ERROR;
  case WebSocketServer::CloseReason::close_timeout: return Z80_WEB_TERMINAL_WS_CLOSE_TIMEOUT;
  case WebSocketServer::CloseReason::server_abort: return Z80_WEB_TERMINAL_WS_CLOSE_SERVER_ABORT;
  case WebSocketServer::CloseReason::local_close: return Z80_WEB_TERMINAL_WS_CLOSE_LOCAL_CLOSE;
  default: return Z80_WEB_TERMINAL_WS_CLOSE_UNKNOWN;
  }
}

void on_close_details(WebSocketServer &, uint32_t connection,
                      WebSocketServer::CloseReason reason, int transport_error,
                      size_t queued_messages, size_t queued_bytes,
                      size_t peak_queued_messages, size_t peak_queued_bytes,
                      size_t queue_message_limit, size_t queue_byte_limit) {
  int32_t active = active_connection.load(std::memory_order_acquire);
  if (active != (int32_t)connection &&
      last_disconnected_connection.load(std::memory_order_acquire) !=
          (int32_t)connection)
    return;
  last_disconnected_connection.store((int32_t)connection,
                                      std::memory_order_release);
  pending_ws_close_reason.store((uint32_t)reason, std::memory_order_release);
  pending_ws_transport_error.store(transport_error, std::memory_order_release);
  __atomic_store_n(&terminal_stats.last_ws_close_reason, ws_close_reason_code(reason),
                   __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
  __atomic_store_n(&terminal_stats.last_ws_transport_error, transport_error,
                   __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
  __atomic_store_n(&terminal_stats.last_ws_queue_messages,
                   (uint32_t)queued_messages, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
  __atomic_store_n(&terminal_stats.last_ws_queue_bytes,
                   (uint32_t)queued_bytes, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
  __atomic_store_n(&terminal_stats.last_ws_queue_peak_messages,
                   (uint32_t)peak_queued_messages, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
  __atomic_store_n(&terminal_stats.last_ws_queue_peak_bytes,
                   (uint32_t)peak_queued_bytes, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
  __atomic_store_n(&terminal_stats.last_ws_queue_message_limit,
                   (uint32_t)queue_message_limit, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
  __atomic_store_n(&terminal_stats.last_ws_queue_byte_limit,
                   (uint32_t)queue_byte_limit, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
  // A previous session may finish closing after its replacement connects.
  if (active >= 0 && active != (int32_t)connection)
    return;
  __atomic_store_n(&terminal_stats.rx_queue_messages,
                   active >= 0 ? (uint32_t)queued_messages : 0, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
  __atomic_store_n(&terminal_stats.rx_queue_bytes,
                   active >= 0 ? (uint32_t)queued_bytes : 0, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
  __atomic_store_n(&terminal_stats.rx_queue_peak_messages,
                   (uint32_t)peak_queued_messages, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
  __atomic_store_n(&terminal_stats.rx_queue_peak_bytes,
                   (uint32_t)peak_queued_bytes, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
  __atomic_store_n(&terminal_stats.rx_queue_message_limit,
                   (uint32_t)queue_message_limit, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
  __atomic_store_n(&terminal_stats.rx_queue_byte_limit,
                   (uint32_t)queue_byte_limit, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
}

void record_peak(uint32_t &counter, uint32_t value) {
  if (value > __atomic_load_n(&counter, __ATOMIC_RELAXED))
    __atomic_store_n(&counter, value, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
}

void publish_buffer_usage() {
  uint32_t frames = (uint32_t)output_count;
  uint32_t bytes = (uint32_t)(retained_output_bytes + staged_output_length);
  __atomic_store_n(&terminal_stats.window_frames, frames, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
  __atomic_store_n(&terminal_stats.retained_bytes, bytes, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
  __atomic_store_n(&terminal_stats.staged_bytes, (uint32_t)staged_output_length,
                   __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
  record_peak(terminal_stats.window_frames_peak, frames);
  record_peak(terminal_stats.retained_bytes_peak, bytes);
}

void reset_receive_queue_usage() {
  __atomic_store_n(&terminal_stats.rx_queue_messages, 0, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
  __atomic_store_n(&terminal_stats.rx_queue_bytes, 0, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
  __atomic_store_n(&terminal_stats.rx_queue_peak_messages, 0, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
  __atomic_store_n(&terminal_stats.rx_queue_peak_bytes, 0, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
  __atomic_store_n(&terminal_stats.rx_queue_message_limit, 0, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
  __atomic_store_n(&terminal_stats.rx_queue_byte_limit, 0, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
}

void clear_receive_queue_current() {
  __atomic_store_n(&terminal_stats.rx_queue_messages, 0, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
  __atomic_store_n(&terminal_stats.rx_queue_bytes, 0, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
}

uint32_t read_sequence(const uint8_t *data) {
  return (uint32_t)data[0] | (uint32_t)data[1] << 8 |
         (uint32_t)data[2] << 16 | (uint32_t)data[3] << 24;
}

void write_sequence(uint8_t *data, uint32_t value) {
  for (unsigned i = 0; i < 4; ++i)
    data[i] = (uint8_t)(value >> (8 * i));
}

void reset_session() {
  protocol_ready = false;
  reported_reboot_status = UINT32_MAX;
  input_sequence = output_sequence = 1;
  output_head = output_count = pending_input_length = 0;
  input_ack_pending = false;
  staged_output_length = 0;
  retained_output_bytes = 0;
  publish_buffer_usage();
  output_batch_deadline = nil_time;
  hello_retry = nil_time;
  ping_retry = nil_time;
  awaiting_pong = false;
  activity_since_ping = false;
  missed_pongs = 0;
  pong_deadline = nil_time;
}

void note_browser_activity() {
  missed_pongs = 0;
  if (awaiting_pong)
    activity_since_ping = true;
}

void close_connection(WebSocketServer &websocket, uint32_t connection) {
  if (!websocket.close(connection))
    printf("[network] Close frame not sent; connection scheduled for cleanup.\n");
}

void disconnect_client(z80_web_terminal_disconnect_reason_t reason) {
  int32_t connection = active_connection.exchange(-1, std::memory_order_acq_rel);
  if (connection >= 0) {
    last_disconnected_connection.store(connection, std::memory_order_release);
    set_disconnect_reason(reason);
    // Do not pair this new disconnect with a previous session's close details.
    __atomic_store_n(&terminal_stats.last_ws_close_reason,
                     Z80_WEB_TERMINAL_WS_CLOSE_UNKNOWN, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
    __atomic_store_n(&terminal_stats.last_ws_transport_error, 0, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
    __atomic_store_n(&terminal_stats.last_ws_queue_messages, 0, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
    __atomic_store_n(&terminal_stats.last_ws_queue_bytes, 0, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
    __atomic_store_n(&terminal_stats.last_ws_queue_peak_messages, 0, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
    __atomic_store_n(&terminal_stats.last_ws_queue_peak_bytes, 0, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
    __atomic_store_n(&terminal_stats.last_ws_queue_message_limit, 0, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
    __atomic_store_n(&terminal_stats.last_ws_queue_byte_limit, 0, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
    clear_receive_queue_current();
  }
  if (connection >= 0 && server != nullptr && !server->abort((uint32_t)connection))
    printf("[network] Terminal connection already removed during teardown.\n");
  pending_connected.store(false, std::memory_order_release);
  pending_disconnected.store(false, std::memory_order_release);
  z80_terminal_browser_disconnect();
  reset_session();
}

bool send_control(uint8_t type, uint32_t sequence) {
  uint8_t frame[HEADER_BYTES] = {type};
  write_sequence(frame + 1, sequence);
  return server->sendMessage((uint32_t)active_connection.load(), frame,
                             sizeof(frame));
}

void check_reboot_deadline() {
  if (!reboot_deadline_active)
    return;
  uint32_t status = reboot_status.load(std::memory_order_acquire);
  while (status == Z80_WEB_REBOOT_REQUESTED || status == Z80_WEB_REBOOT_FLUSHING ||
         status == Z80_WEB_REBOOT_RESTARTING) {
    if (!time_reached(reboot_deadline))
      return;
    if (reboot_status.compare_exchange_weak(status, Z80_WEB_REBOOT_TIMEOUT,
                                             std::memory_order_acq_rel)) {
      printf("[web] Reboot timed out waiting for supervisor progress. "
             "No forced reset; inspect USB supervisor status.\n");
      break;
    }
  }
  reboot_deadline_active = false;
}

void report_reboot_status() {
  uint32_t status = reboot_status.load(std::memory_order_acquire);
  if (protocol_ready && status != reported_reboot_status && send_control(REBOOT_STATUS, status)) {
    reported_reboot_status = status;
    // A watchdog reset sends no TCP FIN. Close explicitly while the network is
    // still alive so the browser can reconnect without waiting for TCP timeout.
    if (status == Z80_WEB_REBOOT_RESTARTING)
      close_connection(*server, (uint32_t)active_connection.load());
  }
}

void retry_input_ack() {
  if (input_ack_pending && send_control(INPUT_ACK, input_sequence - 1))
    input_ack_pending = false;
}

void accept_pending_input() {
  if (!pending_input_length ||
      !z80_terminal_browser_try_receive(pending_input, pending_input_length))
    return;
  pending_input_length = 0;
  ++input_sequence;
  input_ack_pending = true;
  retry_input_ack();
}

void on_connect(WebSocketServer &websocket, uint32_t connection) {
  int32_t expected = -1;
  if (active_connection.compare_exchange_strong(
          expected, (int32_t)connection, std::memory_order_acq_rel)) {
    reset_receive_queue_usage();
    pending_connected.store(true, std::memory_order_release);
  } else {
    close_connection(websocket, connection);
    printf("[network] Terminal busy; rejected another browser.\n");
  }
}

void on_close(WebSocketServer &, uint32_t connection) {
  int32_t expected = (int32_t)connection;
  if (active_connection.compare_exchange_strong(
          expected, -1, std::memory_order_acq_rel)) {
    last_disconnected_connection.store((int32_t)connection,
                                        std::memory_order_release);
    set_disconnect_reason(Z80_WEB_TERMINAL_DISCONNECT_SOCKET_CLOSED);
    clear_receive_queue_current();
    pending_disconnected.store(true, std::memory_order_release);
  }
}

void on_message(WebSocketServer &, uint32_t connection,
                const void *data, size_t length) {
  if (active_connection.load(std::memory_order_acquire) != (int32_t)connection)
    return;
  const uint8_t *frame = static_cast<const uint8_t *>(data);
  if (length < HEADER_BYTES) {
    printf("[network] FAIL: invalid terminal protocol; reload the terminal page.\n");
    disconnect_client(Z80_WEB_TERMINAL_DISCONNECT_PROTOCOL_ERROR);
    return;
  }
  uint32_t sequence = read_sequence(frame + 1);
  if (frame[0] == READY && length == HEADER_BYTES &&
      sequence == PROTOCOL_VERSION) {
    protocol_ready = true;
    report_reboot_status();
    if (ping_retry == nil_time)
      ping_retry = make_timeout_time_ms(HEARTBEAT_MS);
    note_browser_activity();
  } else if (frame[0] == REBOOT && protocol_ready &&
             length == HEADER_BYTES && sequence == 0) {
    note_browser_activity();
    uint32_t status = reboot_status.load(std::memory_order_acquire);
    // Repeated commands cannot restart an active operation. Failure can be
    // retried, but only core 0 decides whether it is safe to proceed.
    while (status != Z80_WEB_REBOOT_REQUESTED &&
           status != Z80_WEB_REBOOT_FLUSHING &&
           status != Z80_WEB_REBOOT_RESTARTING &&
           status != Z80_WEB_REBOOT_TIMEOUT) {
      if (reboot_status.compare_exchange_weak(status, Z80_WEB_REBOOT_REQUESTED,
                                               std::memory_order_acq_rel)) {
        reboot_deadline = make_timeout_time_ms(REBOOT_DEADLINE_MS);
        reboot_deadline_active = true;
        break;
      }
    }
    reported_reboot_status = UINT32_MAX;
  } else if (frame[0] == OUTPUT_ACK && protocol_ready &&
             length == HEADER_BYTES) {
    note_browser_activity();
    for (size_t i = 0; i < output_count; ++i) {
      const OutputFrame &candidate = output_frames[(output_head + i) % OUTPUT_WINDOW];
      if (candidate.sent && read_sequence(candidate.data + 1) == sequence) {
        for (size_t j = 0; j <= i; ++j)
          retained_output_bytes -=
              output_frames[(output_head + j) % OUTPUT_WINDOW].length - HEADER_BYTES;
        output_head = (output_head + i + 1) % OUTPUT_WINDOW;
        output_count -= i + 1;
        publish_buffer_usage();
        break;
      }
    }
  } else if (frame[0] == INPUT && protocol_ready &&
             length > HEADER_BYTES && length <= HEADER_BYTES + INPUT_BYTES) {
    note_browser_activity();
    if (sequence == input_sequence) {
      size_t bytes = length - HEADER_BYTES;
      if (pending_input_length &&
          (pending_input_length != bytes ||
           memcmp(pending_input, frame + HEADER_BYTES, bytes) != 0)) {
        printf("[network] FAIL: changed pending terminal input; disconnecting.\n");
        disconnect_client(Z80_WEB_TERMINAL_DISCONNECT_PROTOCOL_ERROR);
        return;
      }
      memcpy(pending_input, frame + HEADER_BYTES, bytes);
      pending_input_length = bytes;
      accept_pending_input();
    } else if (sequence == input_sequence - 1) {
      input_ack_pending = true;
      retry_input_ack();
    } else {
      printf("[network] FAIL: out-of-order terminal input; disconnecting.\n");
      disconnect_client(Z80_WEB_TERMINAL_DISCONNECT_PROTOCOL_ERROR);
    }
  } else {
    printf("[network] FAIL: invalid terminal frame; reload the terminal page.\n");
    disconnect_client(Z80_WEB_TERMINAL_DISCONNECT_PROTOCOL_ERROR);
  }
}

void on_pong(WebSocketServer &, uint32_t connection,
             const void *data, size_t length) {
  if (active_connection.load() != (int32_t)connection)
    return;
  if (awaiting_pong && length == sizeof(ping_payload) &&
      memcmp(data, ping_payload, length) == 0) {
    awaiting_pong = false;
    missed_pongs = 0;
    activity_since_ping = false;
    pong_deadline = nil_time;
  } else {
    // Even a late PONG proves the peer is responsive and can satisfy a
    // newer ping's liveness check through note_browser_activity().
    note_browser_activity();
  }
}

void process_events() {
  if (pending_disconnected.exchange(false, std::memory_order_acq_rel)) {
    auto reason = (WebSocketServer::CloseReason)pending_ws_close_reason.load(
        std::memory_order_acquire);
    int transport_error = pending_ws_transport_error.load(std::memory_order_acquire);
    printf("[network] WebSocket server closed connection: %s",
           ws_close_reason_name(reason));
    if (transport_error)
      printf(" (lwIP error=%d)", transport_error);
    printf("; queue=%lu/%lu messages, peak=%lu/%lu; bytes=%lu/%lu, peak=%lu/%lu.\n",
           (unsigned long)__atomic_load_n(&terminal_stats.last_ws_queue_messages,
                                          __ATOMIC_RELAXED),
           (unsigned long)__atomic_load_n(&terminal_stats.last_ws_queue_message_limit,
                                          __ATOMIC_RELAXED),
           (unsigned long)__atomic_load_n(&terminal_stats.last_ws_queue_peak_messages,
                                          __ATOMIC_RELAXED),
           (unsigned long)__atomic_load_n(&terminal_stats.last_ws_queue_message_limit,
                                          __ATOMIC_RELAXED),
           (unsigned long)__atomic_load_n(&terminal_stats.last_ws_queue_bytes,
                                          __ATOMIC_RELAXED),
           (unsigned long)__atomic_load_n(&terminal_stats.last_ws_queue_byte_limit,
                                          __ATOMIC_RELAXED),
           (unsigned long)__atomic_load_n(&terminal_stats.last_ws_queue_peak_bytes,
                                          __ATOMIC_RELAXED),
           (unsigned long)__atomic_load_n(&terminal_stats.last_ws_queue_byte_limit,
                                          __ATOMIC_RELAXED));
    z80_terminal_browser_disconnect();
    reset_session();
  }
  if (pending_connected.exchange(false, std::memory_order_acq_rel) &&
      active_connection.load(std::memory_order_acquire) >= 0) {
    reset_session();
    z80_terminal_browser_connect();
  }
}

bool ensure_server() {
  if (server_started)
    return true;
  if (!time_reached(server_retry_deadline))
    return false;
  if (server == nullptr) {
    server = new (std::nothrow) WebSocketServer(SERVER_CONNECTIONS);
    if (server == nullptr) {
      printf("[network] FAIL: server allocation; retry in 5 seconds.\n");
      server_retry_deadline = make_timeout_time_ms(SERVER_RETRY_MS);
      return false;
    }
    server->setConnectCallback(on_connect);
    server->setCloseCallback(on_close);
    server->setCloseDetailsCallback(on_close_details);
    server->setMessageCallback(on_message);
    server->setPongCallback(on_pong);
    server->setTcpNoDelay(true);
    // ACK/PONG control messages are tiny but can arrive in a burst within one
    // CYW43 poll. Give the queue room to absorb that burst, then drain more of
    // it on each application poll; the byte cap still bounds payload storage.
    if (!server->setReceiveLimits({HEADER_BYTES + INPUT_BYTES, 1024, 64, 32})) {
      printf("[network] FAIL: terminal receive limits; retry in 5 seconds.\n");
      delete server;
      server = nullptr;
      server_retry_deadline = make_timeout_time_ms(SERVER_RETRY_MS);
      return false;
    }
  }
  server_started = server->startListening(SERVER_PORT);
  if (!server_started) {
    printf("[network] FAIL: HTTP/WebSocket listen; retry in 5 seconds.\n");
    server_retry_deadline = make_timeout_time_ms(SERVER_RETRY_MS);
  }
  return server_started;
}

void poll_output() {
  int32_t connection = active_connection.load(std::memory_order_acquire);
  if (connection < 0)
    return;
  if (output_count && time_reached(output_frames[output_head].deadline)) {
    increment_stat(terminal_stats.ack_timeouts);
    printf("[network] Terminal client timed out; restoring USB.\n");
    disconnect_client(Z80_WEB_TERMINAL_DISCONNECT_OUTPUT_ACK_TIMEOUT);
    return;
  }
  if (awaiting_pong && time_reached(pong_deadline)) {
    awaiting_pong = false;
    pong_deadline = nil_time;
    if (activity_since_ping) {
      missed_pongs = 0;
    } else {
      increment_stat(terminal_stats.pong_timeouts);
      ++missed_pongs;
      if (missed_pongs > MAX_MISSED_PONGS) {
        printf("[network] Terminal client missed too many PONGs; restoring USB.\n");
        disconnect_client(Z80_WEB_TERMINAL_DISCONNECT_PONG_TIMEOUT);
        return;
      }
    }
    activity_since_ping = false;
    // Keep the 30-second send cadence; enqueue backpressure is retried on the
    // normal short retry cadence.
  }
  if (protocol_ready && !awaiting_pong && time_reached(ping_retry)) {
    write_sequence(ping_payload, ++ping_sequence);
    if (server->sendPing((uint32_t)connection, ping_payload,
                         sizeof(ping_payload))) {
      awaiting_pong = true;
      activity_since_ping = false;
      // A queued ping is outstanding until its matching PONG or the client
      // timeout. Do not retransmit it every poll; retry only failed enqueues.
      ping_retry = make_timeout_time_ms(HEARTBEAT_MS);
      pong_deadline = make_timeout_time_ms(PONG_TIMEOUT_MS);
    } else {
      ping_retry = make_timeout_time_ms(FRAME_RETRY_MS);
    }
  }
  if (!protocol_ready) {
    if (time_reached(hello_retry)) {
      send_control(HELLO, PROTOCOL_VERSION);
      hello_retry = make_timeout_time_ms(FRAME_RETRY_MS);
    }
    return;
  }
  bool output_changed = false;
  while (output_count < OUTPUT_WINDOW) {
    OutputFrame &frame = output_frames[(output_head + output_count) % OUTPUT_WINDOW];
    // ACKs advance head and reduce count together, preserving this staging slot.
    size_t supplied = z80_terminal_supply(
        frame.data + HEADER_BYTES + staged_output_length,
        FRAME_BYTES - staged_output_length);
    staged_output_length += supplied;
    output_changed |= supplied != 0;
    if (!staged_output_length)
      break;
    if (staged_output_length < FRAME_BYTES && !time_reached(output_batch_deadline))
      break;
    frame.data[0] = OUTPUT;
    write_sequence(frame.data + 1, output_sequence++);
    frame.length = HEADER_BYTES + staged_output_length;
    frame.retry = nil_time;
    frame.deadline = make_timeout_time_ms(OUTPUT_ACK_TIMEOUT_MS);
    frame.sent = false;
    retained_output_bytes += staged_output_length;
    ++output_count;
    output_changed = true;
    staged_output_length = 0;
    output_batch_deadline = make_timeout_time_us(OUTPUT_COALESCE_US);
  }
  if (output_changed)
    publish_buffer_usage();
  bool queued = false;
  for (size_t i = 0; i < output_count; ++i) {
    OutputFrame &frame = output_frames[(output_head + i) % OUTPUT_WINDOW];
    if (time_reached(frame.retry)) {
      auto result = server->enqueueMessage((uint32_t)connection, frame.data, frame.length);
      if (result == WebSocketServer::SendResult::would_block)
        break;
      if (result != WebSocketServer::SendResult::queued) {
        printf("[network] FAIL: terminal output enqueue (%u); restoring USB.\n",
               (unsigned)result);
        disconnect_client(Z80_WEB_TERMINAL_DISCONNECT_OUTPUT_SEND_ERROR);
        return;
      }
      queued = true;
      if (frame.sent)
        increment_stat(terminal_stats.retransmits);
      frame.sent = true;
      frame.retry = make_timeout_time_ms(FRAME_RETRY_MS);
    }
    if (!frame.sent)
      break;
  }
  if (queued && !server->flush((uint32_t)connection))
    increment_stat(terminal_stats.flush_failures);
}
}  // namespace

extern "C" z80_web_terminal_stats_t z80_web_terminal_get_stats(void) {
  z80_web_terminal_stats_t stats = {};
  stats.retransmits =
      __atomic_load_n(&terminal_stats.retransmits, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
  stats.flush_failures =
      __atomic_load_n(&terminal_stats.flush_failures, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
  stats.ack_timeouts =
      __atomic_load_n(&terminal_stats.ack_timeouts, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
  stats.pong_timeouts =
      __atomic_load_n(&terminal_stats.pong_timeouts, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
  stats.window_frames =
      __atomic_load_n(&terminal_stats.window_frames, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
  stats.window_frames_peak =
      __atomic_load_n(&terminal_stats.window_frames_peak, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
  stats.retained_bytes =
      __atomic_load_n(&terminal_stats.retained_bytes, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
  stats.retained_bytes_peak =
      __atomic_load_n(&terminal_stats.retained_bytes_peak, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
  stats.staged_bytes =
      __atomic_load_n(&terminal_stats.staged_bytes, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
  stats.last_disconnect_reason =
      __atomic_load_n(&terminal_stats.last_disconnect_reason, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
  stats.last_ws_close_reason =
      __atomic_load_n(&terminal_stats.last_ws_close_reason, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
  stats.last_ws_transport_error =
      __atomic_load_n(&terminal_stats.last_ws_transport_error, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
  stats.last_ws_queue_messages =
      __atomic_load_n(&terminal_stats.last_ws_queue_messages, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
  stats.last_ws_queue_bytes =
      __atomic_load_n(&terminal_stats.last_ws_queue_bytes, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
  stats.last_ws_queue_peak_messages =
      __atomic_load_n(&terminal_stats.last_ws_queue_peak_messages,
                      __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
  stats.last_ws_queue_peak_bytes =
      __atomic_load_n(&terminal_stats.last_ws_queue_peak_bytes, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
  stats.last_ws_queue_message_limit =
      __atomic_load_n(&terminal_stats.last_ws_queue_message_limit,
                      __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
  stats.last_ws_queue_byte_limit =
      __atomic_load_n(&terminal_stats.last_ws_queue_byte_limit, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
  stats.rx_queue_messages =
      __atomic_load_n(&terminal_stats.rx_queue_messages, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
  stats.rx_queue_bytes =
      __atomic_load_n(&terminal_stats.rx_queue_bytes, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
  stats.rx_queue_peak_messages =
      __atomic_load_n(&terminal_stats.rx_queue_peak_messages, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
  stats.rx_queue_peak_bytes =
      __atomic_load_n(&terminal_stats.rx_queue_peak_bytes, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
  stats.rx_queue_message_limit =
      __atomic_load_n(&terminal_stats.rx_queue_message_limit, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
  stats.rx_queue_byte_limit =
      __atomic_load_n(&terminal_stats.rx_queue_byte_limit, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);

  int32_t connection = active_connection.load(std::memory_order_acquire);
  if (server != nullptr && connection >= 0) {
    WebSocketServer::ReceiveQueueStats queue;
    if (server->getReceiveQueueStats((uint32_t)connection, queue)) {
      stats.rx_queue_active = 1;
      stats.rx_queue_messages = (uint32_t)queue.queuedMessages;
      stats.rx_queue_bytes = (uint32_t)queue.queuedBytes;
      stats.rx_queue_peak_messages = (uint32_t)queue.peakQueuedMessages;
      stats.rx_queue_peak_bytes = (uint32_t)queue.peakQueuedBytes;
      stats.rx_queue_message_limit = (uint32_t)queue.messageLimit;
      stats.rx_queue_byte_limit = (uint32_t)queue.byteLimit;
      __atomic_store_n(&terminal_stats.rx_queue_messages,
                       stats.rx_queue_messages, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
      __atomic_store_n(&terminal_stats.rx_queue_bytes,
                       stats.rx_queue_bytes, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
      __atomic_store_n(&terminal_stats.rx_queue_peak_messages,
                       stats.rx_queue_peak_messages, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
      __atomic_store_n(&terminal_stats.rx_queue_peak_bytes,
                       stats.rx_queue_peak_bytes, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
      __atomic_store_n(&terminal_stats.rx_queue_message_limit,
                       stats.rx_queue_message_limit, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
      __atomic_store_n(&terminal_stats.rx_queue_byte_limit,
                       stats.rx_queue_byte_limit, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
    }
  }
  return stats;
}

extern "C" void z80_web_terminal_poll(bool online, uint32_t generation) {
  check_reboot_deadline();
  if (!online && !network_online && generation == session_network_generation)
    return;
  if (!online && server == nullptr) {
    session_network_generation = generation;
    return;
  }
  cyw43_arch_lwip_begin();
  if (!online || generation != session_network_generation) {
    disconnect_client(Z80_WEB_TERMINAL_DISCONNECT_NETWORK_LOST);
    session_network_generation = generation;
  }
  network_online = online;
  if (online && ensure_server()) {
    process_events();
    server->popMessages();
    process_events();
    accept_pending_input();
    retry_input_ack();
    report_reboot_status();
    poll_output();
  } else if (server != nullptr) {
    server->popMessages();
    process_events();
  }
  cyw43_arch_lwip_end();
}

extern "C" z80_web_reboot_status_t z80_web_terminal_reboot_status(void) {
  return (z80_web_reboot_status_t)reboot_status.load(std::memory_order_acquire);
}

extern "C" bool z80_web_terminal_begin_reboot(void) {
  uint32_t expected = Z80_WEB_REBOOT_REQUESTED;
  return reboot_status.compare_exchange_strong(expected, Z80_WEB_REBOOT_FLUSHING,
                                                std::memory_order_acq_rel);
}

extern "C" void z80_web_terminal_set_reboot_status(z80_web_reboot_status_t status) {
  if (status == Z80_WEB_REBOOT_CPM_READY) {
    uint32_t expected = Z80_WEB_REBOOT_IDLE;
    reboot_status.compare_exchange_strong(expected, status, std::memory_order_acq_rel);
  } else {
    uint32_t previous = reboot_status.load(std::memory_order_acquire);
    // Timeout is terminal for this boot. A late supervisor must not overwrite
    // it with progress, or allow a browser retry to resurrect a cancelled stop.
    while (previous != Z80_WEB_REBOOT_TIMEOUT &&
           !reboot_status.compare_exchange_weak(previous, status,
                                                std::memory_order_acq_rel)) {}
  }
}

#include "z80sbc/pins.h"
#include "z80sbc/supervisor.h"

static const uint BUFFER_INPUT_PINS[] = {PIN_CLK, PIN_BUSREQ_N, PIN_BOOT_READ_DISABLE};
static const uint BUFFER_OUTPUT_CONTACTS[] = {18, 16, 14};
static const uint BUFFER_INPUT_CONTACTS[] = {2, 4, 6};
static int held_step = -1;

static void restore_test_outputs(void) {
  z80_clock_stop();
  z80_safe_startup();
  held_step = -1;
}

static void step_buffer_output(void) {
  int next_step = held_step + 1;
  restore_test_outputs();
  if (next_step >= 6) {
    printf("DONE: safe levels restored\n");
    return;
  }
  held_step = next_step;
  unsigned index = (unsigned)held_step / 2;
  bool high = held_step % 2 != 0;
  gpio_put(BUFFER_INPUT_PINS[index], high);
  printf("GP%u -> AHCT244 input %u -> output %u: HELD %s; verification=unmeasured\n",
         BUFFER_INPUT_PINS[index], BUFFER_INPUT_CONTACTS[index],
         BUFFER_OUTPUT_CONTACTS[index], high ? "HIGH" : "LOW");
}

int main(void) {
  restore_test_outputs();
  stdio_init_all();
  printf("\nStage 2: AHCT244 clock and boot-read inhibit; CPU/SRAM absent\n");
  printf("d=held LOW/HIGH steps, 1=1kHz, 2=100kHz, 3=1MHz, x=safe restore\n");
  while (true) {
    int command = getchar_timeout_us(0);
    if (command == 'd') {
      step_buffer_output();
    } else if (command >= '1' && command <= '3') {
      restore_test_outputs();
      uint32_t hz = command == '1' ? 1000 : command == '2' ? 100000 : 1000000;
      printf(z80_clock_set_hz(hz) ? "clock_actual=%lu verification=unmeasured\n"
                                : "FAIL: clock configuration %lu\n",
             (unsigned long)z80_clock_get_hz());
    } else if (command == 'x') {
      restore_test_outputs();
    }
    tight_loop_contents();
  }
}
Shared clock generation - src/common/clock.c 
#include "z80sbc/clock.h"

#include "hardware/clocks.h"
#include "hardware/pwm.h"
#include "pico/stdlib.h"
#include "z80sbc/pins.h"

static uint32_t actual_clock_hz;

void __not_in_flash_func(z80_clock_prepare_stepping)(void) {
  z80_clock_stop();
  gpio_put(PIN_CLK, 0);
  gpio_set_dir(PIN_CLK, GPIO_OUT);
  if (gpio_get_function(PIN_CLK) != GPIO_FUNC_SIO) {
    // Extend a frozen PWM HIGH before the mux can create a falling edge.
    busy_wait_us_32(1);
    gpio_set_function(PIN_CLK, GPIO_FUNC_SIO);
  }
}

bool z80_clock_set_hz(uint32_t hz) {
  if (hz < Z80_CLOCK_MIN_HZ || hz > Z80_CLOCK_MAX_HZ)
    return false;

  uint slice_num = pwm_gpio_to_slice_num(PIN_CLK);
  uint channel = pwm_gpio_to_channel(PIN_CLK);
  uint32_t sys_clk = clock_get_hz(clk_sys);
  uint32_t best_divider = 0;
  uint32_t best_count = 0;

  for (uint32_t divider = 1; divider <= 255; ++divider) {
    uint64_t denominator = (uint64_t)hz * divider;
    uint64_t count = ((uint64_t)sys_clk + denominator - 1u) / denominator;
    count = (count + 1u) & ~UINT64_C(1);
    if (count < 2)
      count = 2;
    if (count > 65536)
      continue;
    uint64_t product = (uint64_t)divider * count;
    uint64_t best_product = (uint64_t)best_divider * best_count;
    if (best_divider == 0 || product < best_product ||
        (product == best_product && count > best_count)) {
      best_divider = divider;
      best_count = (uint32_t)count;
    }
  }
  if (best_divider == 0)
    return false;

  z80_clock_prepare_stepping();
  busy_wait_us_32(1);
  pwm_set_clkdiv_int_frac4(slice_num, (uint8_t)best_divider, 0);
  pwm_set_wrap(slice_num, (uint16_t)(best_count - 1u));
  pwm_set_chan_level(slice_num, channel, (uint16_t)(best_count / 2u));
  pwm_set_counter(slice_num, 0);
  gpio_set_function(PIN_CLK, GPIO_FUNC_PWM);
  pwm_set_enabled(slice_num, true);
  uint64_t product = (uint64_t)best_divider * best_count;
  actual_clock_hz = (uint32_t)(((uint64_t)sys_clk + product / 2u) / product);
  return true;
}

uint32_t z80_clock_get_hz(void) {
  return actual_clock_hz;
}

void __not_in_flash_func(z80_clock_stop)(void) {
  pwm_set_enabled(pwm_gpio_to_slice_num(PIN_CLK), false);
}

void __not_in_flash_func(z80_clock_resume)(void) {
  pwm_set_counter(pwm_gpio_to_slice_num(PIN_CLK), 0);
  gpio_set_function(PIN_CLK, GPIO_FUNC_PWM);
  pwm_set_enabled(pwm_gpio_to_slice_num(PIN_CLK), true);
}

void z80_clock_one_cycle(uint32_t half_period_us) {
  z80_clock_prepare_stepping();
  z80_clock_step_prepared(half_period_us);
}

void __not_in_flash_func(z80_clock_step_prepared)(uint32_t half_period_us) {
  busy_wait_us_32(half_period_us);
  gpio_put(PIN_CLK, 1);
  busy_wait_us_32(half_period_us);
  gpio_put(PIN_CLK, 0);
  // Let CPU controls, translators and input synchronizers settle before return.
  busy_wait_us_32(1);
}

void z80_reset_with_clock_cycles(unsigned int cycles,
                                 uint32_t half_period_us) {
  gpio_put(PIN_RESET_N, 0);
  for (unsigned int cycle = 0; cycle < cycles; ++cycle)
    z80_clock_one_cycle(half_period_us);
  z80_clock_stop();
}

docs.title: Exception: Reset-Held Multimeter Guide for a Partially Populated Board
docs.text:
If the Z80 and SRAM are already fitted, together with Pico 2 W, U3 SN74HCT32N and U4 SN74AHCT244N, use the separate z80_reset_meter application for static measurements. U7 SN74LVC244AN, U9 SN74AHCT245N and U10 SN74LVC245AN may be absent. This is a troubleshooting exception, not permission to skip the normal population order or a Phase 4/6 pass. Do not use the ordinary Phase 2 output walk or the active address diagnostic with this partial population.

The guide never releases reset, drives the data bus, reads missing monitor buffers, or starts a free-running clock. It holds each clock HIGH and LOW on separate commands so a multimeter can settle. Six complete reset clocks are generated only as you explicitly advance through twelve held levels. The SRAM output inhibit remains asserted throughout.

docs.title: Build and open the console
docs.text:
From the repository root, using the firmware toolchain:

cmake --build build --target z80_reset_meter

UF2: build/src/stage02_buffers_clock/z80_reset_meter.uf2. The maintained application prints the full procedure, pin numbers, expected readings and next command in the USB serial console. Select the Pico USB serial port, 115200 baud (USB CDC does not use this rate for signal timing). The guide waits for the console connection before printing. Reconnecting restores safe levels and starts the guide again; a disconnected console does not leave CLK HIGH.

Before powering or flashing, verify orientations, common GND, bypasses, startup pulls, and absence of any raw 5 V connection to Pico GPIOs. All installed 5 V ICs must be powered. Apply external 5 V before USB; disconnect USB before external 5 V. Do not program this populated board with USB alone. If BOOTSEL flashing is needed, hold BOOTSEL while connecting USB after external 5 V is present. Do not change wiring or insert/remove ICs with either supply connected.

docs.title: Meter and keypress procedure
docs.text:
Use DC volts, black lead in COM and red lead in V, not the current socket. Connect black to common circuit GND. Measure named pins with the red probe, using insulated tips to avoid bridging adjacent contacts. Power off before moving clips. IC pins are numbered from the package notch/dot, not by breadboard row; U4 faces notch-down in the documented layout.

Type one command letter, then Enter. Do not paste command sequences or hold a key. An empty Enter does nothing; CR/LF/CRLF are supported.

Command Action n + Enter Acknowledge the current measurements and advance one step r + Enter Repeat current instructions without changing the held level h + Enter Show help and the current measurement instructions x Immediately stop without waiting for Enter; restore CLK LOW, RESET# LOW and read inhibit HIGH b + Enter Restart at preparation, with safe levels restored

On any unexpected voltage, press x, record the actual reading, and disconnect USB then external power before investigating. Do not advance. After x, Enter clears the discarded input line; then b + Enter restarts.

Console step Measure / expected outcome 1: preparation Confirm the hardware and meter safety instructions; CLK and RESET# held LOW 2: power U1.11, U2.32/U2.30, U3.14 and U4.20: nominal 5 V, bench target 4.75-5.25 V; Pico header 36: nominal 3.3 V, target 3.2-3.4 V; listed ground/enable/A16 pins near 0 V 3: safe outputs RESET# and CLK LOW; BUSREQ# inactive HIGH; inhibit HIGH; both data enables off; SRAM OE# HIGH. Follow every Pico/input/output endpoint printed in the console 4-15: six reset clocks Alternate one held HIGH and one held LOW per n + Enter; measure GP2/header 4 and U4.2 at approximately 3.3/0 V, and U4.18/Z80.6 at approximately 5/0 V. RESET# stays LOW and SRAM OE# stays HIGH 16: reset controls MREQ#/WR#/RD# inactive HIGH; buffered SRAM CE#/WE# and read-control outputs near 5 V 17: static HCT32 SRAM OE#, WAIT# and upward-path OE# HIGH at the listed endpoints; inhibit HIGH and IO_RELEASE LOW 18: address pulls All sixteen SRAM address pins near 5 V through the existing pulls; A16 LOW. Exact pins are printed 19: complete CLK LOW, reset asserted, no additional clocks. Save actual voltage readings; there is no automatic hardware PASS

Typical LOW target is at most 0.3 V. Pico HIGH is near 3.3 V; buffered 5 V HIGH should be within 0.5 V of its measured rail under this light load. Raw CPU HIGH is TTL and may be below 5 V (expect at least 2.4 V). These are conservative troubleshooting indications, not timing or full datasheet qualification.

The address check sees pull-ups on a floated bus, not CPU address drive. The floating 5 V data bus has no useful expected byte. This procedure cannot prove instruction execution, SRAM contents, address uniqueness, full OR-gate truth tables, clock edge quality or pulse timing. It does not replace unpowered continuity checks, the missing buffers, or Phase 6 instrument qualification.

docs.title: Optional Active Address Diagnostic
docs.text:
For all ICs installed and console control of each loader clock, use the Phase 6 console-stepped miniature loader. It writes the three specified test bytes, clears the Z80 accumulator before each read-back, and prints expected versus monitored bus behavior. It is separate from the reset-held partial-population guide above.

The same firmware now accepts f + Enter for the automatic full 64 KiB test: fill/read the sequential low-byte pattern, then fill/read the high-byte pattern, with one concise address/value/expected/SUCCESS-or-FAIL line per verified address. x aborts; all ICs and Phase 6 wiring are required.

Only after Phase 6 hardware is fitted and loader timing is qualified, build z80_stage04_address_bus; UF2 lives in build/src/stage04_address_bus/. Maintained application. a injects writes/readback at walking-one addresses; x holds reset and isolates. This is destructive RAM testing, not a held DC address generator.

Use separate analyzer captures of the complete address bus and write controls to confirm addresses actually appear during CPU writes. A successful byte readback alone cannot prove absence of all address aliases; the full-memory tests in Phase 6 are required.

docs.title: Pass Gate
docs.text:
• Sixteen distinct, correctly mapped address nets.
  • No shorts.
  • Valid monitor taps.

No active-load claim is made until Phase 6.

docs.text:
The complete application below is included from the repository at documentation build time, not copied into this page. Its active diagnostic remains deferred until Phase 6.

Phase 4 application - src/stage04_address_bus/main.c 
#include <stdio.h>
#include "pico/stdlib.h"
#include "z80sbc/cpu.h"
#include "z80sbc/sram.h"
#include "z80sbc/supervisor.h"
int main(void) {
  z80_safe_startup();
  stdio_init_all();
  printf("\nStage 4: CPU-driven address bus; Z80 and SRAM fitted\n");
  printf("a=walking addresses and readback, x=fail closed\n");
  while (true) {
    int command = getchar_timeout_us(0);
    if (command == 'a') {
      bool ok = z80_cpu_prepare_loader();
      for (unsigned bit = 0; ok && bit < 16; ++bit) {
        uint16_t address = (uint16_t)(1u << bit);
        uint8_t actual;
        ok = z80_sram_write_byte(address, (uint8_t)bit) &&
             z80_sram_read_byte(address, &actual) && actual == bit;
        printf("address=%04x verification=%s\n", address, ok ? "readback" : "FAIL");
        sleep_ms(250);
      }
      z80_cpu_fail_closed();
    } else if (command == 'x') z80_cpu_fail_closed();
    tight_loop_contents();
  }
}

docs.text:
Verify existing Phase 0/1/2 connections rather than adding duplicate wires or capacitors. Supply, ground and DIR links are direct wires, not resistors.

Done Pin / component Required connection U9 pin 20, VCC +5 V U9 pin 10, GND Common GND U9 pin 1, DIR +5 V: A to B U10 pin 20, VCC Pico-derived +3.3 V, not +5 V U10 pin 10, GND Common GND U10 pin 1, DIR Common GND: B to A U9 pin 19, OE# U3 HCT32 output pin 8; U3 input pin 9 receives Z80 RD# pin 21 and input pin 10 receives Pico pin 9 (GP6) U10 pin 19, OE# Pico pin 10 (GP7) C6/C7, 100 nF each C6 near U9 pin 20 across +5 V/GND; C7 near U10 pin 20 across +3.3 V/GND Installation Confirm no raw 5 V bus reaches Pico pins; verify rails, continuity, adjacent-pin isolation and pin-1 orientation before fitting U9/U10 with power and USB disconnected

Once fitted, apply external +5 V before USB and disconnect USB before removing +5 V. U9 lacks data-port power-off isolation; disabling OE does not make USB-only operation safe. Never enable both data paths at once.

docs.title: Firmware and Tests
docs.text:
Build z80_stage05_data_bus; UF2 lives in build/src/stage05_data_bus/. Maintained application.

For upward d patterns, temporarily pull raw RD# LOW through 1 kOhm with CPU absent; otherwise the HCT32 correctly keeps U9 disabled. Keep SRAM absent and boot inhibit HIGH.

Scope 00/FF/55/AA and walking-bit patterns on all eight bus lines. Verify U10 remains disabled throughout upward drive.

Remove the temporary RD pull. For i, apply weak external test pulls to D0-D7 and sample the downward path; U9 must remain disabled.

For e, reinstall the 1 kOhm raw RD# pull-down at the empty Z80 socket pin 21, keeping CPU/SRAM absent and boot inhibit HIGH. Fit external 0xAA test pulls: D1/D3/D5/D7 each through 10 kOhm to +5 V, and D0/D2/D4/D6 each through 10 kOhm to GND. Do not attach another push-pull bus driver. Disconnect USB and external power before changing any test pull, then restore external +5 V before USB.

e repeats 1000 drive/isolate/receive cycles. Capture U9 OE# pin 19 and U10 OE# pin 19: require each to go LOW in its respective phase, an interval with both HIGH between phases, and no overlapping LOW enables. Without the RD# pull-down, U9 stays disabled and the test can report PASS just by reading the external 0xAA pulls. Even with the correct fixture, byte readback alone does not prove upward drive or exclusion; retain the upward d captures and the actual-OE captures as separate pass evidence.

x isolates both paths. The software result does not measure voltage.

docs.title: Pass Gate
docs.text:
• Correct 5 V upward and 3.3 V downward levels.
  • Stable disabled paths and no simultaneous OE assertion.
  • No excessive current.
  • Remove every temporary test pull before fitting CPU/SRAM in Phase 6.

docs.title: Maintained Source
docs.text:
These complete files are included from the repository at documentation build time, not copied into this page. The shared bus module also implements the four-bit port sampling used in Phase 3.

Phase 5 application - src/stage05_data_bus/main.c 
#include <stdio.h>

#include "pico/stdlib.h"
#include "z80sbc/bus.h"
#include "z80sbc/supervisor.h"

static void output_data_patterns(void) {
  static const uint8_t patterns[] = {0x00, 0xFF, 0x55, 0xAA};
  for (size_t index = 0; index < sizeof(patterns); ++index) {
    z80_data_bus_drive(patterns[index]);
    printf("data=%02x\n", patterns[index]);
    sleep_ms(250);
  }
  for (unsigned int bit = 0; bit < 8; ++bit) {
    z80_data_bus_drive((uint8_t)(1u << bit));
    sleep_ms(100);
    z80_data_bus_drive((uint8_t)~(1u << bit));
    sleep_ms(100);
  }
  z80_data_bus_isolate();
  printf("PASS: patterns complete; verify on analyzer\n");
}

static bool data_endurance_test(void) {
  const uint8_t expected = 0xAA;
  for (unsigned int cycle = 0; cycle < 1000; ++cycle) {
    z80_data_bus_drive(expected);
    z80_data_bus_isolate();
    z80_data_bus_prepare_input();
    uint8_t actual = z80_data_bus_sample();
    z80_data_bus_isolate();
    if (actual != expected) {
      printf("FAIL: data cycle %u expected=%02x actual=%02x\n",
             cycle, expected, actual);
      return false;
    }
  }
  return true;
}

int main(void) {
  z80_safe_startup();
  stdio_init_all();
  printf("\nStage 5: data transceivers; CPU/SRAM absent\n");
    printf("d=output patterns, i=sample data, e=1000 cycles with external "
      "AA test pulls, x=isolate\n");

  while (true) {
    int command = getchar_timeout_us(0);
    if (command == 'd') {
      output_data_patterns();
    } else if (command == 'i') {
      z80_data_bus_prepare_input();
      printf("data=%02x\n", z80_data_bus_sample());
      z80_data_bus_isolate();
    } else if (command == 'e') {
      printf(data_endurance_test() ? "PASS: 1000 data interlock cycles\n"
                                   : "FAIL: data endurance\n");
    } else if (command == 'x') {
      z80_isolate_buses();
    }
    tight_loop_contents();
  }
}
Shared data paths and port sampling - src/common/bus.c 
#include "z80sbc/bus.h"

#include "pico/stdlib.h"
#include "z80sbc/pins.h"

enum { DATA_MASK = 0xFFu << PIN_DATA_0 };
_Static_assert(PIN_DATA_7 == PIN_DATA_0 + 7, "data GPIOs must be contiguous");
_Static_assert(PIN_PORT_A1 == PIN_PORT_A0 + 1 &&
                   PIN_PORT_A2 == PIN_PORT_A0 + 2 &&
                   PIN_PORT_A4 == PIN_PORT_A0 + 3,
               "port GPIO snapshot mapping changed");

uint8_t __not_in_flash_func(z80_port_bus_sample)(void) {
  uint32_t pins = gpio_get_all() >> PIN_PORT_A0;
  return (uint8_t)((pins & 7u) | ((pins & 8u) << 1));
}

void __not_in_flash_func(z80_data_bus_isolate)(void) {
  gpio_set_mask((1u << PIN_DATA_UP_OE_N) | (1u << PIN_DATA_DOWN_OE_N));
}

void __not_in_flash_func(z80_data_bus_drive)(uint8_t value) {
  z80_data_bus_isolate();
  busy_wait_us_32(1);
  gpio_put_masked(DATA_MASK, (uint32_t)value << PIN_DATA_0);
  gpio_set_dir_masked(DATA_MASK, DATA_MASK);
  busy_wait_us_32(1);
  gpio_put(PIN_DATA_UP_OE_N, 0);
}

void __not_in_flash_func(z80_data_bus_prepare_input)(void) {
  z80_data_bus_isolate();
  gpio_set_dir_masked(DATA_MASK, 0);
  busy_wait_us_32(1);
  gpio_put(PIN_DATA_DOWN_OE_N, 0);
}

uint8_t __not_in_flash_func(z80_data_bus_sample)(void) {
  return (uint8_t)(gpio_get_all() >> PIN_DATA_0);
}

Clear checklist

Prerequisite: Complete the loader and RAM checks in Phase 6. Install: No additional chips; CPU was fitted in Phase 6.

This diagnostic retains the unique bus-grant and receiving-pin measurement checks formerly in the separate Phase 7. Phase 6's arithmetic and SRAM tests already provide much stronger execution coverage than this small loop, but they do not request/release the CPU bus or prove analogue reset/clock margins. There is no longer a separate Phase 7 page or firmware target; Phase 8-10 keep their existing numbers.

Do not flash this diagnostic during another running test. It is a separate, manual low-rate fixture, not a new mode in the arithmetic soak.

Build z80_stage06_bus_grant; UF2 lives in build/src/stage06_sram_dma/. Maintained application. The test image is NOP; NOP; JP 0000. It is injected, read back, then reset again before execution from SRAM.

Done Command Test l Load/verify for stepping; hold RESET afterward s Release reset on first step, clock one manual cycle with 50 ms minimum half-pulses 0/1/2/3 Reload and run at 10 Hz / 1 kHz / 100 kHz / 1 MHz r Reload/run 1 MHz q BUSREQ/BUSACK round-trip; no Pico memory drive z Reset/restart current run rate x Assert reset, disable paths, stop clock

Commands are single characters; Enter is not required. q requires a free-running mode, not manual stepping. A request or release timeout fails closed and clears the run state: start a fresh run before retrying. The diagnostic does not enable an I/O trap; its Z80 loop contains no port I/O. On a successful grant, the Pico never takes over the memory address/data bus.

Build from the repository root with the firmware toolchain:

cmake -S . -B build -G Ninja -DPICO_BOARD=pico2_w
cmake --build build --target z80_stage06_bus_grant

docs.title: Test Plan
docs.text:
Capture reset, first fetch at 0000, M1, CE/OE/WE and data. Both Pico data enables stay HIGH during SRAM execution and boot inhibit stays LOW.

Verify RESET# rises while CLK is stopped LOW, with at least 1 us before PWM starts. The first clock edge must meet the Z80 reset setup requirement. Verify normal fetches differ from the injected boot stream; observe the NOP/JP loop.

Measure the loaded clock at Z80 pin 6. Progress through slow rates before 1 MHz. q must float the CPU bus while BUSACK LOW without activating either Pico path; rearm I/O before releasing a grant in integrated firmware.

Test a missing BUSACK using a test-only isolated input fixture, not by shorting the CPU output. Timeout must not authorize memory access; release timeout must assert RESET and isolate. Power off before fault wiring changes.

docs.title: Pass Gate
docs.text:
• Verified reset-to-SRAM fetch.
  • Repeated cold loads.
  • Correct instruction loop.
  • Safe bus-grant timeout behavior.

Higher rates need the separate qualification plan.

docs.title: Maintained Source
docs.text:
These complete files are included from the repository at documentation build time, not copied into this page.

Phase 6 bus-grant diagnostic - src/stage06_sram_dma/bus_grant_test.c 
#include <stdio.h>

#include "pico/stdlib.h"
#include "z80sbc/clock.h"
#include "z80sbc/cpu.h"
#include "z80sbc/pins.h"
#include "z80sbc/supervisor.h"

static const uint8_t CPU_TEST_PROGRAM[] = {
  0x00,             /* NOP */
  0x00,             /* NOP */
  0xC3, 0x00, 0x00, /* JP 0000h */
};

static bool step_image_loaded;
static uint32_t running_clock_hz;

static void stop_test(void) {
  z80_cpu_fail_closed();
  step_image_loaded = false;
  running_clock_hz = 0;
}

static bool load_and_start(uint32_t clock_hz) {
  stop_test();
  if (!z80_cpu_load_and_verify(CPU_TEST_PROGRAM, sizeof(CPU_TEST_PROGRAM)))
    return false;
  if (!z80_cpu_release_reset_and_run(clock_hz))
    return false;
  running_clock_hz = clock_hz;
  return true;
}

static bool load_for_single_step(void) {
  stop_test();
  step_image_loaded = z80_cpu_load_and_verify(
      CPU_TEST_PROGRAM, sizeof(CPU_TEST_PROGRAM));
  running_clock_hz = 0;
  z80_reset_with_clock_cycles(6, 1);
  return step_image_loaded;
}

static bool single_step(void) {
  if (!step_image_loaded)
    return false;
  if (!gpio_get(PIN_RESET_N)) {
    gpio_put(PIN_BOOT_READ_DISABLE, 0);
    z80_isolate_buses();
    gpio_put(PIN_BUSREQ_N, 1);
    gpio_put(PIN_RESET_N, 1);
  }
  z80_clock_one_cycle(50000);
  return true;
}

static bool reset_running_cpu(void) {
  if (running_clock_hz == 0)
    return false;
  uint32_t clock_hz = running_clock_hz;
  stop_test();
  z80_reset_with_clock_cycles(3, 1);
  if (!z80_cpu_release_reset_and_run(clock_hz))
    return false;
  running_clock_hz = clock_hz;
  return true;
}

static bool bus_round_trip(void) {
  if (running_clock_hz == 0)
    return false;
  if (!z80_cpu_request_bus(500000) || !z80_cpu_release_bus(500000)) {
    stop_test();
    return false;
  }
  return true;
}

int main(void) {
  z80_safe_startup();
  stdio_init_all();
  printf("\nStage 6: CPU reset/fetch and bus-grant qualification\n");
  printf("l=load for stepping, s=single cycle (50ms minimum half-pulses), "
      "0=run 10Hz, 1=run 1kHz, 2=run 100kHz, 3/r=run 1MHz, "
      "q=BUSREQ round-trip, z=reset/restart, x=fail closed\n");

  while (true) {
    int command = getchar_timeout_us(0);
    if (command == 'l') {
      printf(load_for_single_step() ? "PASS: image loaded; RESET# held\n"
                                    : "FAIL: image load\n");
    } else if (command == 's') {
      printf(single_step() ? "step complete\n"
                           : "FAIL: use l before stepping\n");
    } else if (command == '0') {
      printf(load_and_start(10) ? "PASS: CPU running at 10Hz\n"
                                : "FAIL: load/start\n");
    } else if (command == '1') {
      printf(load_and_start(1000) ? "PASS: CPU running at 1kHz\n"
                                  : "FAIL: load/start\n");
    } else if (command == '2') {
      printf(load_and_start(100000) ? "PASS: CPU running at 100kHz\n"
                                    : "FAIL: load/start\n");
    } else if (command == '3' || command == 'r') {
      printf(load_and_start(1000000) ? "PASS: CPU running at 1MHz\n"
                                     : "FAIL: load/start\n");
    } else if (command == 'q') {
      printf(bus_round_trip() ? "PASS: bus round-trip\n"
                              : "FAIL: start a run mode first or grant failed; inspect state\n");
    } else if (command == 'z') {
      printf(reset_running_cpu() ? "PASS: reset and restart\n"
                                 : "FAIL: start a run mode first\n");
    } else if (command == 'x') {
      stop_test();
      printf("CPU held in reset\n");
    }
    tight_loop_contents();
  }
}
Shared CPU reset and bus grants - src/common/cpu.c 
#include "z80sbc/cpu.h"

#include "pico/stdlib.h"
#include "z80sbc/clock.h"
#include "z80sbc/pins.h"
#include "z80sbc/sram.h"
#include "z80sbc/supervisor.h"

void z80_cpu_fail_closed(void) {
  z80_isolate_buses();
  gpio_put(PIN_RESET_N, 0);
  gpio_put(PIN_BUSREQ_N, 1);
  gpio_put(PIN_BOOT_READ_DISABLE, 1);
  gpio_put(PIN_IO_RELEASE, 0);
  z80_clock_stop();
}

bool z80_cpu_prepare_loader(void) {
  z80_cpu_fail_closed();
  z80_reset_with_clock_cycles(3, 1);
  if (!gpio_get(PIN_BUSACK_N) || !gpio_get(PIN_IORQ_N) ||
      !gpio_get(PIN_RD_N) || !gpio_get(PIN_WR_N))
    return false;
  return z80_sram_prepare_loader();
}

bool z80_cpu_load_and_verify(const uint8_t *image, uint32_t length) {
  if (image == NULL || length == 0 || length > 65536u ||
      !z80_cpu_prepare_loader())
    return false;
  bool loaded = z80_sram_load(0, image, length) &&
                z80_sram_verify(0, image, length);
  if (!loaded)
    z80_cpu_fail_closed();
  return loaded;
}

bool z80_cpu_release_reset_and_run(uint32_t clock_hz) {
  if (clock_hz < Z80_CLOCK_MIN_HZ || clock_hz > Z80_CLOCK_MAX_HZ) {
    z80_cpu_fail_closed();
    return false;
  }
  z80_isolate_buses();
  z80_reset_with_clock_cycles(6, 1);
  gpio_put(PIN_BOOT_READ_DISABLE, 0);
  gpio_put(PIN_IO_RELEASE, 0);
  gpio_put(PIN_BUSREQ_N, 1);
  gpio_put(PIN_RESET_N, 1);
  busy_wait_us_32(1);
  if (!z80_clock_set_hz(clock_hz)) {
    z80_cpu_fail_closed();
    return false;
  }
  return true;
}

bool z80_cpu_request_bus(uint32_t timeout_us) {
  absolute_time_t deadline = make_timeout_time_us(timeout_us);
  z80_isolate_buses();
  gpio_put(PIN_BUSREQ_N, 0);
  while (gpio_get(PIN_BUSACK_N)) {
    if (time_reached(deadline)) {
      gpio_put(PIN_BUSREQ_N, 1);
      return false;
    }
    tight_loop_contents();
  }
  return true;
}

bool z80_cpu_release_bus(uint32_t timeout_us) {
  absolute_time_t deadline = make_timeout_time_us(timeout_us);
  z80_isolate_buses();
  gpio_put(PIN_BUSREQ_N, 1);
  while (!gpio_get(PIN_BUSACK_N)) {
    if (time_reached(deadline)) {
      z80_cpu_fail_closed();
      return false;
    }
    tight_loop_contents();
  }
  return true;
}

docs.title: Firmware and Loader Qualification
