docs.title: What This Phase Adds
docs.text:
Phase 6 owns comprehensive CPU/arithmetic/stack/SRAM tests. Its soak's result reports exercise OUT to port 06h only; an IN is treated as an error. Those results do not qualify the bidirectional I/O or terminal service.

This phase retains the existing z80_stage08_virtual_io firmware at nominal 1 MHz, adding:

  • IN replies: the Pico drives data to the Z80 during a trapped I/O read.
  • OUT/IN address decoding: selected raw ports and their masked aliases.
  • USB terminal round-trip: host input, status polling, Z80 IN, Z80 OUT and returned USB characters, with receive/transmit queue and drop counters.
  • Repeated boot/I/O integration: 100 software reset/load/verify/self-test cycles; these are not 100 physical cold power cycles.
  • Analogue timing and fault evidence: WAIT, stepped release, input data setup/hold, both actual data-buffer enables and invalid-control recovery.

The RAM/USB checker uses a single working byte at 0100h while exchanging terminal traffic. Its image is loaded and verified across 64 KiB before execution, but its runtime checker is not a full-memory sweep or a replacement for Phase 6's SRAM tests. Likewise, its one-hour command is an I/O/USB integration run, not another arithmetic/SRAM qualification. A Phase 6 pass at the scope-measured 20 MHz does not qualify IN or terminal operation at that frequency.

On boot this firmware starts the RAM/USB checker automatically. Deploy only after another running diagnostic has finished and its results are saved.

docs.title: Synchronous I/O Trap Handler (Phase 8)
docs.text:
Raw IORQ# immediately asserts WAIT through U3 while GP9 IO_RELEASE is LOW. The buffered falling edge interrupts core 0, which stops PWM, samples the four port bits, and requires exactly one of RD#/WR# LOW. OUT enables the downward path; IN preloads a reply and enables the upward path.

Only after the data path is ready does GP9 rise. Firmware completes the I/O cycle using slow single clocks, waits for IORQ and the active strobe to rise, disables both paths, waits at least 1 us for isolation, lowers GP9 to rearm WAIT, then restarts PWM. Each clock step includes at least 1 us of LOW settling after the falling edge before polling the buffered controls. PWM-to-SIO handover preloads the LOW latch and extends a frozen HIGH by at least 1 us before selecting SIO. This guard is not repeated on already-SIO steps; capture both stopped phases to rule out short pulses. A stuck strobe times out after 500 ms and causes fail-closed reset/watchdog recovery. U3 also gates upward OE with RD; no SPI or address-driver operation occurs.

Shared bus access uses one GPIO snapshot for port/data sampling and masked SIO writes for data preload and direction changes. Data GPIO pads are initialized at safe startup rather than on every OUT. All isolation, preload-before-drive and settling guards above remain in force.

docs.title: Register access and SRAM-resident hardware path
docs.text:
The trap prepares stopped-SIO clock mode once, then uses a pulse-only helper for each release clock. Each pulse retains its requested LOW and HIGH waits and the final 1 us LOW settling interval. General loader/reset callers still use the self-preparing single-cycle API; the prepared-step API is restricted to the core-0 bus owner, with no intervening clock ownership or mode change.

Each release check samples IORQ and the active RD/WR strobe together in one GPIO snapshot. Both must be HIGH before completion, even when they release on different clocks. Both data-buffer disable bits are set together using the SDK masked GPIO operation, without touching unrelated outputs. The SDK can use the RP2350 GPIO coprocessor; raw SIO-register replacements are not required.

The trap handler/release loop, clock stop/resume/preparation/prepared pulse, and shared data/port bus helpers use the SDK SRAM code-placement attribute. This removes instruction fetches from flash for those selected routines, not for the complete call chain: SDK timing/mux helpers, Phase 8 application callbacks and failure handling can still execute from flash. Phases 9/10 also place their terminal/disk callbacks and register handlers in SRAM; see the placement checks and limits. This is not permission to execute during flash programming; the existing BUSACK, IRQ and multicore flash-lockout contracts remain mandatory.

Native tests verify constant preparation work for one to three release clocks, independently releasing controls, both frozen PWM phases, unchanged settling intervals, data patterns and fail-closed faults. SDK symbol and disassembly checks verify SRAM addresses, the pulse-only body and one masked buffer-isolation operation. These establish work counts, placement and correctness, not measured throughput or proof that XIP-cache contention caused a slowdown. Hardware qualification still requires before/after trap-duration and I/O-throughput measurements, including concurrent network traffic.

Decode is address & 0x17: 00/01 terminal and 10-14 disk ports retain their contracts. A3/A5-A7 and high-byte aliases are intentional. A trap while BUSACK LOW is ignored and IRQ disabled until the grant-release path rearms it.

The Phase 8 diagnostic result port is 06, which survives the mask. The self-test still emits raw ports 00/01/55/AA/FF to exercise aliases: OUT checks the masked port and the full transmitted byte; IN expects (raw_port & 0x17) ^ 0xA5. Both successful completion and the RAM-checker's E1 error report use 06; FE would decode as 16, not as FE.

Application read/write hooks must not print, sleep, touch networking, wait for a queue, or initiate another bus operation. Pico queue operations use bounded spinlock critical sections, not lock-free access.

docs.title: USB Diagnostic Commands
docs.text:
Ordinary console bytes go to the Z80. Ctrl-] followed by one command byte selects framed supervisor diagnostics; configure the serial terminal to pass this escape through. Use Ctrl-] s for clock and fault-counter status, and the command list below for terminal, port and repeated-boot tests. Do not treat supervisor diagnostics as CP/M input.

Input Action in the existing firmware Ordinary bytes Queue terminal input; running checker reads with IN and echoes with OUT Ctrl-] s Print configured clock and boot/verify/RAM/trap/queue counters Ctrl-] r Reload/verify and restart the 1 MHz RAM/USB checker Ctrl-] p Run the selected-port OUT/IN self-test Ctrl-] b Run 100 reset/load/verify/port-test cycles Ctrl-] h Run the one-hour RAM/USB integration check Ctrl-] x Disable trapping, assert reset, isolate data paths and stop the clock Ctrl-] Ctrl-] Queue a literal 1Dh terminal byte

The built-in port test selects raw ports 00h/01h/55h/AAh/FFh; it does not exhaust every data byte or port alias. Record which patterns were actually tested. The running checker also emits A-Z heartbeat bytes, so distinguish those from echoed host input when inspecting the terminal.

docs.title: Test Plan
docs.text:
Use I/O ports and services as the allocation reference. Its extended services are implemented in Phases 9/10, not in this Phase 8 application, and are not required by these tests.

Capture IORQ, WAIT, CLK, RD/WR and both OEs. Confirm WAIT asserts before the CPU could complete the I/O cycle, and the stepped release isolates before the next memory fetch. Include both stopped clock phases described above.

Check IN replies and OUT bytes at every bit pattern, all supported ports, and intentional aliases.

Run sustained USB echo and repeated boot/verify/RAM tests; counters must not increase.

Use isolated test-only inputs to exercise neither/both strobes asserted, stuck IORQ/RD/WR, and BUSACK races. Do not short CPU-driven outputs. Faults must leave RESET LOW, both OEs HIGH, boot inhibit HIGH, and clock stopped before watchdog reboot.

Repeat after cold power cycles.

docs.title: Pass Gate
docs.text:
• Correct terminal bytes and aliases.
  • No RAM corruption.
  • No enable overlap.
  • Bounded WAIT release.
  • Zero unexpected control/timeout/readback failures.
  • Save analog and digital evidence before adding flash/network concurrency.

docs.title: Maintained Source
docs.text:
These complete files are included from the repository at documentation build time, not copied into this page.

Phase 8 application - src/stage08_virtual_io/main.c 
#include <stdio.h>
#include <string.h>

#include "pico/stdio_usb.h"
#include "pico/stdlib.h"
#include "pico/util/queue.h"
#include "z80sbc/bus.h"
#include "z80sbc/clock.h"
#include "z80sbc/cpu.h"
#include "z80sbc/io_trap.h"
#include "z80sbc/sram.h"
#include "z80sbc/supervisor.h"
#include "z80sbc/test_progress.h"

enum {
  TERMINAL_DATA_PORT = 0x00,
  TERMINAL_STATUS_PORT = 0x01,
  TEST_RESULT_PORT = 0x06,
  TERMINAL_RX_DEPTH = 128,
  TERMINAL_TX_DEPTH = 512,
  TERMINAL_STATUS_RX_READY = 1u << 0,
  TERMINAL_STATUS_TX_ROOM = 1u << 1,
  TERMINAL_STATUS_CONNECTED = 1u << 7,
  USB_COMMAND_ESCAPE = 0x1D,
  IO_MODE_RAM_CHECKER = 1,
  IO_MODE_SELF_TEST = 2,
  AUTOMATED_BOOT_CYCLES = 100,
};

_Static_assert((TEST_RESULT_PORT & Z80_PORT_ADDRESS_MASK) == TEST_RESULT_PORT,
               "test result port must survive the hardware address mask");

static const uint8_t RAM_CHECK_PROGRAM[] = {
  0x31, 0xFE, 0xFF, 0x21, 0x00, 0x01, 0x36, 0x00,
  0x1E, 0x00, 0x16, 0x41, 0x1C, 0x34, 0x7E, 0xBB,
  0xC2, 0x33, 0x00, 0x7A, 0xD3, 0x00, 0xDB, 0x01,
  0xE6, 0x01, 0x28, 0x04, 0xDB, 0x00, 0xD3, 0x00,
  0x14, 0x7A, 0xFE, 0x5B, 0x20, 0x02, 0x16, 0x41,
  0x01, 0xFF, 0xFF, 0x0B, 0x78, 0xB1, 0x20, 0xFB,
  0xC3, 0x0C, 0x00, 0x3E, 0xE1, 0xD3, TEST_RESULT_PORT, 0x76,
};

static const uint8_t SELF_TEST_PORTS[] = {0x00, 0x01, 0x55, 0xAA, 0xFF};

static queue_t terminal_rx_queue;
static queue_t terminal_tx_queue;
static uint8_t full_test_image[65536];
static uint8_t self_test_image[128];
static size_t self_test_image_length;
static uint32_t io_mode;
static uint32_t usb_connected;
static uint32_t usb_rx_drops;
static uint32_t usb_tx_drops;
static uint32_t boot_attempts;
static uint32_t dma_failures;
static uint32_t readback_failures;
static uint32_t ram_failures;
static uint32_t ram_heartbeats;
static z80_test_progress_t hour_progress;
static uint32_t self_test_write_index;
static uint32_t self_test_errors;
static uint32_t self_test_complete;
static bool self_test_pending;
static absolute_time_t self_test_deadline;
static bool boot_cycle_active;
static unsigned int boot_cycles_remaining;
static unsigned int boot_cycles_passed;
static bool hour_test_active;
static absolute_time_t hour_test_started;
static absolute_time_t hour_test_deadline;
static uint32_t hour_trap_timeout_baseline;
static uint32_t hour_control_error_baseline;
static bool usb_command_pending;
static bool usb_was_connected;

static void clear_queue(queue_t *queue) {
  uint8_t discard;
  while (queue_try_remove(queue, &discard)) {}
}

static void clear_terminal_queues(void) {
  clear_queue(&terminal_rx_queue);
  clear_queue(&terminal_tx_queue);
}

static void terminal_receive(uint8_t value) {
  if (!queue_try_add(&terminal_rx_queue, &value)) {
    uint8_t discard;
    if (queue_try_remove(&terminal_rx_queue, &discard))
      __atomic_fetch_add(&usb_rx_drops, 1, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
    if (!queue_try_add(&terminal_rx_queue, &value))
      __atomic_fetch_add(&usb_rx_drops, 1, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
  }
}

static uint8_t virtual_read(uint8_t port, void *context) {
  (void)context;
  if (__atomic_load_n(&io_mode, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE) == IO_MODE_SELF_TEST)
    return (uint8_t)(port ^ 0xA5u);
  if (port == TERMINAL_DATA_PORT) {
    uint8_t value = 0;
    queue_try_remove(&terminal_rx_queue, &value);
    return value;
  }
  if (port != TERMINAL_STATUS_PORT)
    return 0xFF;
  uint8_t status = 0;
  if (queue_get_level(&terminal_rx_queue) != 0)
    status |= TERMINAL_STATUS_RX_READY;
  if (queue_get_level(&terminal_tx_queue) < TERMINAL_TX_DEPTH)
    status |= TERMINAL_STATUS_TX_ROOM;
  if (__atomic_load_n(&usb_connected, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE))
    status |= TERMINAL_STATUS_CONNECTED;
  return status;
}

static void virtual_write(uint8_t port, uint8_t value, void *context) {
  (void)context;
  if (__atomic_load_n(&io_mode, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE) == IO_MODE_SELF_TEST) {
    if (port == TEST_RESULT_PORT) {
      bool passed = value == 0x5A &&
                    __atomic_load_n(&self_test_write_index,
                                    __ATOMIC_RELAXED) ==
                        sizeof(SELF_TEST_PORTS) &&
                    __atomic_load_n(&self_test_errors,
                                    __ATOMIC_RELAXED) == 0;
      if (!passed)
        __atomic_fetch_add(&self_test_errors, 1, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
      __atomic_store_n(&self_test_complete, 1, __ATOMIC_RELEASE);
      return;
    }
    uint32_t index = __atomic_load_n(&self_test_write_index,
                                     __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
    if (index >= sizeof(SELF_TEST_PORTS) ||
        port != (SELF_TEST_PORTS[index] & Z80_PORT_ADDRESS_MASK) ||
        value != SELF_TEST_PORTS[index]) {
      __atomic_fetch_add(&self_test_errors, 1, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
      return;
    }
    __atomic_store_n(&self_test_write_index, index + 1, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
    return;
  }
  if (port == TEST_RESULT_PORT && value == 0xE1) {
    __atomic_fetch_add(&ram_failures, 1, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
    return;
  }
  if (port == TERMINAL_DATA_PORT) {
    __atomic_fetch_add(&ram_heartbeats, 1, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
    if (!queue_try_add(&terminal_tx_queue, &value))
      __atomic_fetch_add(&usb_tx_drops, 1, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
  }
}

static bool load_and_start(const uint8_t *program, size_t length,
                           uint32_t mode) {
  for (uint32_t address = 0; address < sizeof(full_test_image); ++address)
    full_test_image[address] =
        (uint8_t)address ^ (uint8_t)(address >> 8);
  memcpy(full_test_image, program, length);
  z80_io_trap_disable();
  z80_cpu_fail_closed();
  __atomic_fetch_add(&boot_attempts, 1, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
  if (!z80_cpu_prepare_loader() ||
      !z80_sram_load(0, full_test_image, sizeof(full_test_image))) {
    __atomic_fetch_add(&dma_failures, 1, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
    return false;
  }
  if (!z80_sram_verify(0, full_test_image, sizeof(full_test_image))) {
    __atomic_fetch_add(&readback_failures, 1, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
    return false;
  }
  clear_terminal_queues();
  __atomic_store_n(&io_mode, mode, __ATOMIC_RELEASE);
  return z80_io_trap_enable(virtual_read, virtual_write, NULL) &&
         z80_cpu_release_reset_and_run(1000000);
}

static bool start_ram_checker(void) {
  return load_and_start(RAM_CHECK_PROGRAM, sizeof(RAM_CHECK_PROGRAM),
                        IO_MODE_RAM_CHECKER);
}

static void emit_self_test_byte(uint8_t value) {
  self_test_image[self_test_image_length++] = value;
}

static void build_self_test_image(void) {
  size_t failure_patches[sizeof(SELF_TEST_PORTS)];
  self_test_image_length = 0;
  for (size_t index = 0; index < sizeof(SELF_TEST_PORTS); ++index) {
    uint8_t port = SELF_TEST_PORTS[index];
    emit_self_test_byte(0x3E);
    emit_self_test_byte(port);
    emit_self_test_byte(0xD3);
    emit_self_test_byte(port);
  }
  for (size_t index = 0; index < sizeof(SELF_TEST_PORTS); ++index) {
    uint8_t port = SELF_TEST_PORTS[index];
    uint16_t address = (uint16_t)(0x0200u + index);
    emit_self_test_byte(0xDB);
    emit_self_test_byte(port);
    emit_self_test_byte(0x32);
    emit_self_test_byte((uint8_t)address);
    emit_self_test_byte((uint8_t)(address >> 8));
    emit_self_test_byte(0x3A);
    emit_self_test_byte((uint8_t)address);
    emit_self_test_byte((uint8_t)(address >> 8));
    emit_self_test_byte(0xFE);
    emit_self_test_byte((uint8_t)((port & Z80_PORT_ADDRESS_MASK) ^ 0xA5u));
    emit_self_test_byte(0xC2);
    failure_patches[index] = self_test_image_length;
    emit_self_test_byte(0x00);
    emit_self_test_byte(0x00);
  }
  emit_self_test_byte(0x3E);
  emit_self_test_byte(0x5A);
  emit_self_test_byte(0xD3);
  emit_self_test_byte(TEST_RESULT_PORT);
  emit_self_test_byte(0x76);
  uint16_t failure_address = (uint16_t)self_test_image_length;
  emit_self_test_byte(0x3E);
  emit_self_test_byte(0xE1);
  emit_self_test_byte(0xD3);
  emit_self_test_byte(TEST_RESULT_PORT);
  emit_self_test_byte(0x76);
  for (size_t index = 0; index < sizeof(SELF_TEST_PORTS); ++index) {
    self_test_image[failure_patches[index]] = (uint8_t)failure_address;
    self_test_image[failure_patches[index] + 1] =
        (uint8_t)(failure_address >> 8);
  }
}

static bool start_self_test(void) {
  __atomic_store_n(&self_test_write_index, 0, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
  __atomic_store_n(&self_test_errors, 0, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
  __atomic_store_n(&self_test_complete, 0, __ATOMIC_RELEASE);
  bool started = load_and_start(self_test_image, self_test_image_length,
                                IO_MODE_SELF_TEST);
  self_test_pending = started;
  if (started)
    self_test_deadline = make_timeout_time_ms(500);
  return started;
}

static void print_status(void) {
  int64_t elapsed_us = hour_test_active
                           ? absolute_time_diff_us(hour_test_started,
                                                   get_absolute_time())
                           : 0;
    printf("\n[diag] stage=8 clock_requested=1000000 clock_actual=%lu "
      "boots=%lu dma_fail=%lu verify_fail=%lu ram_fail=%lu "
         "trap_timeout=%lu control_error=%lu rx_drop=%lu tx_drop=%lu "
         "hour_seconds=%llu\n",
         (unsigned long)z80_clock_get_hz(),
         (unsigned long)__atomic_load_n(&boot_attempts, __ATOMIC_RELAXED),
         (unsigned long)__atomic_load_n(&dma_failures, __ATOMIC_RELAXED),
         (unsigned long)__atomic_load_n(&readback_failures, __ATOMIC_RELAXED),
         (unsigned long)__atomic_load_n(&ram_failures, __ATOMIC_RELAXED),
         (unsigned long)z80_io_trap_timeout_count(),
         (unsigned long)z80_io_trap_control_error_count(),
         (unsigned long)__atomic_load_n(&usb_rx_drops, __ATOMIC_RELAXED),
         (unsigned long)__atomic_load_n(&usb_tx_drops, __ATOMIC_RELAXED),
         (unsigned long long)(elapsed_us > 0 ? elapsed_us / 1000000 : 0));
}

static void process_command(uint8_t command) {
  if (command == USB_COMMAND_ESCAPE) {
    terminal_receive(command);
  } else if (command == 's') {
    print_status();
  } else if (command == 'r') {
    boot_cycle_active = false;
    hour_test_active = false;
    printf(start_ram_checker() ? "\n[diag] RAM/USB checker started\n"
                               : "\n[diag] FAIL: RAM/USB checker\n");
  } else if (command == 'p') {
    boot_cycle_active = false;
    hour_test_active = false;
    printf(start_self_test() ? "\n[diag] port self-test started\n"
                             : "\n[diag] FAIL: port self-test start\n");
  } else if (command == 'b') {
    hour_test_active = false;
    boot_cycle_active = true;
    boot_cycles_remaining = AUTOMATED_BOOT_CYCLES;
    boot_cycles_passed = 0;
    bool started = start_self_test();
    if (!started)
      boot_cycle_active = false;
    printf(started ? "\n[diag] 100 boot cycles started\n"
                   : "\n[diag] FAIL: boot-cycle start\n");
  } else if (command == 'h') {
    boot_cycle_active = false;
    __atomic_store_n(&ram_failures, 0, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
    hour_trap_timeout_baseline = z80_io_trap_timeout_count();
    hour_control_error_baseline = z80_io_trap_control_error_count();
    hour_test_active = start_ram_checker();
    if (hour_test_active) {
      hour_test_started = get_absolute_time();
      hour_test_deadline = make_timeout_time_ms(60u * 60u * 1000u);
      z80_test_progress_start(
          &hour_progress, __atomic_load_n(&ram_heartbeats, __ATOMIC_RELAXED));
    }
    printf(hour_test_active ? "\n[diag] one-hour RAM/USB test started\n"
                            : "\n[diag] FAIL: one-hour test start\n");
  } else if (command == 'x') {
    boot_cycle_active = false;
    hour_test_active = false;
    z80_io_trap_disable();
    z80_cpu_fail_closed();
    printf("\n[diag] CPU held in reset\n");
  }
}

static void service_usb(void) {
  bool connected = stdio_usb_connected();
  __atomic_store_n(&usb_connected, connected, __ATOMIC_RELEASE);
  if (usb_was_connected && !connected) {
    clear_terminal_queues();
    usb_command_pending = false;
  }
  usb_was_connected = connected;

  int input;
  while ((input = getchar_timeout_us(0)) >= 0) {
    uint8_t value = (uint8_t)input;
    if (usb_command_pending) {
      usb_command_pending = false;
      process_command(value);
    } else if (value == USB_COMMAND_ESCAPE) {
      usb_command_pending = true;
    } else if (__atomic_load_n(&io_mode, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE) ==
               IO_MODE_RAM_CHECKER) {
      terminal_receive(value);
    }
  }

  if (!connected)
    return;
  for (unsigned int sent = 0; sent < 32; ++sent) {
    uint8_t value;
    if (!queue_try_remove(&terminal_tx_queue, &value))
      break;
    putchar_raw(value);
  }
}

static void service_self_test(void) {
  if (!self_test_pending)
    return;
  bool complete = __atomic_load_n(&self_test_complete, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE);
  bool failed = __atomic_load_n(&self_test_errors, __ATOMIC_RELAXED) != 0;
  if (!complete && !failed && !time_reached(self_test_deadline))
    return;
  self_test_pending = false;
  if (!complete || failed) {
    boot_cycle_active = false;
    printf("\n[diag] FAIL: port self-test errors=%lu\n",
           (unsigned long)__atomic_load_n(&self_test_errors,
                                          __ATOMIC_RELAXED));
    return;
  }
  if (!boot_cycle_active) {
    printf("\n[diag] PASS: OUT/IN ports and SRAM stores\n");
    return;
  }
  ++boot_cycles_passed;
  if (--boot_cycles_remaining == 0) {
    boot_cycle_active = false;
    printf("\n[diag] PASS: %u reset-held boot/IO cycles\n",
           boot_cycles_passed);
    return;
  }
  if (!start_self_test()) {
    boot_cycle_active = false;
    printf("\n[diag] FAIL: boot cycle %u start\n", boot_cycles_passed + 1);
  }
}

static void service_hour_test(void) {
  if (!hour_test_active)
    return;
  if (!z80_test_progress_poll(
          &hour_progress, __atomic_load_n(&ram_heartbeats, __ATOMIC_RELAXED))) {
    hour_test_active = false;
    printf("\n[diag] FAIL: one-hour RAM/USB test: heartbeat timeout\n");
    return;
  }
  if (!time_reached(hour_test_deadline))
    return;
  hour_test_active = false;
  bool passed = hour_progress.observed &&
                __atomic_load_n(&ram_failures, __ATOMIC_RELAXED) == 0 &&
                z80_io_trap_timeout_count() == hour_trap_timeout_baseline &&
                z80_io_trap_control_error_count() ==
                    hour_control_error_baseline;
  printf(passed ? "\n[diag] PASS: one-hour RAM/USB test\n"
                : "\n[diag] FAIL: one-hour RAM/USB test\n");
}

int main(void) {
  z80_safe_startup();
  stdio_init_all();
  queue_init(&terminal_rx_queue, sizeof(uint8_t), TERMINAL_RX_DEPTH);
  queue_init(&terminal_tx_queue, sizeof(uint8_t), TERMINAL_TX_DEPTH);
  build_self_test_image();
  printf("\n[diag] Stage 8: virtual-ROM, USB CDC, and I/O trap\n");
  printf("[diag] normal bytes=terminal input; Ctrl-] then "
         "s=status r=restart p=port-test b=100-boots h=one-hour x=stop\n");
  printf(start_ram_checker() ? "[diag] PASS: RAM/USB checker at 1MHz\n"
                             : "[diag] FAIL: boot/trap initialization\n");

  while (true) {
    service_usb();
    service_self_test();
    service_hour_test();
    tight_loop_contents();
  }
}
Shared synchronous I/O trap - src/common/io_trap.c 
#include "z80sbc/io_trap.h"

#include "hardware/watchdog.h"
#include "pico/stdlib.h"
#include "z80sbc/bus.h"
#include "z80sbc/clock.h"
#include "z80sbc/cpu.h"
#include "z80sbc/pins.h"

enum { TRAP_RELEASE_TIMEOUT_US = 500000 };
static const uint32_t RESET_FAULT_MAGIC = 0x5A384954;

static z80_io_read_handler_t application_read;
static z80_io_write_handler_t application_write;
static void *application_context;
static uint32_t trap_timeouts;
static uint32_t control_errors;
static uint32_t inactive_irqs;

z80_io_trap_reset_fault_t z80_io_trap_take_reset_fault(void) {
  uint32_t magic = watchdog_hw->scratch[0];
  uint32_t reason = watchdog_hw->scratch[1];
  uint32_t gpio = watchdog_hw->scratch[2];
  uint32_t check = watchdog_hw->scratch[3];
  watchdog_hw->scratch[0] = 0;
  if (!watchdog_caused_reboot() || magic != RESET_FAULT_MAGIC ||
      check != (magic ^ reason ^ gpio) ||
      reason < Z80_IO_TRAP_RESET_RELEASE_TIMEOUT ||
      reason > Z80_IO_TRAP_RESET_INVALID_CONTROLS)
    return (z80_io_trap_reset_fault_t){0};
  return (z80_io_trap_reset_fault_t){
    .reason = (z80_io_trap_reset_reason_t)reason,
    .gpio = gpio,
  };
}

static _Noreturn void trap_fail_closed(z80_io_trap_reset_reason_t reason,
                                       uint32_t controls) {
  // Scratch 0-3 survive watchdog reset; the SDK reserves 4-7 for reboot.
  watchdog_hw->scratch[0] = 0;
  watchdog_hw->scratch[1] = reason;
  watchdog_hw->scratch[2] = controls;
  watchdog_hw->scratch[3] = RESET_FAULT_MAGIC ^ reason ^ controls;
  watchdog_hw->scratch[0] = RESET_FAULT_MAGIC;
  z80_cpu_fail_closed();
  z80_reset_with_clock_cycles(3, 1);
  watchdog_reboot(0, 0, 0);
  while (true)
    tight_loop_contents();
}

static void __not_in_flash_func(resume_and_wait_for_release)(uint control_pin) {
  absolute_time_t deadline = make_timeout_time_us(TRAP_RELEASE_TIMEOUT_US);
  uint32_t released_mask = (1u << PIN_IORQ_N) | (1u << control_pin);
  gpio_put(PIN_IO_RELEASE, 1);
  uint32_t controls = gpio_get_all();
  if ((controls & released_mask) != released_mask) {
    z80_clock_prepare_stepping();
    do {
      if (time_reached(deadline)) {
        __atomic_fetch_add(&trap_timeouts, 1, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
        trap_fail_closed(Z80_IO_TRAP_RESET_RELEASE_TIMEOUT, gpio_get_all());
      }
      z80_clock_step_prepared(1);
      controls = gpio_get_all();
    } while ((controls & released_mask) != released_mask);
  }
  z80_data_bus_isolate();
  busy_wait_us_32(1);
  gpio_put(PIN_IO_RELEASE, 0);
  z80_clock_resume();
}

static void __not_in_flash_func(io_trap_handler)(uint gpio, uint32_t events) {
  (void)events;
  if (gpio != PIN_IORQ_N)
    return;
  if (!gpio_get(PIN_BUSACK_N)) {
    gpio_set_irq_enabled(PIN_IORQ_N, GPIO_IRQ_EDGE_FALL, false);
    return;
  }

  z80_clock_stop();
  busy_wait_us_32(1);
  uint32_t controls = gpio_get_all();
  if (controls & (1u << PIN_IORQ_N)) {
    // A latched edge is not an active I/O cycle once IORQ# has released.
    __atomic_fetch_add(&inactive_irqs, 1, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
    __atomic_fetch_add(&control_errors, 1, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
    z80_clock_resume();
    return;
  }
  bool is_read = (controls & (1u << PIN_RD_N)) == 0;
  bool is_write = (controls & (1u << PIN_WR_N)) == 0;
  if (is_read == is_write) {
    __atomic_fetch_add(&control_errors, 1, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
    trap_fail_closed(Z80_IO_TRAP_RESET_INVALID_CONTROLS, controls);
  }
  uint8_t port = z80_port_bus_sample();

  if (is_write) {
    z80_data_bus_prepare_input();
    uint8_t value = z80_data_bus_sample();
    if (application_write != NULL)
      application_write(port, value, application_context);
    resume_and_wait_for_release(PIN_WR_N);
    return;
  }

  uint8_t value = application_read == NULL
                      ? 0xFF
                      : application_read(port, application_context);
  z80_data_bus_drive(value);
  resume_and_wait_for_release(PIN_RD_N);
}

bool z80_io_trap_enable(z80_io_read_handler_t read_handler,
                        z80_io_write_handler_t write_handler,
                        void *context) {
  application_read = read_handler;
  application_write = write_handler;
  application_context = context;
  z80_io_trap_rearm();
  return true;
}

void z80_io_trap_rearm(void) {
  gpio_init(PIN_IORQ_N);
  gpio_set_dir(PIN_IORQ_N, GPIO_IN);
  gpio_disable_pulls(PIN_IORQ_N);
  gpio_acknowledge_irq(PIN_IORQ_N, GPIO_IRQ_EDGE_FALL);
  gpio_set_irq_enabled_with_callback(PIN_IORQ_N, GPIO_IRQ_EDGE_FALL, true,
                                     io_trap_handler);
}

void z80_io_trap_disable(void) {
  gpio_set_irq_enabled(PIN_IORQ_N, GPIO_IRQ_EDGE_FALL, false);
  gpio_acknowledge_irq(PIN_IORQ_N, GPIO_IRQ_EDGE_FALL);
}

uint32_t z80_io_trap_timeout_count(void) {
  return __atomic_load_n(&trap_timeouts, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
}

uint32_t z80_io_trap_control_error_count(void) {
  return __atomic_load_n(&control_errors, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
}

uint32_t z80_io_trap_inactive_irq_count(void) {
  return __atomic_load_n(&inactive_irqs, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
}

docs.title: Phase 9 - USB CP/M and flash storage
Phase 9 - USB CP/M Terminal and Flash Storage
docs.text:
Tick setup items when complete and tests only after recording the measured result. Progress is saved in this browser; ticks are not automatic verification. Leave Phase 10 network-dependent tests unticked until completed there. The bring-up checkpoint is not the final storage pass gate.

Clear checklist

Prerequisite: The Phase 8 pass gate must pass.

For building C applications with DCC, importing application disks from Altair 8800 AI Edition, and deploying them with VS Code tasks, see Related projects. Use the supplied applications for this phase's bring-up tests before adding your own.

Hardware: Keep the tested Phase 8 wiring unchanged.

Goal: Boot CP/M over USB and verify persistent disks, SRAM loading, and recovery from interrupted writes.

docs.title: Build and provision from VS Code
docs.text:
Open the Z80ROMlessSBC project folder, run Tasks: Run Task from the Command Palette, then choose:

Task Result Build and flash Pico - Phase 9 firmware Builds and force-flashes firmware; preserves disks and ENV Build and flash Pico - Phase 9 firmware and disks Builds and writes the complete image; replaces disks and ENV

Choose Diagnostic for bring-up tests or Automatic loader after those tests pass. Both tasks force-update without checking the previous firmware. Use firmware and disks for initial installation or a complete BIOS/disk refresh; use firmware only for routine updates. See task requirements.

Before deployment

Save CP/M work. Apply external +5 V before USB and keep it applied. Disk tasks overwrite selected drives without backups.

Matching Phase 9 firmware, boot package, and disks installed; host backups retained.

Use disposable disk contents for fault tests

Complete normal boot/read/write checks before injecting faults. Tests that corrupt images, overwrite all records, or interrupt flash updates can destroy files. Preserve the original images and expected old/new blocks first. Use the documented one-shot watchdog hooks; do not simulate faults by pulling individual live signal wires or shorting pins.

Fail-closed means the supervisor deliberately holds the CPU in reset or reboots into recovery instead of executing an unverified image. Capture the USB error/status first. Do not bypass verification merely to get a prompt.

USB terminal first; 20 MHz after loading

Phase 9 implements the same 0x00/0x01 terminal contract as in Phases 8 and 10, using USB CDC rather than Wi-Fi. The diagnostic firmware requires separate load/start commands; the automatic loader below performs both on Pico reset. In either case, slow, Z80-assisted loading and complete readback happen before execution at 20,000,000 Hz, 50% configured duty (120 MHz / 6). The Z80 clock frequency has been scope-measured at 20 MHz on the project prototype. This does not establish CP/M, disk-I/O or receiving-pin timing margins. I/O traps and flash writes still pause execution. The replacement Phase 10 inherits this tested automatic-loader application and its clock settings; combined network operation still requires acceptance testing.

docs.title: Automatic CP/M loader
docs.text:
Both Phase 9 variants also implement ROMLESS-SVC/1 extended ports: countdown timers, stopwatches, uptime, utilities, onboard LED control and persistent ENV. The LED uses Utility payload [4, 0] for off, [4, 1] for on, and [5] to read its last successfully commanded state. Its wireless-chip driver is initialized on demand without enabling Wi-Fi networking; USB and 20 MHz operation are unchanged. Calendar queries explicitly report CLOCK_UNSYNCED in this USB-only phase. No additional wiring is required; the interrupt timer remains deferred. Check these services with the updated Drive C applications after the terminal/disk pass gates. Software regression tests do not replace physical timing and persistence checks.

After the bring-up tests pass, run Build and flash Pico - Phase 9 firmware and choose Automatic loader. Switching variants requires only a firmware update when the installed boot package and disks already match; the diagnostic variant uses manual l/g commands.

Every Pico reset now:

  1. Establishes safe GPIO levels, holds the Z80 in reset and stops its clock. Launches core 1, which initializes its flash-lockout participation, the default alarm pool and USB before acknowledging readiness.
  2. Recovers the flash journal and validates the boot manifest and payload CRC.
  3. Uses Z80-assisted loading to write the complete 65,536-byte SRAM image, then independently reads back and compares every byte.
  4. Resets the Z80 again, enables I/O trapping and starts CP/M at 20 MHz.
  5. Continues terminal and disk service without waiting for a USB terminal.

Core 0 owns Z80 GPIO, loading, clock generation and I/O traps. Core 1 owns all USB endpoint access, USB interrupts/background tasks, ANSI input mapping and terminal pumping, plus runtime storage and service workers. Core 1 starts before loading, but disk/service workers are enabled only after successful load/verify and CP/M startup. The earlier single-core bring-up phases are unchanged.

USB supervisor commands cross a four-entry queue to core 0; they never manipulate Z80 GPIO from core 1. A full queue explicitly rejects the command and asks the user to retry. Core 0 publishes running/loading/stopping flags; manual-loader cancellation and USB connection state are published back from core 1. The cancellation check remains at a 256-byte loader checkpoint.

Diagnostics from either core use a separate 4 KiB bounded log ring. Core 1 drains at most 128 bytes per pass, subject to CDC room, without holding the ring lock over USB calls. Connected overflow is reported as log_drops; disconnected logs are discarded and not replayed. CP/M output retains its separate 512-byte terminal ring. The SDK stdout mutex is disabled for these targets, so core 0 never waits on USB output serialization. CP/M USB output submits at most 32 bytes in one nonblocking CDC write per pass, with one flush attempt when bytes are accepted. It peeks at the terminal ring and removes only the accepted prefix, leaving short or rejected writes queued for a later pass. No terminal lock is held during endpoint calls, and single interactive characters are submitted immediately without a batching delay. USB remains serviced while stopped or draining for a stop. Flash programming can temporarily suspend it through SDK lockout. Real enumeration, concurrent network traffic and timing still require bench acceptance.

docs.title: SRAM-resident terminal and disk register path
docs.text:
The local performance hypothesis is that SRAM instruction placement reduces flash-cache-dependent latency in the core-0 I/O trap. It is not a claim that flash instruction fetches are the dominant cost. The SDK __not_in_flash_func attribute places the following routines in SRAM:

  • The shared Phase 9/10 application's virtual_read and virtual_write.
  • z80_terminal_io_read, z80_terminal_io_write, and their ring-add and connection-state helpers.
  • z80_flash_disk_io_read, z80_flash_disk_io_write, their command/status/address helpers, and z80_flash_backend_read_record.

Small helpers may be inlined into these SRAM-resident handlers and have no separate linked symbol. The application still runs on core 0; USB, networking, and runtime flash programming remain on core 1. Locks, queue bounds, register semantics, and all hardware-settling waits are unchanged.

This is not a completely flash-independent call chain. SDK timing/mux helpers, failure handling, extended service/timer ports, queue_try_add, and memcpy can still execute from flash. Uncached disk records and diagnostic comparison bytes are still read from flash. SRAM placement does not permit trapping during flash programming or relax BUSACK/IRQ/multicore lockout.

docs.title: Build verification
docs.text:
The 2026-10-23 comparison used the same local SDK, toolchain, build configuration, and working-tree sources before and after adding placement attributes. Each The Phase 9/10 linker map and ELF place the seven top-level routines above in .data at SRAM addresses beginning 0x2000...; disassembly also places callback switch tables there. Terminal ring/connection helpers and disk command/status/ address helpers are inlined into their handlers in this build.

Target Initialized SRAM .data, before After Additional SRAM Phase 9 diagnostic 9,256 bytes 10,472 bytes 1,216 bytes Phase 9 automatic loader 9,256 bytes 10,472 bytes 1,216 bytes Phase 10 WebSocket terminal 13,936 bytes 15,152 bytes 1,216 bytes

BSS and stack reservations are unchanged. Total loadable ELF content grows by 32 bytes for each Phase 9 variant and 40 bytes for Phase 10, including linker alignment and veneers. SRAM code is included in .data; the plain size summary's data column alone does not measure its RAM cost. Inspect ELF sections and the linker map:

elf=build/src/stage10_websocket_terminal/z80_stage10_websocket_terminal.elf
arm-none-eabi-objdump -h "$elf"
arm-none-eabi-nm -S -n "$elf" |
  grep -E ' (virtual_read|virtual_write|z80_terminal_io_read|z80_terminal_io_write|z80_flash_disk_io_read|z80_flash_disk_io_write|z80_flash_backend_read_record)$'
arm-none-eabi-objdump -d --disassemble=virtual_read "$elf"
arm-none-eabi-objdump -d --disassemble=z80_flash_disk_io_write "$elf"

Repeat for both Phase 9 ELFs. Check that the selected functions have SRAM execution addresses, not merely flash load addresses. Inspect each handler's disassembly for outlined helpers and veneers: a veneer in SRAM can still jump to flash. In this build terminal register handlers need no out-of-line calls; disk record copies and queue submission still reach flash-resident routines.

docs.title: Hardware comparison still required
docs.text:
No before/after trap-latency result was recorded for this change; hardware deployment and measurement were explicitly deferred. Successful builds, placement checks and host tests do not establish a measured speedup.

For a comparison, preserve both firmware builds and use identical clock settings, CP/M images, workload, USB/browser ownership and network load. With the safe setup in the logic-analyzer procedure, capture Group C IN and OUT separately in 16-channel, 100 MHz Buffer Mode. Separate terminal status/data accesses, disk status/data accesses, read commands, and write-record submission rather than mixing their latency distributions.

Measure IORQ falling to IO_RELEASE rising as the service-response interval, and the end of free-running CLK to its resumed free-running edges as the total Z80 clock pause, including stepped completion. Neither is an exact IRQ-entry/ exit timestamp. Record sample count, sample resolution, median, tail percentile, maximum, and workload/capture length for each category, both idle and with concurrent network traffic. Check control errors, drops and trap timeouts before and after; review the original data setup/hold, isolation, PWM handover and settling guards on raw captures. The acceptance gate is a repeatable reduction in the selected latency metric with no correctness/timing regression, not an assumed improvement based on SRAM addresses alone.

Connect picocom whenever convenient, using the actual USB CDC port name:

picocom --baud 115200 --databits 8 --parity n --stopbits 1 --flow n /dev/cu.usbmodemXXXX

There are no load/start commands to type. Output produced without a connected terminal is discarded, including the CP/M banner and A> prompt. If CP/M is idle at its command prompt, press Return after connecting to obtain a fresh prompt; reconnecting does not restart a running application. While a terminal is connected during automatic boot, the supervisor reports SRAM load and independent verification progress every 4,096 bytes, for example:

[boot] SRAM load: 32768/65536
[boot] SRAM load: 36864/65536
...
[boot] SRAM verify: 32768/65536
...
[boot] verified; RESET held LOW: 65536/65536

The last line precedes releasing reset and starting CP/M. Progress is not retained or replayed when no terminal is connected, and automatic boot never waits for USB. After CP/M starts, reconnecting preserves the current program and does not reboot the Z80 or replay progress or a supervisor menu. ANSI key mapping is the same as in the diagnostic firmware.

Verification or startup failure keeps the CPU stopped; it never runs an unverified image or retries endlessly. A later terminal connection reports the stopped state and retained failure details. Optional Ctrl+] then s still shows status, and Ctrl+] then h prints supervisor help. For a safe software restart, use Ctrl+] then x, wait for Disk quiescent; RESET held LOW, PWM stopped, then use Ctrl+] then r. The Pico reboots and automatically reloads CP/M. The stop confirmation also prints the full Ctrl+] command menu and marks r (reboot), s (status), and h (help) as available while stopped. Loading/running/testing (l/g/t) requires a Pico reboot before another run; fault commands (0-8) require a running CPU. This resets USB CDC too, so picocom may exit with Device not configured. Reconnect using the current USB port name; if loading or verification is still underway, progress appears at the next 4,096-byte boundary before the CP/M banner.

Reset is not a substitute for saving and flushing

A Pico reset reloads SRAM and discards the running CP/M program. Save work and stop/flush first. Journal recovery protects committed flash updates, not unsaved application data or disk changes still held only in RAM. Keep external +5 V applied throughout in-board USB programming.

For new/disposable storage, z80_stage09_cpm_loader_images builds the complete matching package in build/cpm-stage09-loader/. Its full-flash image contains the automatic loader and replaces all disk contents when programmed; do not use it for a firmware-only update.

docs.title: Controlled USB workflow
docs.text:
This section uses the original manual diagnostic firmware, not the automatic loader above.

Do not deploy this firmware while another physical test or soak is running. No probing, wiring changes or firmware replacement is required to build it. After that test finishes, follow the power and provisioning procedure. Both the Pico firmware and the boot package/Drive A system tracks must come from the same new build: the BIOS now emits startup evidence.

For an already provisioned board, selectively update the Phase 9 UF2, z80boot.pkg, and matching drive_a_cpm63k-z80.img using Section 7's addresses. Updating Drive A overwrites its existing files; the development workflow does not create backups. For disposable/new storage, the complete build/cpm-stage09/z80romless-flash.bin contains everything. Building either target never flashes the board.

For a terminal-mapping-only firmware update on an already matching Phase 9 installation, flash only z80_stage09_flash_storage.uf2. The boot package, CP/M disks and journal do not need to be rewritten.

Open the Pico's USB CDC port with a terminal, using your actual port name:

picocom --baud 115200 --databits 8 --parity n --stopbits 1 --flow n /dev/cu.usbmodemXXXX

Do not open a second serial owner. Disable local echo. In picocom, Ctrl+A then Ctrl+X exits the host terminal; Ctrl+] then a command controls the supervisor. Ordinary letters, digits and CP/M control keys are terminal input, not diagnostic commands.

Sequence Supervisor action Ctrl+] then l Recover journal; validate manifest/CRCs, exact 65,536-byte payload and JP FD00h; load and independently read back every SRAM byte; leave RESET LOW Ctrl+] then g Start the verified image from a fresh reset at 20 MHz Ctrl+] then t After loading, replace the SRAM entry code with a read-only Z80 disk diagnostic; compare every byte of all four drives; reboot afterward Ctrl+] then s Print run state, configured clock, BIOS evidence, disk/fatal state, queue drops and trap error counts Ctrl+] then x While running CP/M, complete/flush disk work, pause the flash worker, then hold RESET LOW and stop PWM; during the read-only diagnostic, stop directly Ctrl+] then r Reboot the Pico only while stopped; journal recovery runs on the next l Ctrl+] then 0 Disarm a fault while running Ctrl+] then 1-8 Arm a one-shot journal/flash-safe watchdog fault while running; disposable disks only Ctrl+] then h Print help Ctrl+] then Ctrl+] Send a literal Ctrl+] to CP/M

docs.title: ANSI keyboard mapping
docs.text:
Phase 9 ports the ESP32 Altair ansi_input mapper into the USB receive path. Picocom forwards the host terminal's ANSI input sequences; the firmware converts these to the CP/M application's WordStar-style control keys:

Host key ANSI input CP/M byte Up ESC [ A Ctrl+E (05h) Down ESC [ B Ctrl+X (18h) Right ESC [ C Ctrl+D (04h) Left ESC [ D Ctrl+S (13h) Insert ESC [ 2 ~ Ctrl+O (0Fh) Delete ESC [ 3 ~ Ctrl+G (07h) Page Up ESC [ 5 ~ Ctrl+R (12h) Page Down ESC [ 6 ~ Ctrl+V (16h) Backspace (7Fh or 08h) Single byte Ctrl+H (08h)

A standalone Escape is delivered once after a 30 ms grace period, even when no further serial bytes arrive. Sequences may span USB reads. Ordinary text and other nonzero control bytes pass through; CRLF still becomes one carriage return. As in the Altair mapper, NUL means no input, unsupported ESC [ keys are consumed, and Escape followed by a non-[ byte forwards that byte. This is not a general ANSI keyboard decoder: Home/End, function keys, modified arrows and application-cursor (ESC O) sequences are not mapped. Use normal cursor-key mode in the host terminal.

Ctrl+] supervisor commands are intercepted before mapping. Starting a supervisor command, stopping the CPU or changing the USB connection resets partial ANSI state. Terminal output and Phase 10's WebSocket keyboard handling are unchanged. Test the keys in an application configured for these control bindings; individual CP/M programs can assign different meanings.

docs.title: 1. Prove loading without executing CP/M
docs.text:
Type Ctrl+] then l. Loading reports recovery, manifest validation, load and verify progress every 4 KiB. Cancellation is checked every 256 bytes: type x (plain or after Ctrl+]) to cancel; loss of the USB connection also cancels at the next checkpoint. Failure/cancellation asserts reset, inhibits SRAM reads, isolates the data paths and stops PWM. The first fault includes phase, address, expected/actual bytes and error category.

Success says 65,536 bytes loaded and independently read back; CPU not running. Check RESET LOW before proceeding. One load attempt is allowed per Pico boot; reboot after cancellation/failure or a stopped run instead of reinitializing live storage queues. Initial journal recovery uses SDK lockout with the already-running USB core.

docs.title: 2. Optional read-only Z80 disk qualification
docs.text:
After l, type Ctrl+] then t. The actual Z80 program selects drives A-D and LBAs 0-2559, reads exactly 128 bytes per record using INIR, and reports those bytes using OTIR on diagnostic port 0x06. The Pico compares them in order with the recovered XIP flash image. A PASS requires exactly 1,310,720 matching bytes, all 10,240 records, and the final success report on port 0x05. The test issues no disk write or flush commands. It stops at the first mismatch, disk-reported failure, or five-minute timeout.

The byte offset in a mismatch identifies the drive (offset / 327680), LBA within that drive ((offset % 327680) / 128) and byte within the record (offset % 128). This is stronger than calling the C handlers directly, but is not proof of journal durability, filesystem behavior or analogue timing margins. Progress is printed every 64 KiB.

The diagnostic overwrites part of SRAM, so it cannot subsequently start CP/M from that image. Use Ctrl+] r, reconnect if needed, then Ctrl+] l to load CP/M again. Flash disk contents remain unchanged.

docs.title: 3. Start CP/M and prove it is alive
docs.text:
After a fresh successful l, type Ctrl+] then g. These are separate milestones:

  1. The supervisor reports reset released and the configured clock.
  2. The Z80 BIOS reports cold entry (OUT (05h),B0h).
  3. The BIOS reports handoff to CCP (OUT (05h),C0h); warm boot reports this too.
  4. The CP/M banner and A> prompt, followed by successful commands, prove the console and operating system are functioning.

The first three are not an automatic CP/M PASS. Missing BIOS/handoff evidence after ten seconds requests a safe stop; check that the matching BIOS package was provisioned. Read-only disk testing and a real CP/M prompt remain distinct acceptance results.

Start with DIR, DIR B:, DIR C: and DIR D:; check the distinct sentinels listed below. Run LS and require a natural return through BIOS warm boot to the prompt. Only then test copies/writes on disposable contents. The file named drive_d_blank.img currently contains the documented DOCTOR.COM sentinel; its historical filename is not evidence that it is empty.

The shared terminal queues hold 128 input and 512 output bytes. While a terminal is connected, output remains buffered for Z80 throughput: the BIOS waits only when the output queue is full, and USB output is pumped only when the CDC transport has space. With no terminal connected, writes are discarded immediately and transmit-ready stays asserted, so console output cannot stall the application. Disconnecting clears pending output; reconnecting does not replay it. Bytes already handed to USB at disconnect are in flight and are not guaranteed. Intentional disconnected-output discards are not overflow errors. CRLF input becomes one CP/M carriage return. Actual queue overflow is counted and printed as FAIL; reduce paste rate and repeat any affected acceptance test.

To stop, use Ctrl+] then x and wait for Disk quiescent; RESET held LOW, PWM stopped. Do not remove power or request reboot before that confirmation. A fatal storage error instead holds reset and requires reboot recovery; preserve the error log first.

Firmware feature: On explicit l, recover any valid journal and validate the boot manifest and CRC32 while the CPU is held reset. Then initialize the assisted loader, release reset, inject instructions to write SRAM, and compare every byte. Reset again before normal execution. The Pico never drives addresses or SRAM write control; BUSACK is not required for cold loading. Follow the injection protocol. Once running, ports 0x10-0x14 provide command/status, drive, 16-bit LBA, and 128-byte data transfers. Reads are synchronous XIP copies; writes use the journaled core-1 service and BUSY/READY/ERROR behavior defined in the flash-storage architecture.

Before erasing a target sector, the backend reads back and compares the complete journal data sector and header page. A failed journal program therefore leaves the old target intact and latches a storage error. Target readback and header-clear checks remain required after programming.

Application source: src/stage09_flash_storage/main.c, the ANSI input mapper and its interface, with the shared disk device, terminal queues, flash backend, and flash layout.

docs.title: Flash Disk Image Loader (Final Phase 9 Integration)
docs.text:
Maintained source: flash_disk.h, flash_layout.h, disk_device.c, and flash_backend.c.

Loading a boot image is now a synchronous, core-0-only operation: a flash read is an ordinary memory access through the XIP-mapped pointer described in the flash-storage architecture, so bringing the initial image into SRAM needs no filesystem, blocking I/O call, or core 1 task. Only CP/M's live disk-sector writes still need to run on core 1 and cross back to core 0's foreground loop, because only they need to freeze the Z80 around a flash erase/program cycle using those same storage ownership rules.

docs.title: Maintained Source
docs.text:
These complete files are included from the repository at documentation build time, not copied into this page.

Phase 9 application - src/stage09_flash_storage/main.c

enum {
  RUN_CLOCK_HZ = 20000000,
  SYSTEM_CLOCK_HZ = 120000000,
  USB_COMMAND_ESCAPE = 0x1D,
  USB_REPORT_CONNECTION = 0x100,
  USB_CONFIG_REBOOT = 0x101,
  DISK_READY = 1,
  DISK_BUSY = 8,
  DIAGNOSTIC_BYTES = Z80_FLASH_DISK_SLOT_COUNT * Z80_FLASH_DISK_SLOT_BYTES,
  CPU_RUNNING = 1u << 0,
  CPU_STOPPING = 1u << 1,
  CPU_LOADING = 1u << 2,
  USB_CONNECTED = 1u << 0,
  USB_BROWSER = 1u << 1,
  USB_SETUP = 1u << 2,
};

static void publish_cpu_state(void) {
  __atomic_store_n(&cpu_state,
                   (running ? CPU_RUNNING : 0) |
                   (stop_requested ? CPU_STOPPING : 0) |
                   (loading ? CPU_LOADING : 0), __ATOMIC_RELEASE);
}

static uint8_t __not_in_flash_func(virtual_read)(uint8_t port, void *context) {
  (void)context;
  switch (port) {
  case 0x00:
  case 0x01:
    return z80_terminal_io_read(port);
  case 0x10:
  case 0x11:
  case 0x12:
  case 0x13:
  case 0x14:
    return z80_flash_disk_io_read(port);
  case IO_SERVICE_COMMAND_PORT:
  case IO_SERVICE_REQUEST_PORT:
  case IO_SERVICE_RESPONSE_PORT:
  case IO_TIMER_PORT:
  case HTTP_COMMAND_PORT:
  case HTTP_DATA_PORT:
    return z80_io_port_in(port);
  default:
    return 0xFF;
  }
}

static void __not_in_flash_func(virtual_write)(uint8_t port, uint8_t value,
                                              void *context) {
  (void)context;
  if (port == 0x00) {
    z80_terminal_io_write(port, value);
    return;
  }
  if (diagnostic_active && port == 0x06) {
    uint32_t offset = diagnostic_count;
    if (offset < DIAGNOSTIC_BYTES) {
      const uint8_t *source =
          (const uint8_t *)(XIP_BASE + Z80_FLASH_DISK_OFFSET);
      if (value != source[offset] && diagnostic_result == 0) {
        diagnostic_fault_offset = offset;
        diagnostic_expected = source[offset];
        diagnostic_actual = value;
        diagnostic_result = 0xE1;
      }
    } else {
      diagnostic_result = 0xE1;
    }
    diagnostic_count = offset + 1;
    return;
  }
  if (diagnostic_active && port == Z80_BOOT_REPORT_PORT) {
    if (diagnostic_result == 0)
      diagnostic_result = value == 0x5A &&
                          diagnostic_count == DIAGNOSTIC_BYTES ? 0x5A : 0xE1;
    return;
  }
  switch (port) {
  case Z80_BOOT_REPORT_PORT:
    if (value == Z80_BOOT_REPORT_BIOS)
      __atomic_fetch_or(&boot_markers, 1u, __ATOMIC_RELEASE);
    else if (value == Z80_BOOT_REPORT_CCP)
      __atomic_fetch_or(&boot_markers, 2u, __ATOMIC_RELEASE);
    break;
  case 0x10:
  case 0x11:
  case 0x12:
  case 0x13:
  case 0x14:
    z80_flash_disk_io_write(port, value);
    break;
  case IO_SERVICE_COMMAND_PORT:
  case IO_SERVICE_REQUEST_PORT:
  case IO_SERVICE_RESPONSE_PORT:
  case IO_TIMER_PORT:
  case HTTP_COMMAND_PORT:
  case HTTP_DATA_PORT:
    z80_io_port_out(port, value);
    break;
  default:
    break;
  }
}

static void core1_service(void) {
  bool active = __atomic_load_n(&workers_ready, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE);
  if (active) {
    if (__atomic_load_n(&flash_pause_request, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE)) {
      if (!__atomic_load_n(&flash_paused, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE)) {
        z80_flash_core1_service();
        z80_io_ports_core1_service();
#ifdef Z80_STAGE10_NETWORK
        z80_network_setup_core1_service();
#endif
        if (z80_flash_disk_quiescent() && z80_io_ports_quiescent()
#ifdef Z80_STAGE10_NETWORK
            && z80_network_setup_quiescent()
#endif
        )
          __atomic_store_n(&flash_paused, 1, __ATOMIC_RELEASE);
      }
    } else {
      __atomic_store_n(&flash_paused, 0, __ATOMIC_RELEASE);
      z80_flash_core1_service();
      z80_io_ports_core1_service();
#ifdef Z80_STAGE10_NETWORK
      z80_network_setup_core1_service();
#endif
    }
  }
  z80_usb_console_service();
  service_usb();
#ifdef Z80_STAGE10_NETWORK
  if (active) {
    if (__atomic_load_n(&flash_pause_request, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE))
      z80_network_terminal_core1_service();
    else
      z80_network_core1_service();
  }
  if (active) {
    uint32_t state = __atomic_load_n(&cpu_state, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE);
    z80_matrix_core1_service(
        (state & (CPU_RUNNING | CPU_STOPPING | CPU_LOADING)) == CPU_RUNNING &&
        !__atomic_load_n(&flash_pause_request, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE));
  }
#endif
}

static void core1_main(void) {
  bool flash_ready = flash_safe_execute_core_init();
  bool usb_ready = z80_usb_console_init();
  if (!flash_ready || !usb_ready)
    printf("\n[diag] FAIL: core 1 USB/flash-safe initialization.\n");
  __atomic_store_n(&core1_ready, flash_ready && usb_ready ? 1u : 2u,
                    __ATOMIC_RELEASE);
  while (true) {
    if (usb_ready)
      core1_service();
    tight_loop_contents();
  }
}

static void hold_cpu(void) {
  z80_io_trap_disable();
  z80_cpu_fail_closed();
  running = false;
  image_verified = false;
  stop_requested = false;
  diagnostic_active = false;
}

static const char *fault_name(z80_flash_fault_point_t point) {
  static const char *const names[] = {
    "none", "after journal data", "after journal header",
    "after target erase", "after partial target program",
    "after target verification", "after journal header clear",
    "safe-execute entry failure", "safe-execute exit failure",
  };
  return point <= Z80_FLASH_FAULT_SAFE_EXECUTE_EXIT
             ? names[(unsigned int)point] : "invalid";
}

static const char *boot_error_name(z80_boot_error_t error) {
  static const char *const names[] = {
    "none", "journal recovery",
    "manifest (requires 65536 bytes and JP FD00h)",
    "payload CRC", "loader controls", "SRAM write", "SRAM read",
    "SRAM mismatch", "flash-safe core initialization", "cancelled",
  };
  return (unsigned int)error < sizeof(names) / sizeof(names[0])
             ? names[(unsigned int)error] : "invalid";
}

static bool observe_boot(const z80_boot_status_t *status, void *context) {
  (void)context;
  static const char *const phases[] = {
    "journal recovery", "manifest/CRC validation", "SRAM load",
    "SRAM verify", "verified; RESET held LOW",
  };
  if (status->completed % 4096u == 0 &&
      (!Z80_STAGE09_AUTOBOOT ||
       (__atomic_load_n(&usb_state, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE) & USB_CONNECTED)))
    printf("[boot] %s: %lu/%lu\n", phases[status->phase],
           (unsigned long)status->completed, (unsigned long)status->total);
  if (Z80_STAGE09_AUTOBOOT)
    return true;
  return !__atomic_load_n(&load_cancelled, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE) &&
         (__atomic_load_n(&usb_state, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE) & USB_CONNECTED);
}

static void load_image(void) {
  if (boot_attempted || running || runtime_started) {
    printf("\n[diag] Load already attempted; stop and reboot Pico to reload.\n");
    return;
  }
  boot_attempted = true;
  loading = true;
  __atomic_store_n(&load_cancelled, 0, __ATOMIC_RELEASE);
  publish_cpu_state();
  if (!Z80_STAGE09_AUTOBOOT)
    printf("\n[boot] Load/verify only; x cancels at a 256-byte boundary.\n");
  bool loaded = z80_flash_storage_init_observed(observe_boot, NULL);
  loading = false;
  publish_cpu_state();
  if (!loaded) {
    const z80_boot_status_t *status = z80_flash_boot_status();
    boot_failure = boot_error_name(status->error);
    hold_cpu();
    printf("[boot] FAIL: %s phase=%u completed=%lu address=%04x "
           "expected=%02x actual=%02x; RESET held LOW\n",
           boot_error_name(status->error), (unsigned int)status->phase,
           (unsigned long)status->completed, status->address,
           status->expected, status->actual);
    return;
  }
  image_verified = true;
  if (!Z80_STAGE09_AUTOBOOT)
    printf("[boot] PASS: 65536 bytes loaded and independently read back; "
           "CPU not running. Ctrl-] g starts CP/M at nominal 20 MHz.\n");
}

static void start_cpm(void) {
  if (!image_verified || running || runtime_started) {
    printf("\n[diag] Start rejected: first load/verify with Ctrl-] l; "
           "a stopped run requires Pico reboot.\n");
    return;
  }
  __atomic_store_n(&boot_markers, 0, __ATOMIC_RELEASE);
  bios_announced = ccp_announced = false;
  boot_timed_out = false;
  z80_io_ports_init();
  runtime_started = true;
  if (!z80_io_trap_enable(virtual_read, virtual_write, NULL) ||
      !z80_cpu_release_reset_and_run(RUN_CLOCK_HZ)) {
    boot_failure = "trap/clock start";
    hold_cpu();
    printf("[boot] FAIL: trap/clock start; RESET held LOW\n");
    return;
  }
  running = true;
  __atomic_store_n(&workers_ready, 1, __ATOMIC_RELEASE);
  boot_deadline = make_timeout_time_ms(10000);
  if (!Z80_STAGE09_AUTOBOOT)
    printf("\n[boot] CPU released from reset; configured clock=%lu Hz. "
           "Waiting for BIOS evidence, not yet a CP/M PASS.\n",
           (unsigned long)z80_clock_get_hz());
}

static void start_disk_diagnostic(void) {
  if (!image_verified || runtime_started || running) {
    printf("\n[diag] Disk test requires Ctrl-] l and no prior run.\n");
    return;
  }
  image_verified = false;
  diagnostic_count = diagnostic_result = 0;
  diagnostic_fault_offset = UINT32_MAX;
  diagnostic_next_progress = 65536;
  if (!z80_cpu_load_and_verify(z80_disk_diagnostic,
                               sizeof(z80_disk_diagnostic))) {
    hold_cpu();
    printf("\n[diag] FAIL: disk diagnostic load/readback; RESET held LOW\n");
    return;
  }
  diagnostic_active = true;
  if (!z80_io_trap_enable(virtual_read, virtual_write, NULL) ||
      !z80_cpu_release_reset_and_run(RUN_CLOCK_HZ)) {
    hold_cpu();
    printf("\n[diag] FAIL: disk diagnostic start; RESET held LOW\n");
    return;
  }
  running = true;
  boot_deadline = make_timeout_time_ms(300000);
  printf("\n[diag] Read-only Z80 INIR/OTIR disk test at nominal 20 MHz: "
         "all 4 drives x 2560 records x 128 bytes. No disk writes. "
         "CP/M SRAM image replaced; reboot afterward.\n");
}

static void print_reset_status(void) {
  const char *reason = "none";
  if (reset_fault.reason == Z80_IO_TRAP_RESET_RELEASE_TIMEOUT)
    reason = "release-timeout";
  else if (reset_fault.reason == Z80_IO_TRAP_RESET_INVALID_CONTROLS)
    reason = "invalid-controls";
  printf("[reset] watchdog=%u io_fault=%s gpio=%08lx\n",
         reset_was_watchdog, reason, (unsigned long)reset_fault.gpio);
}

  if (requested)
    print_reset_status();
  uint64_t uptime_seconds = z80_service_millis() / 1000;
  printf("[system] uptime=%02llu:%02llu:%02llu\n",
         (unsigned long long)(uptime_seconds / 3600),
         (unsigned long long)((uptime_seconds / 60) % 60),
         (unsigned long long)(uptime_seconds % 60));
#ifdef Z80_STAGE10_NETWORK
  if (requested) {
    char address[16];
    bool has_address = z80_io_ports_get_network_address(address, sizeof(address)) != 0;
    printf("[network] browser=%u setup=%u ip=%s\n",
           !!(__atomic_load_n(&usb_state, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE) & USB_BROWSER),
           !!(__atomic_load_n(&usb_state, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE) & USB_SETUP),
           has_address ? address : "unavailable");
    if (has_address)
      printf("[network] Terminal: http://%s:%u/\n", address, Z80_WEB_TERMINAL_PORT);
    z80_matrix_print_status();
  }
  z80_web_terminal_stats_t web = z80_web_terminal_get_stats();
  printf("[web] retransmits=%lu flush_failures=%lu ack_timeouts=%lu "
         "pong_timeouts=%lu\n",
         (unsigned long)web.retransmits, (unsigned long)web.flush_failures,
         (unsigned long)web.ack_timeouts, (unsigned long)web.pong_timeouts);
  const char *last_disconnect = "none";
  switch (web.last_disconnect_reason) {
  case Z80_WEB_TERMINAL_DISCONNECT_SOCKET_CLOSED:
    last_disconnect = "socket-closed";
    break;
  case Z80_WEB_TERMINAL_DISCONNECT_NETWORK_LOST:
    last_disconnect = "network-lost";
    break;
  case Z80_WEB_TERMINAL_DISCONNECT_OUTPUT_ACK_TIMEOUT:
    last_disconnect = "output-ack-timeout";
    break;
  case Z80_WEB_TERMINAL_DISCONNECT_PONG_TIMEOUT:
    last_disconnect = "pong-timeout";
    break;
  case Z80_WEB_TERMINAL_DISCONNECT_PROTOCOL_ERROR:

    last_disconnect = "output-send-error";

  const char *ws_close = "unknown";
  switch (web.last_ws_close_reason) {
  case Z80_WEB_TERMINAL_WS_CLOSE_PEER_TCP_CLOSED: ws_close = "peer-tcp-closed"; break;
  case Z80_WEB_TERMINAL_WS_CLOSE_PEER_WEBSOCKET_CLOSE: ws_close = "peer-ws-close"; break;

  case Z80_WEB_TERMINAL_WS_CLOSE_RECEIVE_QUEUE_BYTE_LIMIT: ws_close = "receive-queue-byte-limit"; break;

         (unsigned long)z80_terminal_tx_drop_count(),
         (unsigned long)z80_io_trap_timeout_count(),

         (unsigned long)z80_io_trap_inactive_irq_count(),
         boot_error_name(boot->error),
         boot_failure != NULL ? boot_failure : "none",
         (unsigned long)z80_usb_console_log_drops());
  if (boot->error != Z80_BOOT_ERROR_NONE)
    printf("[boot] phase=%u completed=%lu address=%04x "
           "expected=%02x actual=%02x\n",
